```{r set_working_dir_load_files, include=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# SET WORKING DIRECTORY AND LOAD RAW DATA FILES
# =============================================================================
# This chunk sets the working directory and loads all data files required
# for the analysis. Data are sourced from:
#       (1) The Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study (v.06):
#           https://dx.doi.org/10.15154/z563-zd2
#       (2) The general exposome factor file needs to be replicated using the
#           following code:
#           https://github.com/PennLINC/exposome_PFNs_cognition/
# =============================================================================

# Set the working directory to the project's R scripts folder
# Make directories called "Figures" and "Tables" in the projects folder
# Results will be saved in those folders 
setwd("/projects/standard/bart/shared/projects/ABCD_menarche/R_scripts")

# --- Demographic and Static/Dynamic Variables ---

# Participant demographics (e.g., age, sex, race/ethnicity, income)
demographics <- read.csv("/projects/standard/bart/shared/projects/ABCD_menarche/ABCD_6_files/ab_p_demo.tsv", 
                         sep = "", 
                         na.strings = "n/a")

# Static variables (time-invariant participant-level characteristics)
staticVariables <- read.csv("/projects/standard/bart/shared/projects/ABCD_menarche/ABCD_6_files/ab_g_stc.tsv", 
                            sep = "\t", 
                            na.strings = "n/a")

# Dynamic variables (time-varying participant-level characteristics)
dynamicVariables <- read.csv("/projects/standard/bart/shared/projects/ABCD_menarche/ABCD_6_files/ab_g_dyn.tsv", 
                             sep = "\t", 
                             na.strings = "n/a")

# --- Puberty Measures ---

# Youth-reported Pubertal Development Scale (PDS)
puberty_y <- read.csv("/projects/standard/bart/shared/projects/ABCD_menarche/ABCD_6_files/ph_y_pds.tsv", 
                      sep = "", 
                      na.strings = "n/a")

# Parent-reported Pubertal Development Scale (PDS)
puberty_p <- read.csv("/projects/standard/bart/shared/projects/ABCD_menarche/ABCD_6_files/ph_p_pds.tsv", 
                      sep = "", 
                      na.strings = "n/a")

# --- Socioeconomic and Environmental Variables ---

# Area Deprivation Index (ADI; neighborhood-level socioeconomic disadvantage)
adi <- read.csv("/projects/standard/bart/shared/projects/ABCD_menarche/ABCD_6_files/le_l_adi.tsv", 
                sep = "", 
                na.strings = "n/a") 

# General Exposome (derived externally from ABCD data)
exposome <- read.csv("/projects/standard/bart/shared/projects/ABCD_menarche/Exposome/abcd_longitudinal_factor_scores_7f_bifactor.csv")

# --- Mental Health Measures ---

# Parent-reported Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL)
cbcl <- read.csv("/projects/standard/bart/shared/projects/ABCD_menarche/ABCD_6_files/mh_p_cbcl.tsv", 
                 sep = "", 
                 na.strings = "n/a")

# Youth-reported Kiddie Schedule for Affective Disorders and Schizophrenia,
# depression module (KSADS-COMP)
ksads <- read.csv("/projects/standard/bart/shared/projects/ABCD_menarche/ABCD_6_files/mh_y_ksads__dep.tsv", 
                  sep = "", 
                  na.strings = "n/a")

# Youth-reported Brief Problem Monitor (BPM)
bpm <- read.csv("/projects/standard/bart/shared/projects/ABCD_menarche/ABCD_6_files/mh_y_bpm.tsv", 
                sep = "", 
                na.strings = "n/a")

# --- Neuroimaging Data (sMRI) ---

# Subcortical and total brain volumes (FreeSurfer aseg parcellation)
brain_volume <- read.csv("/projects/standard/bart/shared/projects/ABCD_menarche/ABCD_6_files/mr_y_smri__vol__aseg.tsv",
                         sep = "", 
                         na.strings = "n/a")

# Cortical volumes by region (Desikan-Killiany parcellation)
brain_volume_dsk <- read.csv("/projects/standard/bart/shared/projects/ABCD_menarche/ABCD_6_files/mr_y_smri__vol__dsk.tsv",
                             sep = "", 
                             na.strings = "n/a")

# Cortical thickness by region (Desikan-Killiany parcellation)
brain_thickness <- read.csv("/projects/standard/bart/shared/projects/ABCD_menarche/ABCD_6_files/mr_y_smri__thk__dsk.tsv", 
                            sep = "", 
                            na.strings = "n/a")

# Cortical surface area by region (Desikan-Killiany parcellation)
brain_surface <- read.csv("/projects/standard/bart/shared/projects/ABCD_menarche/ABCD_6_files/mr_y_smri__area__dsk.tsv",
                          sep = "", 
                          na.strings = "n/a")

# MRI quality control inclusion flags (used to filter usable scans)
qc <- read.csv("/projects/standard/bart/shared/projects/ABCD_menarche/ABCD_6_files/mr_y_qc__incl.tsv", 
               sep = "", 
               na.strings = "n/a")


# --- ABCD-ARMS Dataset ---

# ABCD Analyst-Recommended Matched Samples (ARMS) 
ABCD_arms <-read.delim("/projects/standard/bart/shared/projects/ABCD_menarche/ABCD_arms/participants.tsv")

# Physical health for BMI
phys_y <- read.csv("/projects/standard/bart/shared/projects/ABCD_menarche/ABCD_6_files/ph_y_anthr.tsv", 
                sep = "", 
                na.strings = "n/a") 

phys_p <- read.csv("/projects/standard/bart/shared/projects/ABCD_menarche/ABCD_6_files/ph_p_anthr.tsv", 
                sep = "", 
                na.strings = "n/a") 
```

```{r variables_descriptions, include=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# VARIABLE IDENTIFICATION, RECODING, AND DATA HARMONISATION
# =============================================================================
# This chunk documents the key variables selected from each loaded file, recodes
# KSADS depression diagnoses into a binary composite variable, and harmonizes
# participant and session ID formats across files to enable merging.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# VARIABLE DOCUMENTATION
# Each variable name is listed alongside its label and coding scheme for
# reference.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Static Variables ---
names(staticVariables)
#"ab_g_stc__cohort_sex"       --> Cohort description: Participant's sex (1 = Male; 2 = Female)
#"ab_g_stc__cohort_race__nih" --> Cohort description: Race (NIH classification reporting 7 levels) [Based on baseline response; missingness filled in from longitudinal responses] (2=White; 3=Black (African American); 4=Asian; 5=American Indian/Alaska Native; 6=Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander; 8=More than One Race; 13=Other (Unknown or not reported))

# --- Dynamic Variables ---
names(dynamicVariables)
#"ab_g_dyn__visit_age"                  --> Age in years at each visit
#"ab_g_dyn__cohort_income__hhold__6lvl" --> Cohort description: Household income - 6 levels; (1=<25k; 2=25k to 50k; 3=50k to 75k; 4=75k to 100k; 5=100k to 200k; 6=>200k; 777 = Don't know; 999 = Decline to answer)
#"ab_g_dyn__design_site"                --> Assessment site

# --- Area Deprivation Index ---
names(adi)
#"le_l_adi__addr1__national_prcnt" --> National percentiles, higher means higher value of ADI [Area Deprivation Index] (Address 1) (address 1)

# --- Youth-Reported Puberty (PDS) ---
names(puberty_y)
#"ph_y_pds__f_002" --> Have you begun to menstruate (started to have your period)? (0 = No, 1 = Yes, 999 = Don't know, 777 = Refuse)
#"ph_y_pds__f_002__01" --> If yes, how old were you when you started to menstruate?
#"ph_y_pds__f_002__03" --> On average, how many days are there between the first day of your period and the first day of your next period? For example, if the first day of bleeding is typically at the beginning of each month, the interval between periods is 30 days.
#"ph_y_pds__f_002__04" --> Is your menstrual cycle regular? (1 = Yes; 0 = No; 999 = Don't know; 777 = Refuse to answer)
#"ph_y_pds__f_002__05" --> Are you currently using hormonal birth control (eg. the pill, hormone patch, hormone injection)? (1 = Yes; 0 = No; 999 = Don't know; 777 = Refuse to answer)

#ph_y_pds_001 --> Would you say that your growth in height: 2 = "has barely started"; 3 = "is definitely underway (has definitely started)"

#ph_y_pds_002 --> 'And how about the growth of your body hair? ("Body hair" means hair any place other than your head, such as under your arms) Would you say that your body hair growth: 2 = "has barely started"; 3 = "is definitely underway (has definitely started)"

#ph_y_pds_003 --> 'Have you noticed any skin changes, especially pimples. 2 = "has barely started"; 3 = "is definitely underway (has definitely started)"

#ph_y_pds__f_001 --> Have you noticed that your breasts have begun to grow?: 32 = "has barely started"; 3 = "is definitely underway (has definitely started)"

#ph_y_pds__m_001 --> Have you noticed a deepening of your voice?: 3 = 2 = "has barely started"; 3 = "is definitely underway (has definitely started)"

# --- Parent-Reported Puberty (PDS) ---
names(puberty_p)
#"ph_p_pds__f_002" --> Has your child begun to menstruate? (0 = No, 1 = Yes, 999 = Don't know)
#"ph_p_pds__f_002__01" --> How old were they when they started to menstruate?
#"ph_p_pds__f_002__03" --> On average, how many days are there between the first day of their period and the first day of their next period? (e.g., 30 days)
#"ph_p_pds__f_002__04" --> Is your child's menstrual cycle regular? (1 = Yes; 0 = No; 999 = Don't know)
#"ph_p_pds__f_002__05" --> Is your child currently using hormonal birth control (e.g. the pill, hormone patch, hormone injection)? (1 = Yes; 0 = No; 999 = Don't know)

#ph_p_pds_001 --> Would you say that your child's growth in height: 2 = "has barely started"; 3 = "is definitely underway (has definitely started)"

#ph_p_pds_002 --> 'And how about the growth of your child's body hair? ("Body hair" means hair any place other than your head, such as under your arms) Would you say that your body hair growth: 2 = "has barely started"; 3 = "is definitely underway (has definitely started)"

#ph_p_pds_003 --> 'Have you noticed any skin changes, especially pimples. 2 = "has barely started"; 3 = "is definitely underway (has definitely started)"

#ph_p_pds__f_001 --> Have you noticed that your breasts have begun to grow?: 32 = "has barely started"; 3 = "is definitely underway (has definitely started)"

#ph_p_pds__m_001 --> Have you noticed a deepening of your voice?: 3 = 2 = "has barely started"; 3 = "is definitely underway (has definitely started)"

# --- Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL; parent-reported) ---
names(cbcl)
#"mh_p_cbcl__synd__int_sum" --> Child Behavior Checklist [Parent] (Syndrome Scale - Internalizing): Sum\n[Validation: No more than 2 missing or declined]
#"mh_p_cbcl__synd__ext_sum" --> Child Behavior Checklist [Parent] (Syndrome Scale - Externalizing): Sum\n[Validation: No more than 2 missing or declined]
#"mh_p_cbcl_sum" --> Child Behavior Checklist [Parent] (Syndrome Scale): Sum\n[Validation: No more than 8 missing or declined]
#"mh_p_cbcl__dsm__anx_sum" --> Child Behavior Checklist [Parent] (DSM-5 Oriented Scale - Anxiety)
#"mh_p_cbcl__dsm__dep_sum" --> Child Behavior Checklist [Parent] (DSM-5 Oriented Scale - Depressive problems)

# --- KSADS Depression Module (youth-reported) ---
names(ksads)
#mh_y_ksads__dep__mdd__pres_dx" --> Major Depressive Disorder Present
#mh_y_ksads__dep__mdd__partrem_dx" --> Major Depressive Disorder, Current, in Partial Remission (F32.4)
#mh_y_ksads__dep__mdd__past_dx" --> Major Depressive Disorder, Past (F32.9)
#mh_y_ksads__dep__pdd__pres_dx" --> Persistent Depressive Disorder (Dysthymia) PRESENT F34.1
#mh_y_ksads__dep__pdd__partrem_dx" --> Persistent Depressive Disorder (Dysthymia) In Partial Remission F34.1
#mh_y_ksads__dep__pdd__past_dx" --> Persistent Depressive Disorder (Dysthymia) PAST F34.1
#mh_y_ksads__dep__unspec__pres_dx" --> Unspecified Depressive Disorder Present (F32.9)
#mh_y_ksads__dep__unspec__past_dx" --> Unspecified Depressive Disorder PAST (F32.9)

#for all: 0 = "Absent", 1 = "Present", 555 = "Not administered", 888 = "Not asked due to branching logic"

# =============================================================================
# KSADS: BINARY DEPRESSION DIAGNOSIS COMPOSITE
# =============================================================================
# Each of three present-diagnosis variables (MDD, PDD, Unspecified) is recoded
# to binary (0=Absent, 1=Present), treating "not asked due to branching logic"
# (888) as effectively absent, and "not administered" (555) as missing (NA).
# A composite depression_diagnosis variable flags any current depressive
# disorder. A second variable (depression_diagnosis_ever) flags participants
# who received a diagnosis at any study wave.
# =============================================================================

ksads <- ksads %>%
  mutate(
    mdd = case_when(
      mh_y_ksads__dep__mdd__pres_dx %in% c(0, 888) ~ 0,
      mh_y_ksads__dep__mdd__pres_dx == 1            ~ 1,
      .default = NA_real_
    ),
    pdd = case_when(
      mh_y_ksads__dep__pdd__pres_dx %in% c(0, 888) ~ 0,
      mh_y_ksads__dep__pdd__pres_dx == 1            ~ 1,
      .default = NA_real_
    ),
    unspec = case_when(
      mh_y_ksads__dep__unspec__pres_dx %in% c(0, 888) ~ 0,
      mh_y_ksads__dep__unspec__pres_dx == 1            ~ 1,
      .default = NA_real_
    ),
    depression_diagnosis = case_when(
      mdd == 1 | pdd == 1 |unspec == 1 ~ 1,
      mdd == 0 & pdd == 0 |unspec == 0 ~ 0,
      .default = NA_real_
    )
  )

ksads <- ksads %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  mutate(
    depression_diagnosis_ever =
      if (any(depression_diagnosis == 1, na.rm = TRUE)) {
        rep(1L, n())
      } else {
        depression_diagnosis
      }
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# --- Brief Problem Monitor (BPM; youth-reported) ---
names(bpm)
#mh_y_bpm__int_sum <- "Brief Problem Monitor [Youth] (Internalizing): Sum\n[Validation: No more than 0 missing or declined]"
#mh_y_bpm__int_tscore <- "Brief Problem Monitor [Youth] (Internalizing): T-Score"


# =============================================================================
# BMI
# =============================================================================
# =============================================================================

names(phys_y)

phys_y <- phys_y %>%
  mutate(height = ph_y_anthr__height_mean, weight = ph_y_anthr__weight_mean, waist_in = ph_y_anthr__waist_001) %>%
  mutate(bmi = 703 * weight / height^2,
         wthr = waist_in / height) %>%
  mutate(bmi  = ifelse(bmi  < 10  | bmi  > 60 , NA, bmi), # remove implausible values
         wthr = ifelse(wthr < 0.2 | wthr > 1.0, NA, wthr)) %>% # remove implausible values
  select(participant_id, session_id, height, weight, bmi, wthr)

# =============================================================================
# EXPOSOME: ID HARMONISATION
# =============================================================================
# The exposome file uses different column names and ID formats from the main
# ABCD dataset. Column names and ID strings are standardized here to enable
# merging. Session labels are converted from ABCD long-form strings to the
# abbreviated format used across all other files (e.g., "ses-00A").
# =============================================================================

names(exposome)
# Rename ID and timepoint columns to match the naming convention used elsewhere
colnames(exposome)[1] <- "participant_id"
colnames(exposome)[3] <- "session_id"

# Reformat participant IDs: "NDAR_INV" prefix → "sub-" prefix
names(exposome)[names(exposome) == "ID"] <- "participant_id"
exposome$participant_id <- exposome$participant_id %>%
  str_replace("NDAR_INV","sub-")

names(exposome)[names(exposome) == "Timepoint"] <- "session_id"
table(exposome$session_id)
unique(exposome$session_id)

exposome$session_id <- exposome$session_id %>%
  str_replace("baseline_year_1_arm_1", "ses-00A") %>%
  str_replace("1_year_follow_up_y_arm_1", "ses-01A") %>%
  str_replace("2_year_follow_up_y_arm_1", "ses-02A") %>%
  str_replace("3_year_follow_up_y_arm_1", "ses-03A") %>%
  str_replace("4_year_follow_up_y_arm_1", "ses-04A") %>%
  str_replace("5_year_follow_up_y_arm_1", "ses-05A") %>%
  str_replace("6_year_follow_up_y_arm_1", "ses-06A")

# =============================================================================
# ABCD-ARMS: ID HARMONISATION
# =============================================================================
# In our case the ARMS file uses a different participant ID prefix and verbose 
# session labels. Both are standardized to match the format used across all 
# files. If you get the file directly from the ABCD study, it should be ok.
# =============================================================================

names(ABCD_arms)

# Reformat participant IDs: "sub-NDARINV" prefix → "sub-" prefix
ABCD_arms$participant_id <- ABCD_arms$participant_id %>%
  str_replace("sub-NDARINV","sub-")

# Recode session labels to abbreviated format (e.g., "ses-baselineYear1Arm1" → "ses-00A")
ABCD_arms$session_id <- ABCD_arms$session_id %>%
  str_replace("ses-baselineYear1Arm1", "ses-00A") %>%
  str_replace("ses-1YearFollowUpYArm1", "ses-01A") %>%
  str_replace("ses-2YearFollowUpYArm1", "ses-02A") %>%
  str_replace("ses-3YearFollowUpYArm1", "ses-03A") %>%
  str_replace("ses-4YearFollowUpYArm1", "ses-04A") %>%
  str_replace("ses-5YearFollowUpYArm1", "ses-05A") %>%
  str_replace("ses-6YearFollowUpYArm1", "ses-06A")

# =============================================================================
# NEUROIMAGING VARIABLE DOCUMENTATION (sMRI)
# =============================================================================

# --- Subcortical and Global Brain Volumes (FreeSurfer aseg parcellation) ---
names(brain_volume)
#mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__whb_sum --> Total volume of Subcortical ROI: whole brain
#mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__cwm__lh_sum --> Total volume of Subcortical ROI: cerebral white matter (left hemisphere)
```

```{r merge_files, include=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# MERGE FILES INTO A SINGLE ANALYSIS DATAFRAME
# =============================================================================
# Selected variables from each source file are joined into a single merged
# dataframe. The merge strategy reflects the structure of each dataset:
#
#   - full_join: used for datasets that define the participant-wave universe
#     (dynamic variables, static variables, ADI, puberty). This ensures all
#     participant-wave observations are retained regardless of missingness in
#     any single source.
#
#   - left_join: used for supplementary measures (exposome, CBCL, KSADS, BPM,
#     ARMS) to retain all rows from the base dataset while appending available
#     data from these sources.
#
# The base dataset is dynamicVariables, which contains one row per participant
# per study wave and defines the longitudinal structure of the merged dataframe.
# Static variables (sex, race, family ID) have no session_id and are therefore
# joined on participant_id only; their values are broadcast across all waves
# for each participant.
#
# Only the variables required for analysis are selected prior to joining.
# =============================================================================

merged_df <- dynamicVariables %>%
  # --- Base: demographic and visit-level variables (one row per participant-wave) ---
  dplyr::select(
    participant_id, 
    session_id, 
    ab_g_dyn__visit_age, #Age at visit (years)
    ab_g_dyn__visit_dtt, #Date of visit
    ab_g_dyn__cohort_income__hhold__6lvl, #Houshold income
    ab_g_dyn__design_site #Assessment site
    ) %>%
  
  # --- Static participant characteristics (joined on participant_id only;
  #     values are constant across waves) ---
  full_join(staticVariables %>% 
              dplyr::select(
                participant_id, 
                ab_g_stc__cohort_sex, #Participant sex (1=Male; 2=Female)
                ab_g_stc__cohort_race__nih, #Race
                ab_g_stc__design_id__fam #Family ID (to account for familial dependencies)
                ),
            by = c("participant_id")) %>%
  
  # --- Area Deprivation Index (joined on participant_id and session_id) ---
  full_join(adi %>% 
              dplyr::select(
                participant_id, 
                session_id, 
                le_l_adi__addr1__national_prcnt #ADI
                ),
            by = c("participant_id", "session_id")) %>%
  
  # --- Youth-reported Pubertal Development Scale (PDS) ---
  full_join(puberty_y %>% 
              dplyr::select(
                participant_id,
                session_id,
                ph_y_pds__f_002,       # Menarche occurred (0=No; 1=Yes)
                ph_y_pds__f_002__01,   # Age at menarche (years)
                ph_y_pds__f_002__03,   # Average menstrual cycle length (days)
                ph_y_pds__f_002__04,   # Menstrual cycle regular (1=Yes; 0=No)
                ph_y_pds__f_002__05,   # Currently using hormonal birth control (1=Yes; 0=No)
                ph_y_pds_001,          # Height growth status
                ph_y_pds_002,          # Body hair growth status
                ph_y_pds_003,          # Skin/acne change status
                ph_y_pds__f_001,       # Breast development status
                ph_y_pds__m_001        # Voice deepening status
                ),
            by = c("participant_id", "session_id")) %>%
  
  # --- Parent-reported Pubertal Development Scale (PDS) ---
  full_join(puberty_p %>% 
              dplyr::select(
                participant_id,
                session_id,
                ph_p_pds__f_002,       # Child has begun to menstruate (0=No; 1=Yes)
                ph_p_pds__f_002__01,   # Age at menarche (years; parent-reported)
                ph_p_pds__f_002__03,   # Average menstrual cycle length (days; parent-reported)
                ph_p_pds__f_002__04,   # Menstrual cycle regular (parent-reported)
                ph_p_pds__f_002__05,   # Currently using hormonal birth control (parent-reported)
                ph_p_pds_001,          # Height growth status (parent-reported)
                ph_p_pds_002,          # Body hair growth status (parent-reported)
                ph_p_pds_003,          # Skin/acne change status (parent-reported)
                ph_p_pds__f_001,       # Breast development status (parent-reported)
                ph_p_pds__m_001        # Voice deepening status (parent-reported)
                ),
            by = c("participant_id", "session_id")) %>%
  
  # --- Exposome: General SES factor score (left join; supplementary measure) ---
  left_join(exposome %>% 
              dplyr::select(
                participant_id, 
                session_id, 
                General_SES #General Exposome
                ),
             by = c("participant_id", "session_id")) %>%
  
  # --- CBCL: Parent-reported mental health scales (left join; supplementary measure) ---
  left_join(cbcl %>% 
              dplyr::select(
                participant_id, 
                session_id, 
                mh_p_cbcl__synd__int_sum, # Internalizing problems sum score, raw
                mh_p_cbcl__synd__ext_sum, # Externalizing problems sum score, raw
                mh_p_cbcl_sum,            # Total problems sum score, raw
                mh_p_cbcl__dsm__anx_sum,  # DSM-5 anxiety problems sum score, raw
                mh_p_cbcl__dsm__dep_sum,  # DSM-5 depressive problems sum score, raw
                mh_p_cbcl__synd__int_tscore # Internalizing problems T-score
                ),
             by = c("participant_id", "session_id")) %>%
  
  # --- KSADS: Binary depression diagnosis variables (left join; supplementary measure) ---
  # depression_diagnosis      : Any current depressive disorder at this wave
  # depression_diagnosis_ever : Any depressive disorder at any study wave
  left_join(ksads %>% 
              dplyr::select(
                participant_id, 
                session_id, 
                depression_diagnosis, 
                depression_diagnosis_ever
                ),
             by = c("participant_id", "session_id")) %>%
  
  # --- BPM: Youth-reported internalizing problems (left join; supplementary measure) ---
  left_join(bpm %>% 
              dplyr::select(
                participant_id, 
                session_id, 
                mh_y_bpm__int_sum, # Internalizing problems sum score, raw
                mh_y_bpm__int_tscore, # Internalizing problems T-score
                mh_y_bpm__ext_sum, # Externalizing problems sum score, raw
                mh_y_bpm__ext_tscore # Externalizing problems T-score
                ),
             by = c("participant_id", "session_id")) %>%
  
  # --- ABCD-ARMS: Accelerated maturation group assignment (left join) ---
  left_join(ABCD_arms %>% 
              dplyr::select(
                participant_id, 
                session_id, 
                matched_group
                ),
            by = c("participant_id", "session_id")) %>%
  
  # --- BMI ---
  left_join(phys_y %>% 
              dplyr::select(
                participant_id, 
                session_id, 
                bmi
                ),
            by = c("participant_id", "session_id"))
```

```{r females_only, include=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# FILTER BY SEX: CREATE SEX-STRATIFIED SUBSETS
# =============================================================================
# Analyses focus on female participants, as menarche and female pubertal
# development are the primary exposures of interest. Separate female-only and
# male-only subsets are created here. The male-only subset is retained for
# potential use in sensitivity or comparison analyses in the future.
#
# Sex is coded in ab_g_stc__cohort_sex as: 1 = Male; 2 = Female.
# =============================================================================

# Inspect observation counts by session and sex prior to filtering,
# as a quality check on the merged dataset
merged_df %>%
  count(session_id, ab_g_stc__cohort_sex)


# --- Female-only subset ---
# Retain all participant-wave observations where sex == 2 (Female)
female_only <- merged_df %>%
  filter(ab_g_stc__cohort_sex == 2)

# Confirm the number of unique female participants retained
female_only %>%
  distinct(participant_id)

# --- Male-only subset ---
# Retain all participant-wave observations where sex == 1 (Male)
males_only <- merged_df %>%
  filter(ab_g_stc__cohort_sex == 1)

# Confirm the number of unique male participants retained
males_only %>%
  distinct(participant_id)
```

# Create Variable "Age of Menrache Onset" from youth report
```{r create_age_of_menarche_variable, echo=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# CLEAN YOUTH-REPORTED AGE AT MENARCHE AND DERIVE MENARCHE TIMING VARIABLES
# =============================================================================
# This chunk performs three operations:
#
#   1. DATA CLEANING: Invalid and implausible values of youth-reported age at
#      menarche (ph_y_pds__f_002__01) are identified and corrected based on
#      cross-wave inspection of each participant's longitudinal record.
#
#   2. MENARCHE AGE DERIVATION: Because participants may report slightly
#      different ages at menarche across waves (e.g., due to recall variability), 
#      the median of all non-missing, valid reports per participant is used as 
#      the final menarche age estimate (menarche_age_y).
#      Inconsistent reporters are identified and inspected prior to this step.
#
#   3. TIME FROM MENARCHE: A continuous variable representing time (in years)
#      elapsed since menarche at each study wave is computed as visit age minus
#      menarche age (Time_to_from_Menarche_y). We also call this variable
#      GYNECOLOGICAL AGE here and in the manuscript. Negative values indicate
#      pre-menarcheal assessments; positive values indicate post-menarcheal
#      assessments.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: INITIAL CLEANING
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# If a participant reported not yet having had menarche (ph_y_pds__f_002 == 0),
# set their reported age at menarche to NA
female_only <- female_only %>%
  mutate(
    ph_y_pds__f_002__01 = ifelse(ph_y_pds__f_002 == 0, NA, ph_y_pds__f_002__01)
  )

# Inspect the distribution of reported menrache ages
female_only %>%
  count(ph_y_pds__f_002__01)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: IDENTIFY AND INSPECT IMPLAUSIBLE VALUES
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The following values were flagged as implausible or erroneous based on
# inspection of each participant's full longitudinal record:

# 0	needs to be set to 9 (there were multiple entries saying 9)
# 0.11 needs to bet set to 11 (there were multiple entries saying 11)
# 5	needs to be set to NA	(there was only one entry saying 5 as age of menarche onset). 
# This seems very young so we decided to set this to NA)		
# 6	in both participants should be NA (other entries suggested older age of menarche)
# 110 needs to be set to 11 (there were multiple entries saying 11 as age of menarche onset, 
# we assume 110 is a typo meaning 11)
# 117 needs to be set to 11 (117 as age of menarche onset, which we assume should 
# be 11 (years of age), as the participant indicated to be menstruating in year 
# 4 and 5 follow-up (where the participant indicated 11))
# 2021 needs to be set to 12, as other follow-ups indicate 12

# Extract all sessions for participants with any flagged value,
# to allow cross-wave verification of recoding decisions
tbl_zero_participants <- female_only %>%
  filter(
    ph_y_pds__f_002__01 == 0 | 
      ph_y_pds__f_002__01 == 0.11 | 
      ph_y_pds__f_002__01 == 5 | 
      ph_y_pds__f_002__01 == 6 | 
      ph_y_pds__f_002__01 == 110 | 
      ph_y_pds__f_002__01 == 117 | 
      ph_y_pds__f_002__01 == 2021
    ) %>%      
  distinct(participant_id) %>%               # get unique participant IDs
  inner_join(female_only, by = "participant_id") %>%  # get all sessions for them
  dplyr::select(participant_id, session_id, ph_y_pds__f_002__01, ab_g_dyn__visit_age) %>%
  arrange(participant_id, session_id) %>%
  as_tibble()

tbl_zero_participants

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: APPLY CORRECTIONS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Each implausible value is corrected individually using if_else() to preserve
# all other values. Corrections are applied sequentially to cleaned_filtered_female_only,
# a new dataframe that preserves the uncorrected female_only dataframe for reference.

cleaned_filtered_female_only <- female_only %>%
  mutate(ph_y_pds__f_002__01 = if_else(ph_y_pds__f_002__01 == 0, 9, ph_y_pds__f_002__01)) %>%
  mutate(ph_y_pds__f_002__01 = if_else(ph_y_pds__f_002__01 == 0.11, 11, ph_y_pds__f_002__01)) %>%
  mutate(ph_y_pds__f_002__01 = if_else(ph_y_pds__f_002__01 == 5, NA, ph_y_pds__f_002__01)) %>%
  mutate(ph_y_pds__f_002__01 = if_else(ph_y_pds__f_002__01 == 6, NA, ph_y_pds__f_002__01)) %>%
  mutate(ph_y_pds__f_002__01 = if_else(ph_y_pds__f_002__01 == 110, 11, ph_y_pds__f_002__01)) %>%
  mutate(ph_y_pds__f_002__01 = if_else(ph_y_pds__f_002__01 == 117, 11, ph_y_pds__f_002__01)) %>%
  mutate(ph_y_pds__f_002__01 = if_else(ph_y_pds__f_002__01 == 2021, 12, ph_y_pds__f_002__01))

# Verify corrected distribution
cleaned_filtered_female_only %>%
  count(ph_y_pds__f_002__01)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: IDENTIFY PARTICIPANTS WITH INCONSISTENT CROSS-WAVE MENARCHE REPORTS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Participants who reported different ages at menarche across waves are
# identified for inspection. This informs the decision to use the median
# rather than a single wave's value as the final menarche age estimate.

# Summarize the number of distinct non-missing menarche age values per participant
# and list all reported ages for review
pds_summary <- cleaned_filtered_female_only %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  summarise(
    unique_ph_y_pds = n_distinct(ph_y_pds__f_002__01, na.rm = TRUE), # number of distinct reported ages
    ages_list = paste(sort(unique(ph_y_pds__f_002__01[!is.na(ph_y_pds__f_002__01)])), collapse = ", "), # all reported ages
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# Retain only participants with more than one distinct reported menarche age
inconsistent_participants <- pds_summary %>%
  filter(unique_ph_y_pds > 1)

inconsistent_participants


# Pivot the session-level menarche age data to wide format to facilitate
# visual inspection of inconsistencies across waves
pds_wide <- cleaned_filtered_female_only %>%
  dplyr::select(participant_id, session_id, ph_y_pds__f_002__01) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = session_id,
    values_from = ph_y_pds__f_002__01,
    names_prefix = "session_"
  )

# Combine the inconsistency summary with the wide-format session data
# for a complete view of each inconsistent participant's longitudinal record
pds_full_summary <- pds_summary %>%
  filter(unique_ph_y_pds > 1) %>%  # keep only participants with inconsistencies
  left_join(pds_wide, by = "participant_id")

pds_full_summary

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 5: DERIVE FINAL MENARCHE AGE (MEDIAN ACROSS WAVES)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# For participants with consistent reports, the median equals their single
# reported value. For inconsistent reporters, the median provides a robust
# central estimate that down-weights any remaining outlying reports.

cleaned_filtered_female_only <- cleaned_filtered_female_only %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  mutate(
    menarche_age_y = median(ph_y_pds__f_002__01, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Inspect the derived menarche age per wave
menarche_age <- cleaned_filtered_female_only %>%
  dplyr::select(participant_id, session_id, ph_y_pds__f_002__01, menarche_age_y) %>%
  arrange(participant_id, session_id) %>%
  as_tibble() 

menarche_age

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 6: DERIVE TIME FROM MENARCHE AT EACH WAVE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Time from menarche (gynecologial age) is computed as visit age minus 
# menarche age (in years).
# Negative values indicate the visit occurred before menarche;
# positive values indicate the visit occurred after menarche.
# This variable is used as a continuous measure in models.

cleaned_filtered_female_only <- cleaned_filtered_female_only %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  mutate(
    Time_to_from_Menarche_y = ab_g_dyn__visit_age - menarche_age_y
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Inspect the derived variable alongside its components per wave
Time_from_Menarche <- cleaned_filtered_female_only %>%
  dplyr::select(participant_id, 
                session_id, 
                ph_y_pds__f_002__01, 
                menarche_age_y, 
                Time_to_from_Menarche_y) %>%
  arrange(participant_id, session_id) %>%
  as_tibble()  

Time_from_Menarche
```


# Join Dataframe with Brain Measures
```{r join_dataframe_with_brain_measures, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Join Dataframe with Brain Measures
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Step 1: Create bilateral (left + right hemisphere) summary measures
# These variables aggregate region-specific volumes across hemispheres

brain_volume <- brain_volume %>%
  mutate(
    # Cerebellum: gray + white matter (left + right)
    total_cerebellum = mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__cbc__lh_sum + 
      mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__cbc__rh_sum + 
      mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__cbwm__lh_sum + 
      mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__cbwm__rh_sum) %>%
  mutate(
    # Corpus callosum: sum of all subregions
    total_CC = mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__cca_sum + 
      mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__ccam_sum + 
      mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__ccc_sum + 
      mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__ccp_sum + 
      mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__ccpm_sum) %>%
  mutate(
    # Subcortical structures (bilateral sums)
    total_accumbens = mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__ab__lh_sum + mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__ab__rh_sum,
    total_amygdala = mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__ag__lh_sum + mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__ag__rh_sum,
    total_caudate = mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__cd__lh_sum + mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__cd__rh_sum,
    total_hippocampus = mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__hc__lh_sum + mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__hc__rh_sum,
    total_pallidum = mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__pl__lh_sum + mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__pl__rh_sum,
    total_putamen = mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__pt__lh_sum + mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__pt__rh_sum,
    total_thalamus = mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__th__lh_sum + mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__th__rh_sum,
    total_ventralDC = mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__vdc__lh_sum + mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__vdc__rh_sum) %>%
  mutate(
    # Total cerebral white matter (bilateral)
    total_cerebral_WM = mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__cwm__lh_sum + mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__cwm__rh_sum)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: Merge brain measures with main analysis dataset (females only)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain <- cleaned_filtered_female_only %>%
  left_join(brain_volume %>% dplyr::select(participant_id,session_id,
                                           mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__whb_sum, # whole brain volume
                                           mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__csf_sum, # CSF
                                           mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__icv_sum, # ICV
                                           total_cerebral_WM,  
                                           total_cerebellum,
                                           mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__lvs_sum, # lateral ventricles
                                           mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__scgv_sum, # subcortical gray matter
                                           total_thalamus,
                                           total_caudate,
                                           total_putamen,
                                           total_pallidum,
                                           total_hippocampus,
                                           total_amygdala,
                                           total_accumbens,
                                           total_ventralDC,
                                           total_CC),
            by = c("participant_id", "session_id")) %>%
  # Add global cortical measures
  left_join(brain_volume_dsk %>% dplyr::select(participant_id,session_id,
                                               mr_y_smri__vol__dsk_sum), # cortical volume
            by = c("participant_id", "session_id")) %>%
  left_join(brain_thickness %>% dplyr::select(participant_id,session_id, 
                                              mr_y_smri__thk__dsk_mean), # mean cortical thickness
            by = c("participant_id", "session_id")) %>%
  left_join(brain_surface %>% dplyr::select(participant_id,session_id,
                                            mr_y_smri__area__dsk_sum), # surface area
            by = c("participant_id", "session_id")) %>%
  
  # Add QC dataframe
  left_join(qc %>% dplyr::select(participant_id,session_id,
                                 mr_y_qc__incl__smri__t1_indicator),
            by = c("participant_id", "session_id"))


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: Apply MRI quality control filtering
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Set all structural MRI measures to NA if the T1-weighted scan
# did not pass ABCD quality control (indicator == 0).
# This ensures that only good-quality neuroimaging data are used in analyses.
cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__whb_sum,
        mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__csf_sum,
        mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__icv_sum,
        total_cerebral_WM,
        total_cerebellum,
        mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__lvs_sum,
        mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__scgv_sum,
        total_thalamus,
        total_caudate,
        total_putamen,
        total_pallidum,
        total_hippocampus,
        total_amygdala,
        total_accumbens,
        total_ventralDC,
        total_CC,
        mr_y_smri__vol__dsk_sum,
        mr_y_smri__thk__dsk_mean,
        mr_y_smri__area__dsk_sum),
      ~ if_else(mr_y_qc__incl__smri__t1_indicator == 0, NA_real_, .x)
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: Repeat merging and QC procedure for males
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The same processing steps are applied to the male subset to ensure
# consistency across sex-stratified analyses.
males_only_brain <- males_only %>%
  left_join(brain_volume %>% dplyr::select(participant_id,session_id,
                                           mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__whb_sum,
                                           mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__csf_sum,
                                           mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__icv_sum,
                                           total_cerebral_WM,
                                           total_cerebellum,
                                           mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__lvs_sum,
                                           mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__scgv_sum,
                                           total_thalamus,
                                           total_caudate,
                                           total_putamen,
                                           total_pallidum,
                                           total_hippocampus,
                                           total_amygdala,
                                           total_accumbens,
                                           total_ventralDC,
                                           total_CC),
            by = c("participant_id", "session_id")) %>%
  left_join(brain_volume_dsk %>% dplyr::select(participant_id,session_id,
                                               mr_y_smri__vol__dsk_sum),
            by = c("participant_id", "session_id")) %>%
  left_join(brain_thickness %>% dplyr::select(participant_id,session_id,
                                              mr_y_smri__thk__dsk_mean),
            by = c("participant_id", "session_id")) %>%
  left_join(brain_surface %>% dplyr::select(participant_id,session_id,
                                            mr_y_smri__area__dsk_sum),
            by = c("participant_id", "session_id")) %>%
  left_join(qc %>% dplyr::select(participant_id,session_id,
                                 mr_y_qc__incl__smri__t1_indicator),
            by = c("participant_id", "session_id"))


# Apply identical QC filtering for males
males_only_brain <- males_only_brain %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__whb_sum,
        mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__csf_sum,
        mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__icv_sum,
        total_cerebral_WM,
        total_cerebellum,
        mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__lvs_sum,
        mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__scgv_sum,
        total_thalamus,
        total_caudate,
        total_putamen,
        total_pallidum,
        total_hippocampus,
        total_amygdala,
        total_accumbens,
        total_ventralDC,
        total_CC,
        mr_y_smri__vol__dsk_sum,
        mr_y_smri__thk__dsk_mean,
        mr_y_smri__area__dsk_sum),
      ~ if_else(mr_y_qc__incl__smri__t1_indicator == 0, NA_real_, .x)
    )
  )
```

# Use baseline exposome for all sessions
```{r baseline_exposome, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Use baseline general exposome across all longitudinal sessions
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Rationale:
# The general exposome variable is anchored at baseline
# (session "ses-00A") and carried forward to all subsequent timepoints.

# For females
cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  mutate(General_SES_baseline = General_SES[session_id =="ses-00A"][1])

# For Males 
males_only_brain <- males_only_brain %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  mutate(General_SES_baseline = General_SES[session_id =="ses-00A"][1])
```

```{r baseline_exposome NA, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Exclude participants without baseline general exposome data
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Rationale:
# Participants missing the baseline general exposome (session "ses-00A") are excluded
# from all analyses to ensure a consistent sample.

# For Females
cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  filter(!is.na(General_SES_baseline))

# Inspect remaining unique participants after exclusion
cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  distinct(participant_id)

# For Males
males_only_brain <- males_only_brain %>%
  filter(!is.na(General_SES_baseline))
```

# Reporting Menarche Distribution
```{r menarche_reporting_distributions, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reporting Menarche Distribution and Sample Characterization
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Total number of unique participants
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  summarise(total_participants = n_distinct(participant_id)) %>%
  as_tibble()
# Note: This corresponds to the total analytic female sample (n ≈ 5655)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Characterize menarche status across participants
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

menarche_status_summary <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  # Encode session order numerically to identify most recent observation
  mutate(session_id_numeric = case_when(
    session_id == "ses-00A" ~ 0,
    session_id == "ses-01A" ~ 1,
    session_id == "ses-02A" ~ 2,
    session_id == "ses-03A" ~ 3,
    session_id == "ses-04A" ~ 4,
    session_id == "ses-05A" ~ 5,
    session_id == "ses-06A" ~ 6,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  )) %>% 
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  summarise(
    # Indicator: participant ever reported menarche (PDS item == 1)
    has_1 = any(ph_y_pds__f_002 == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    # Most recent available response on the menarche question
    latest_visit = ph_y_pds__f_002[which.max(session_id_numeric)],
    
    # Participant never provided any valid response
    only_na = all(is.na(ph_y_pds__f_002)),
    
    # Participant only provided "don't know" or "refuse" responses
    only_777_999 = all(ph_y_pds__f_002 %in% c(777, 999), na.rm = FALSE),
    
    # Availability of reported menarche age
    menarche_age_reported = any(!is.na(menarche_age_y))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Categorize participants into mutually exclusive groups
    menarche_status = case_when(
      
      # No usable data
      only_na ~ "Missing",
      
      # Non-substantive responses only
      only_777_999 ~ "Don't know / Refuse to answer",
      
      # Reported menarche and provided age
      has_1 & menarche_age_reported ~ "reported menarche + menarche age",
      
      # Reported menarche but missing age
      has_1 & !menarche_age_reported ~ "reported menarche but no menarche age",
      
      # Has not yet reached menarche (based on most recent report)
      !has_1 & latest_visit == 0 ~ "did not hit menarche yet",
      
      # Refusal/don't know at latest visit
      !has_1 & latest_visit %in% c(777,999) ~ "Don't know / Refuse to answer",
      
      # Missing at latest visit
      !has_1 & is.na(latest_visit) ~ "Missing",
      
      # Catch-all for unusual response patterns
      TRUE ~ "777/999/NA on last visit"
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Count participants per menarche status category
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

menarche_status_summary_table <- menarche_status_summary %>%
  count(menarche_status, name = "n_participants") %>%
  arrange(menarche_status) %>%
  as_tibble()

menarche_status_summary_table

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Identify first session at which menarche + age were reported
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# This captures the earliest longitudinal timepoint at which participants
# both reported menarche and provided a valid menarche age.
first_menarche <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  filter(ph_y_pds__f_002 == 1,
         !is.na(menarche_age_y)) %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  summarise(first_session = min(session_id))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cumulative distribution of menarche reporting across sessions
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Number and cumulative proportion of participants reporting menarche age
# by each session (used for visualization of developmental timing)
cumulative_data <- first_menarche %>%
  group_by(first_session) %>%
  summarise(n_reported = n()) %>%
  arrange(first_session) %>%
  mutate(cumulative_reported = cumsum(n_reported),
         cumulative_percentage = (cumulative_reported / 5655) * 100)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Age distribution of participants across sessions
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Mean age per session (chronological age at assessment)
mean_chron_age_per_session <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  group_by(session_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_participants = n_distinct(participant_id),
    mean_age = mean(ab_g_dyn__visit_age, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_age = sd(ab_g_dyn__visit_age, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  arrange(session_id) %>%
  as_tibble()

mean_chron_age_per_session

# Range of ages per session (to characterize age spread within waves)
range_chron_age_per_session <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  group_by(session_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_participants = n_distinct(participant_id),
    min_age = min(ab_g_dyn__visit_age, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_age = max(ab_g_dyn__visit_age, na.rm = TRUE),
  ) %>%
  arrange(session_id) %>%
  as_tibble()
range_chron_age_per_session

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Prepare labels for cumulative figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Combine counts and percentages into formatted labels for visualization
cumulative_data <- cumulative_data %>%
  mutate(label_text = paste0(n_reported, "\n(", round(cumulative_percentage, 1), "%)"))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Figure: Cumulative number of participants reporting menarche age across sessions
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

menarche_across_waves <- ggplot(cumulative_data, aes(x = first_session, y = cumulative_reported, group = 1)) +
  #geom_hline(yintercept = 5655, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
  #geom_hline(yintercept = 5016, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
  geom_line(color = "#99d8c9", size = 1.5) + #"#810f7c"
  geom_point(size = 6, shape = 21, fill = "#99d8c9", colour = "#016c59") +
  geom_text(aes(label = label_text),
            vjust = -0.5, 
            hjust = 0.9,
            size = 4,
            fontface = "bold") +
  labs(
    x = "",
    y = "Number of Participants"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    labels = c(
      "ses-00A" = "Baseline<br><span style='font-size:15px;'>*M* = 10 years</span>",
      "ses-01A" = "Follow-up 1<br><span style='font-size:15px;'>*M* = 11 years</span>",
      "ses-02A" = "Follow-up 2<br><span style='font-size:15px;'>*M* = 12 years</span>",
      "ses-03A" = "Follow-up 3<br><span style='font-size:15px;'>*M* = 13 years</span>",
      "ses-04A" = "Follow-up 4<br><span style='font-size:15px;'>*M* = 14 years</span>",
      "ses-05A" = "Follow-up 5<br><span style='font-size:15px;'>*M* = 15 years</span>",
      "ses-06A" = "Follow-up 6<br><span style='font-size:15px;'>*M* = 16 years</span>"
    )
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_markdown(angle = 45, hjust = 1)  # <- element_markdown is key
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, NA),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2))
  )
menarche_across_waves

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Save figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

save_plot('Figures/menarche_across_waves.pdf',
          plot = menarche_across_waves,
          base_height = 5, 
          base_width = 6)
```

# Age of Menarche Distribution
```{r menarche_age_distributions, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# MENARCHE AGE DISTRIBUTION: DESCRIPTIVE SUMMARY AND FIGURE
# =============================================================================
# This chunk restricts the neuroimaging subsample to participants with a valid
# menarche age estimate, then produces descriptive summaries and a bar chart
# (FIGURE: Menarche age distribution) showing the distribution of menarche age 
# (in whole years) across the sample.
#
# Note: This chunk operates on cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain, the
# neuroimaging subsample defined in a prior chunk, rather than the full
# female-only sample.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: RESTRICT TO PARTICIPANTS WITH A VALID MENARCHE AGE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Participants without a valid menarche age estimate (menarche_age_y = NA)
# are excluded. This removes participants who never reported having had
# menarche across any study wave.

cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  filter(!is.na(menarche_age_y))

# Confirm the number of unique participants remaining after exclusion
# (expected n = 5,016)
cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  summarise(total = n_distinct(participant_id)) %>%
  as_tibble()


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: SUMMARIZE MENARCHE AGE DISTRIBUTION
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# For each participant, the median menarche age across waves is computed
# (consistent with the derivation in the cleaning chunk). The distribution
# of these participant-level estimates is then tabulated.

# Tabulate exact (continuous) median menarche age values across participants
cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  summarise(menarche_age_y = median(menarche_age_y, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%  # or mean()
  ungroup() %>%
  count(menarche_age_y) %>%
  arrange(menarche_age_y) %>%
  as_tibble()

# Tabulate menarche age floored to whole years (for plotting and reporting)
# floor() is used rather than round() to reflect age-at-onset convention
# (i.e., age 11 = any age from 11.0 to 11.2)
count_reported_menarche_age <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  summarise(menarche_age_y = median(menarche_age_y, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%  # or mean()
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(menarche_age_y = floor(menarche_age_y)) %>%
  count(menarche_age_y) %>%
  arrange(menarche_age_y) %>%
  as_tibble()

count_reported_menarche_age

# Add percentage of total sample for each whole-year menarche age bin
count_reported_menarche_age <- count_reported_menarche_age %>%
  mutate(percentage = n / sum(n) * 100) %>%  # Calculate percentage
  ungroup()

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: COMPUTE MEAN AND SD FOR FIGURE ANNOTATION
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mean and SD are computed from the full participant-wave dataset (using the
# participant-level menarche_age_y variable broadcast across waves) rather than
# the collapsed participant-level summary, as na.rm = TRUE handles
# the repeated values correctly. These are used to annotate the figure only.

mean_age <- mean(cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain$menarche_age_y, na.rm = TRUE)
sd_age   <- sd(cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain$menarche_age_y, na.rm = TRUE)
mean_sd_label <- paste0("Mean = ", round(mean_age, 1), "\nSD = ", round(sd_age, 1))

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: PLOT MENARCHE AGE DISTRIBUTION (FIGURE: Menarche age distribution)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Bar chart showing the number of participants per whole-year menarche age bin.
# Bars are annotated with the percentage of the total sample.
# Mean and SD are displayed in the top-right corner as a text label.
menarche_distribution_fig <- ggplot(count_reported_menarche_age, 
       aes(x = menarche_age_y, y = n, fill = as.factor(floor(menarche_age_y)))) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", fill = "#99d8c9", color = "#016c59") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(percentage, 1), "%")),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), vjust = -0.3,
            size = 4,
            fontface="bold") +
  labs(title = "",
       x = "Age of Menarche (Years)",
       y = "Number of Participants",
       fill = "menarche_age_y") +
  #scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Reds") +    #other colors "BuPu" / "Set3"     
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 8:16) +               
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5), legend.position = "none") +
  geom_label(
    aes(x = 16, y = max(n) * 0.99, label = mean_sd_label),
    fill = "white",          # box color
    color = "black",         # text color
    hjust = 1, vjust = 1,    # top-right corner
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 6
  )
menarche_distribution_fig

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Save figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

save_plot('Figures/menarche_distribution_fig.pdf',
          plot = menarche_distribution_fig,
          base_height = 5, 
          base_width = 6)
```

# Alternative puberty markers
```{r alternative puberty markers, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# ALTERNATIVE PUBERTAL MARKERS: ONSET AGE AND VISUALIZATION
# =============================================================================
# In addition to menarche, four alternative pubertal markers are derived from
# the youth-reported PDS to characterize the broader pubertal timeline:
#
#   - Growth spurt onset   (ph_y_pds_001)
#   - Breast budding onset (ph_y_pds__f_001)
#   - Body hair onset      (ph_y_pds_002)
#   - Skin changes    (ph_y_pds_003)
#
# For each marker, onset is operationalized as the age at the first study wave
# at which the participant reported the change as "has barely started" (2)
# or "is definitely underway" (3). This captures the earliest confirmed observation
# of each pubertal event in the longitudinal record.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: DERIVE ONSET AGE FOR EACH PUBERTAL MARKER
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# For each marker, the earliest session at which onset was reported (value 2
# or 3 on the PDS item) is identified per participant. The visit age at that
# session is then retrieved from dynamicVariables and renamed to reflect the
# specific marker.
# Note: Values 2 and 3 correspond to "has barely started" and "definitely underway".
# Participants who never reported onset remain absent from each summary
# dataframe and will receive NA when joined to the main dataset.

# Growth spurt: first session where growth in height was reported as underway or complete
growth_spurt <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  filter(ph_y_pds_001 == 2 | ph_y_pds_001 == 3) %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  summarise(session_id = min(session_id)) %>%
  left_join(dynamicVariables %>% dplyr::select(participant_id, session_id, ab_g_dyn__visit_age),
            by = c("participant_id", "session_id")) %>%
  rename(growth_spurt_started = ab_g_dyn__visit_age)

# Breast budding: first session where breast development was reported as underway or complete
breast_budding <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  filter(ph_y_pds__f_001 == 2 | ph_y_pds__f_001 == 3) %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  summarise(session_id = min(session_id)) %>%
  left_join(dynamicVariables %>% dplyr::select(participant_id, session_id, ab_g_dyn__visit_age),
            by = c("participant_id", "session_id")) %>%
  rename(breast_budding_started = ab_g_dyn__visit_age)

# Body hair: first session where body hair growth was reported as underway or complete
body_hair <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  filter(ph_y_pds_002 == 2 | ph_y_pds_002 == 3) %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  summarise(session_id = min(session_id)) %>%
  left_join(dynamicVariables %>% dplyr::select(participant_id, session_id, ab_g_dyn__visit_age),
            by = c("participant_id", "session_id")) %>%
  rename(body_hair_started = ab_g_dyn__visit_age)

# Skin changes: first session where skin/acne changes were reported as underway or complete
skin_changes <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  filter(ph_y_pds_003 == 2 | ph_y_pds_003 == 3) %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  summarise(session_id = min(session_id)) %>%
  left_join(dynamicVariables %>% dplyr::select(participant_id, session_id, ab_g_dyn__visit_age),
            by = c("participant_id", "session_id")) %>%
  rename(skin_changes_started = ab_g_dyn__visit_age)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: COMBINE ALL PUBERTAL MARKERS INTO A SINGLE SUMMARY DATAFRAME
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A participant-level dataframe is constructed with one row per participant
# and one column per pubertal marker onset age. Menarche age is appended from
# the main dataset. full_join is used throughout so that participants missing
# any individual marker are retained with NA for that marker.

# Extract one menarche age value per participant (constant across waves)
menarche_unique <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  select(participant_id, menarche_age_y) %>%
  distinct()

# Combine all marker onset ages into a single wide-format dataframe
growth_charts <- growth_spurt %>%
  dplyr::select(participant_id, growth_spurt_started) %>%
  full_join(breast_budding %>% dplyr::select(participant_id, breast_budding_started),
            by = c("participant_id")) %>%
  full_join(body_hair %>% dplyr::select(participant_id, body_hair_started),
            by = c("participant_id")) %>%
  full_join(skin_changes %>% dplyr::select(participant_id, skin_changes_started),
```

# Menarche age and Exposome
```{r Menarche age and Exposome, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# ASSOCIATION BETWEEN MENARCHE AGE AND GENERAL EXPOSOME
# =============================================================================
# This chunk examines whether general exposome predicts age at menarche:
#
#   1. A Generalized Additive Mixed Model (GAMM) tests the association
#      between general exposome, with a random intercept
#      for assessment site to account for site-level clustering.
#
#   2. The empirical cumulative distribution function (ECDF) of menarche age is
#      computed separately for each general exposome decile, 
#      enabling visualization of how the full menarche age distribution 
#      shifts across the general exposome spectrum.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: GAMM — EFFECT OF GENERAL EXPOSOME ON MENARCHE AGE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A GAMM is fitted with menarche age as the outcome and general exposome (General_SES_baseline)
# as the linear predictor. A random intercept for assessment site (ab_g_dyn__design_site)
# accounts for non-independence of participants within sites.
# Only baseline observations (ses-00A) are used to avoid participant duplication,
# as menarche_age_y and General_SES_baseline are both constant across waves.
# REML estimation is used for unbiased variance component estimation.

timing_on_exposome <- gamm(menarche_age_y ~ General_SES_baseline,
                           method = "REML",
                           family = gaussian(),
                          data = cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>% 
                            dplyr::select(participant_id, session_id, menarche_age_y, General_SES_baseline, ab_g_dyn__design_site) %>% 
                            filter(session_id == "ses-00A"),
                          random = list(ab_g_dyn__design_site = ~1))
summary(timing_on_exposome$gam)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: COMPUTE ECDF OF MENARCHE AGE BY DECILE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Participants are assigned to exposome deciles (1 = lowest expsome, 10 = highest exposome)
# based on their baseline score. Within each decile, the empirical
# cumulative distribution of menarche age (floored to whole years) is computed.
# This captures how the probability of having reached menarche by a given age
# differs across the exposome spectrum.

ecdf_exposome <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  filter(!is.na(General_SES_baseline),
         !is.na(menarche_age_y)) %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  summarise(
    General_SES_baseline = first(General_SES_baseline),
    menarche_age_y = first(menarche_age_y)
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    SES_decile = ntile(General_SES_baseline, 10),
    menarche_age_y_floor = floor(menarche_age_y)
  ) %>%
  group_by(SES_decile, menarche_age_y_floor) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(SES_decile) %>%
  mutate(cdf = cumsum(count) / sum(count))

colnames(ecdf_exposome)[colnames(ecdf_exposome) == "SES_decile"] <- "General Exposome"

ecdf_exposome <- ecdf_exposome %>%
  mutate(cdf_percent = cdf*100)

# plot_menarche_by_group() produces a two-panel figure combining:
#   - Upper panel: ECDF curves showing cumulative probability of menarche
#     by age, with one line per group level coloured by the specified palette.
#   - Lower panel: Bar chart showing raw participant counts per menarche age
#     bin, coloured by group level.
# Panels are combined vertically using patchwork.
#
# Arguments:
#   data          : dataframe containing menarche_age_y_floor, cdf_percent,
#                   count, and the grouping variable
#   group_var     : character string naming the grouping variable (column name)
#   color_palette : character string specifying the rcartocolor palette to use
#                   ("PurpOr" or "Purp"); legend labels are fixed to "Low"/"High"

plot_menarche_by_group <- function(data, group_var, color_palette) {
  # Generate Color Scale Based on Provided Palette for Line (ECDF)
  color_scale_line <- switch(color_palette,
                             "PurpOr" = scale_color_carto_c(palette = "PurpOr", direction = 1, 
                                                          breaks = c(min(data$`General Exposome`), max(data$`General Exposome`)), 
                                                          labels = c("Low", "High")),
                             "Purp" = scale_color_carto_c(palette = "Purp", direction = 1, 
                                                          breaks = c(min(data$`General Exposome`), max(data$`General Exposome`)), 
                                                          labels = c("Low", "High")),
                             stop("Invalid color palette"))
  
  # Generate Color Scale Based on Provided Palette for Bar Plot (Fill)
  color_scale_fill <- switch(color_palette,
                             "PurpOr" = scale_fill_carto_c(palette = "PurpOr", direction = 1, 
                                                          breaks = c(min(data$`General Exposome`), max(data$`General Exposome`)), 
                                                          labels = c("Low", "High")),
                             "Purp" = scale_fill_carto_c(palette = "Purp", direction = 1, 
                                                          breaks = c(min(data$`General Exposome`), max(data$`General Exposome`)), 
                                                          labels = c("Low", "High")),
                             stop("Invalid color palette"))
  
  # ECDF Plot
  ecdf_plot <- ggplot(data, aes(x = menarche_age_y_floor, y = cdf_percent, color = get(group_var), group = get(group_var))) +
    geom_line(size = 1.5) +  # ECDF for each group
    labs(title = element_blank(),
         x = "",
         y = "Probability (%)",
         color = group_var) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
          legend.justification = c(0.1, 0.5),
          legend.direction = "vertical") +
    color_scale_line +  # Add color scale for the ECDF plot
    xlim(8, 16)
  
  # Bar Plot
  bar_plot <- ggplot(data, aes(x = menarche_age_y_floor, y = count, fill = get(group_var), group = get(group_var))) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", width = 0.9) +  # Bar plot for group counts
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
          legend.position = "none") +
    labs(title = element_blank(),
         x = "Menarche Age (Years)",
         y = "Number of Participants",
         fill = group_var) +
    color_scale_fill +  # Add color scale for the bar plot
    xlim(8, 16)
  
  # Combine the ECDF and Bar Plot Vertically using patchwork
  ecdf_plot / bar_plot
}

menarche_age_exposome_plot <- plot_menarche_by_group(ecdf_exposome, "General Exposome", "Purp")
menarche_age_exposome_plot

#save image as PDF
save_plot('Figures/menarche_age_exposome_plot.pdf',
          plot = menarche_age_exposome_plot,
          base_height = 5, 
          base_width = 6)
```

#Correlation of menarche timing and onset
```{r Make sure Site and Participant ID are factors, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# CORRELATIONS AMONG MENARCHE TIMING, TIME FROM MENARCHE, AND CHRONOLOGICAL AGE
# =============================================================================
# Before entering menarche-related variables into statistical models, pairwise
# Pearson correlations are computed to assess the degree of collinearity among
# three key continuous predictors:
#
#   1. menarche_age_y          : Age at menarche (years; participant-level constant)
#   2. Time_to_from_Menarche_y : Time elapsed since menarche at each wave (years;
#                                visit age − menarche age; varies across waves)
#   3. ab_g_dyn__visit_age     : Chronological age; Age at each study visit (years)
#
# These three variables are mathematically related by construction
# (Time_to_from_Menarche_y = visit_age − menarche_age_y), so high collinearity
# is expected between some pairs. These correlations inform decisions about
# which variables can be included simultaneously in statistical models.
# =============================================================================

# Correlation between menarche age and time from menarche
corr.test(cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain$menarche_age_y, cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain$Time_to_from_Menarche_y, use = "pairwise")

# Correlation between menarche age and chronological age
corr.test(cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain$menarche_age_y, cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain$ab_g_dyn__visit_age, use = "pairwise")

# Correlation between time from menarche and chronological age
corr.test(cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain$Time_to_from_Menarche_y, cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain$ab_g_dyn__visit_age, use = "pairwise")
```
