# ANALYSES
## CBCL Internalizing symptoms
### Chronological Age
```{r Int symptoms and age, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# GAMM: EFFECT OF CHRONOLOGICAL AGE ON CBCL INTERNALIZING SYMPTOMS
# =============================================================================
# This chunk models the non-linear trajectory of parent-reported internalizing
# symptoms (CBCL internalizing sum score) as a function of chronological age across the
# study period, co-varying for general exposome.
#
# Model specification:
#   - Outcome  : CBCL internalizing symptoms sum score (mh_p_cbcl__synd__int_sum)
#                modeled with a negative binomial family to account for the
#                overdispersed count distribution of symptom sum scores.
#   - Smooths  : Smooth functions for chronological age and general exposome
#                (both entered as smooth terms via s()), allowing non-linear
#                trajectories to be estimated from the data.
#   - Random effects: Random intercepts for participant (to account for
#                repeated measures) and site (to account for
#                site-level clustering), specified via the random argument.
#   - Estimation: REML, for unbiased smoothing parameter and variance
#                component estimation.
#
# Following model fitting, derivative-based analyses identify periods of
# significant change in the internalizing symptom trajectory, and a
# composite visualization is produced.
# Results are tidied and annotated with N and R² for reporting.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: FIT GAMM
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

age_on_inter <- mgcv::gamm(mh_p_cbcl__synd__int_sum ~ 
                             s(ab_g_dyn__visit_age) +
                             s(General_SES_baseline),
                           data = cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain,
                           method = "REML",
                           family = nb(),
                           random = list(participant_id = ~1, ab_g_dyn__design_site = ~1))
  
summary(age_on_inter$gam)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: TIDY MODEL OUTPUT AND EXTRACT FIT STATISTICS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# broom::tidy() extracts smooth term statistics (edf, F, p-value) into a
# dataframe. N (number of observations) and R² (deviance explained) are
# appended for inclusion in a results table.

tidy_age_on_inter_output <- tibble(
  model = "age_on_inter",
  tidy  = list(broom::tidy(age_on_inter$gam))
) %>%
  unnest(tidy)
tidy_age_on_inter_output$N = length(age_on_inter$gam$residuals)
summary_model <- summary(age_on_inter$gam)
tidy_age_on_inter_output$R2 = summary_model$r.sq

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: DERIVATIVE-BASED ANALYSIS OF THE AGE SMOOTH
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Simultaneous confidence intervals for the first and second derivatives of
# the age smooth are computed using derivative_stats(). This identifies:
#   - Periods of significant increase or decrease in internalizing symptoms
#     (first derivative significantly different from zero)
#   - The inflection point (maximum of the second derivative), indicating
#     where the rate of change is accelerating most rapidly

age_on_inter_dervs <- derivative_stats(
  age_on_inter,
  smooth_var = "ab_g_dyn__visit_age",
  make_plots = TRUE)  |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = "age_on_inter")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: VISUALIZE MODEL
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# visualize_model() produces a composite figure comprising:
#   - Main panel : fitted age smooth with confidence ribbon 
#   - Derivative panel: first derivative of the age smooth,
#.                      highlighting periods of significant change
#                       (derivative_plot = TRUE)
#   - Vertical reference line at age 11.8 years (mean menarche
#                  age in this sample; v_line = 11.8)
#   - Second derivative inflection point (maximum) annotated with 95% CI
#                  (sd_max_value, sd_max_lower_ci, sd_max_upper_ci)

age_on_inter_plot <- visualize_model(
    age_on_inter,
    smooth_var = "ab_g_dyn__visit_age",
    group_var = "participant_id",
    show.data = FALSE,
    side_density = TRUE,
    derivative_plot = TRUE,
    xlabel = "Age (Years)",
    ylabel = "CBCL Internalizing Symptoms",
    second_deriv_x = age_on_inter_dervs$sd_max_value,
    second_deriv_lower = age_on_inter_dervs$sd_max_lower_ci,
    second_deriv_upper = age_on_inter_dervs$sd_max_upper_ci,
    v_line = 11.8,
    )
age_on_inter_plot

# New Y-axis
age_on_inter_plot <- visualize_model(
    age_on_inter,
    smooth_var = "ab_g_dyn__visit_age",
    group_var = "participant_id",
    show.data = FALSE,
    side_density = FALSE,
    derivative_plot = FALSE,
    xlabel = "Chronological Age \n (Years)",
    ylabel = "CBCL Internalizing Symptoms",
    second_deriv_x = age_on_inter_dervs$sd_max_value,
    second_deriv_lower = age_on_inter_dervs$sd_max_lower_ci,
    second_deriv_upper = age_on_inter_dervs$sd_max_upper_ci,
    v_line = 11.8)
age_on_inter_plot <- age_on_inter_plot +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(2.5,5.5)) +
  labs(title = "Parent report")
age_on_inter_plot

# Tabulate periods of significant first-derivative change for reporting
get_derivative_table(age_on_inter, smooth_var = "ab_g_dyn__visit_age")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Save figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

save_plot('Figures/age_on_inter_plot.pdf',
          plot = age_on_inter_plot,
          base_height = 5, 
          base_width = 7)
```

### Menarche Age (Timing)
```{r Int symptoms and timing, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# GAMM: EFFECT OF MENARCHE AGE ON CBCL INTERNALIZING SYMPTOMS
# =============================================================================
# This chunk models the non-linear trajectory of parent-reported internalizing
# symptoms (CBCL internalizing sum score) as a function of meanrche age (timing)
# across the study period, co-varying for general exposome.
#
# Model specification:
#   - Outcome  : CBCL internalizing symptoms sum score (mh_p_cbcl__synd__int_sum)
#                modeled with a negative binomial family to account for the
#                overdispersed count distribution of symptom sum scores.
#   - Smooths  : Smooth functions for menarche age and general exposome
#                (both entered as smooth terms via s()), allowing non-linear
#                trajectories to be estimated from the data.
#   - Random effects: Random intercepts for participant (to account for
#                repeated measures) and site (to account for
#                site-level clustering), specified via the random argument.
#   - Estimation: REML, for unbiased smoothing parameter and variance
#                component estimation.
#
# Following model fitting, derivative-based analyses identify periods of
# significant change in the internalizing symptom trajectory, and a
# composite visualization is produced.
# Results are tidied and annotated with N and R² for reporting.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: FIT GAMM
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

timing_on_inter <- mgcv::gamm(mh_p_cbcl__synd__int_sum ~ 
                             s(menarche_age_y) +
                             s(General_SES_baseline),
                           data = cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain,
                           method = "REML",
                           family = nb(),
                           random = list(participant_id = ~1, ab_g_dyn__design_site = ~1))
  
summary(timing_on_inter$gam)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: TIDY MODEL OUTPUT AND EXTRACT FIT STATISTICS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# broom::tidy() extracts smooth term statistics (edf, F, p-value) into a
# dataframe. N (number of observations) and R² (deviance explained) are
# appended for inclusion in a results table.

tidy_timing_on_inter_output <- tibble(
  model = "timing_on_inter",
  tidy  = list(broom::tidy(timing_on_inter$gam))
) %>%
  unnest(tidy)
tidy_timing_on_inter_output$N = length(timing_on_inter$gam$residuals)
summary_model <- summary(timing_on_inter$gam)
tidy_timing_on_inter_output$R2 = summary_model$r.sq

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: DERIVATIVE-BASED ANALYSIS OF THE AGE SMOOTH
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Simultaneous confidence intervals for the first and second derivatives of
# the menarche age smooth are computed using derivative_stats(). This identifies:
#   - Periods of significant increase or decrease in internalizing symptoms
#     (first derivative significantly different from zero)
#   - The inflection point (maximum of the second derivative), indicating
#     where the rate of change is accelerating most rapidly; please note that the
#     smooth term was linear (edf = 1), so no inflection point was identified    

timing_on_inter_dervs <- derivative_stats(
  timing_on_inter,
  smooth_var = "menarche_age_y",
  make_plots = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = "timing_on_inter")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: VISUALIZE MODEL
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# visualize_model() produces a composite figure comprising:
#   - Main panel : fitted menarche age smooth with confidence ribbon 
#   - Derivative panel: first derivative of the menarche age smooth,
#                       highlighting periods of significant change
#                       (derivative_plot = TRUE)
#   - Second derivative inflection point (maximum) is not plotted since the smooth
#                       term was linear (edf = 1) and has no inflection point

timing_on_inter_plot <- visualize_model(
    timing_on_inter,
```

### Time from Menarche (Onset)
```{r Int symptoms and onset, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# GAMM: EFFECT OF GYNECOLOGICAL AGE ON CBCL INTERNALIZING SYMPTOMS
# =============================================================================
# This chunk models the non-linear trajectory of parent-reported internalizing
# symptoms (CBCL internalizing sum score) as a function of gynecological age 
# (Time from Menarche) across the study period, co-varying for both menarche age
# (menarche timing) and general exposome.
#
# Model specification:
#   - Outcome  : CBCL internalizing symptoms sum score (mh_p_cbcl__synd__int_sum)
#                modeled with a negative binomial family to account for the
#                overdispersed count distribution of symptom sum scores.
#   - Smooths  : Smooth functions for gynecological age, menarche timing, and
#                general exposome (entered as smooth terms via s()), allowing non-linear
#                trajectories to be estimated from the data.
#   - Random effects: Random intercepts for participant (to account for
#                repeated measures) and site (to account for
#                site-level clustering), specified via the random argument.
#   - Estimation: REML, for unbiased smoothing parameter and variance
#                component estimation.
#
# Following model fitting, derivative-based analyses identify periods of
# significant change in the internalizing symptom trajectory, and a
# composite visualization is produced.
# Results are tidied and annotated with N and R² for reporting.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: FIT GAMM
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

onset_on_inter <- mgcv::gamm(mh_p_cbcl__synd__int_sum ~
                              s(Time_to_from_Menarche_y) +
                              s(menarche_age_y) +
                              s(General_SES_baseline),
                              data = cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain,
                              method = "REML",
                              family = nb(),
                              random = list(participant_id = ~1, ab_g_dyn__design_site = ~1))
  
summary(onset_on_inter$gam)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: TIDY MODEL OUTPUT AND EXTRACT FIT STATISTICS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# broom::tidy() extracts smooth term statistics (edf, F, p-value) into a
# dataframe. N (number of observations) and R² (deviance explained) are
# appended for inclusion in a results table.

tidy_onset_on_inter_output <- tibble(
  model = "onset_on_inter",
  tidy  = list(broom::tidy(onset_on_inter$gam))
) %>%
  unnest(tidy)
tidy_onset_on_inter_output$N = length(onset_on_inter$gam$residuals)
summary_model <- summary(onset_on_inter$gam)
tidy_onset_on_inter_output$R2 = summary_model$r.sq

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: DERIVATIVE-BASED ANALYSIS OF THE AGE SMOOTH
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Simultaneous confidence intervals for the first and second derivatives of
# the gynecological age smooth are computed using derivative_stats(). This identifies:
#   - Periods of significant increase or decrease in internalizing symptoms
#     (first derivative significantly different from zero)
#   - The inflection point (maximum of the second derivative), indicating
#     where the rate of change is accelerating most rapidly

onset_on_inter_dervs <- derivative_stats(
    onset_on_inter, 
    smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y", 
    make_plots = TRUE
    ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = "onset_on_inter")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: VISUALIZE MODEL
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# visualize_model() produces a composite figure comprising:
#   - Main panel : fitted age smooth with confidence ribbon 
#   - Derivative panel: first derivative of the age smooth,
#.                      highlighting periods of significant change
#                       (derivative_plot = TRUE)
#   - Vertical reference line at 0 (person-specific menarche onset; v_line = 0)
#   - Second derivative inflection point (maximum) annotated with 95% CI
#                  (sd_max_value, sd_max_lower_ci, sd_max_upper_ci)

onset_on_inter_plot <- visualize_model(
    onset_on_inter,
    smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y",
    group_var = "participant_id",
    show.data = FALSE,
    side_density = TRUE,
    derivative_plot = TRUE,
    xlabel = "Time from Menarche (Years)",
    ylabel = "CBCL Internalizing Symptoms",
    second_deriv_x = onset_on_inter_dervs$sd_max_value,
    second_deriv_lower = onset_on_inter_dervs$sd_max_lower_ci,
    second_deriv_upper = onset_on_inter_dervs$sd_max_upper_ci,
    v_line = 0)
onset_on_inter_plot

# New Y-axis
onset_on_inter_plot <- visualize_model(
    onset_on_inter,
    smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y",
    group_var = "participant_id",
    show.data = FALSE,
    side_density = FALSE,
    derivative_plot = FALSE,
    xlabel = "Gynecological Age \n (Time from Menarche Onset in Years)",
    ylabel = "CBCL Internalizing Symptoms",
    xlimits = TRUE,
    second_deriv_x = onset_on_inter_dervs$sd_max_value,
    second_deriv_lower = onset_on_inter_dervs$sd_max_lower_ci,
    second_deriv_upper = onset_on_inter_dervs$sd_max_upper_ci,
    v_line = 0)
onset_on_inter_plot <- onset_on_inter_plot +
  #coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-5,5), ylim = c(2.9,5)) +
  labs(title = "Parent report")
onset_on_inter_plot

# Tabulate periods of significant first-derivative change for reporting
get_derivative_table(onset_on_inter, smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Save figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

save_plot('Figures/onset_on_inter_plot.pdf',
          plot = onset_on_inter_plot,
          base_height = 5, 
          base_width = 7)
```

#### Write mental health results
```{r Write mental health results, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# SAFE RESULTS FROM MENTAL HEALTH ANALYSIS IN TABLES
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: SAFE RESULTS FROM GAMMS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Combine results from all mental health models (internalizing + externalizing symptoms)
tidy_inter_exter_output <- bind_rows(
  tidy_age_on_inter_output,
  tidy_timing_on_inter_output,
  tidy_onset_on_inter_output,
  tidy_age_on_exter_output,
  tidy_timing_on_exter_output,
  tidy_onset_on_exter_output) 

## Correct for multiple comparisons using different methods (e.g. FDR, Bonferroni)
## and clean the output
tidy_inter_exter_output <- tidy_inter_exter_output %>%
  mutate(
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p.value, method = "fdr"),
    p_bonferroni = p.adjust(p.value, method = "bonferroni")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(p.value, p_fdr, p_bonferroni),
      ~ ifelse(.x == 0, "<.001", formatC(.x, format = "f", digits = 3))
    )
  )

## Write out results
write.csv(
  tidy_inter_exter_output,
  file = "Results/tidy_inter_exter_output.csv",
  row.names = FALSE)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: SAFE RESULTS FOR INFLECTION POINTS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Combine second derivative results (internalizing + externalizing symptoms)
second_derv_output_inter_exter <- bind_rows(
  age_on_inter_dervs,
  timing_on_inter_dervs,
  onset_on_inter_dervs,
  age_on_exter_dervs,
  timing_on_exter_dervs,
  onset_on_exter_dervs
)

## Clean the output
second_derv_output_inter_exter <- second_derv_output_inter_exter %>%
  dplyr::select(model, sd_min_value, sd_min_lower_ci, sd_min_upper_ci, sd_max_value, sd_max_lower_ci, sd_max_upper_ci) %>%
  mutate(
    second_derv_min_CI = paste0(
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_min_value), " [",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_min_lower_ci), ";",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_min_upper_ci), "]"
    ),
    second_derv_max_CI = paste0(
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_max_value), " [",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_max_lower_ci), ";",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_max_upper_ci), "]"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(model, second_derv_min_CI, second_derv_max_CI)

## Write out results
write.csv(
  second_derv_output_inter_exter,
  file = "Results/second_derv_output_inter_exter.csv",
  row.names = FALSE)
```

## BPM Internalizing symptoms
### Chronological Age
```{r Int symptoms and age, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# GAMM: EFFECT OF CHRONOLOGICAL AGE ON BPM INTERNALIZING SYMPTOMS
# =============================================================================
# This chunk models the non-linear trajectory of youth-reported internalizing
# symptoms (BPM internalizing sum score) as a function of chronological age across the
# study period, co-varying for general exposome.
#
# Model specification:
#   - Outcome  : BPM internalizing symptoms sum score (mh_y_bpm__int_sum)
#                modeled with a negative binomial family to account for the
#                overdispersed count distribution of symptom sum scores.
#   - Smooths  : Smooth functions for chronological age and general exposome
#                (both entered as smooth terms via s()), allowing non-linear
#                trajectories to be estimated from the data.
#   - Random effects: Random intercepts for participant (to account for
#                repeated measures) and site (to account for
#                site-level clustering), specified via the random argument.
#   - Estimation: REML, for unbiased smoothing parameter and variance
#                component estimation.
#
# Following model fitting, derivative-based analyses identify periods of
# significant change in the internalizing symptom trajectory, and a
# composite visualization is produced.
# Results are tidied and annotated with N and R² for reporting.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CONSTRUCT BPM ANALYSIS DATAFRAME
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
unique_ids <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>% distinct(participant_id)

bpm_dataframe <- bpm %>%
  dplyr::select(participant_id, session_id, mh_y_bpm_age, mh_y_bpm__int_sum, mh_y_bpm__ext_sum) %>%
  semi_join(unique_ids, by = "participant_id") %>%
  left_join(dynamicVariables %>% dplyr::select(participant_id, session_id, ab_g_dyn__design_site), 
            by = c("participant_id", "session_id")) %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  fill(ab_g_dyn__design_site, .direction = "updown") %>%  # fill within participant first
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(
    cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>% 
      distinct(participant_id, menarche_age_y),  # one row per participant
    by = "participant_id") %>%
  left_join(cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
             distinct(participant_id, General_SES_baseline, Matched_groups_baseline, ab_g_stc__design_id__fam),
            by = "participant_id") %>%
  left_join(
    cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>% 
      distinct(participant_id, growth_spurt_started),  # one row per participant
    by = "participant_id") %>%
  left_join(
    cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>% 
      distinct(participant_id, breast_budding_started),  # one row per participant
    by = "participant_id") %>%
  left_join(
    cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>% 
      distinct(participant_id, body_hair_started),  # one row per participant
    by = "participant_id") %>%
  left_join(
    cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>% 
      distinct(participant_id, skin_changes_started),  # one row per participant
    by = "participant_id") %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  mutate(
    # Recompute time-from-onset variables using BPM assessment age as reference
    Time_to_from_Menarche_y = mh_y_bpm_age - menarche_age_y,
    Time_to_from_growth_spurt_onset_y = mh_y_bpm_age - growth_spurt_started,
    Time_to_from_breast_budding_onset_y = mh_y_bpm_age - breast_budding_started,
    Time_to_from_body_hair_onset_y = mh_y_bpm_age - body_hair_started,
    Time_to_from_skin_changes_onset_y = mh_y_bpm_age - skin_changes_started
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(
    cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>% 
      dplyr::select(participant_id,
               session_id,
               mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__whb_sum,
               mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__scgv_sum,
               mr_y_smri__vol__dsk_sum,
               mr_y_smri__thk__dsk_mean,
               mr_y_smri__area__dsk_sum,
               total_cerebral_WM,
               mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__lvs_sum,
               mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__csf_sum),  
    by = c("participant_id", "session_id")) %>%
  left_join(phys_y %>% 
              dplyr::select(
                participant_id, 
                session_id, 
                bmi
                ),
            by = c("participant_id", "session_id"))

# Ensure grouping variables are factors for gamm()
bpm_dataframe$ab_g_dyn__design_site <- factor(bpm_dataframe$ab_g_dyn__design_site)
str(bpm_dataframe$ab_g_dyn__design_site)

bpm_dataframe$participant_id <- factor(bpm_dataframe$participant_id)
str(bpm_dataframe$participant_id)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: FIT GAMM
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

age_on_inter_bpm <- mgcv::gamm(mh_y_bpm__int_sum ~ 
                             s(mh_y_bpm_age) +
                             s(General_SES_baseline),
                           data = bpm_dataframe,
                           method = "REML",
                           family = nb(),
                           random = list(participant_id = ~1, ab_g_dyn__design_site = ~1))
  
summary(age_on_inter_bpm$gam)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: TIDY MODEL OUTPUT AND EXTRACT FIT STATISTICS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# broom::tidy() extracts smooth term statistics (edf, F, p-value) into a
# dataframe. N (number of observations) and R² (deviance explained) are
# appended for inclusion in a results table.

tidy_age_on_inter_bpm_output <- tibble(
  model = "age_on_inter_bpm",
  tidy  = list(broom::tidy(age_on_inter_bpm$gam))
) %>%
  unnest(tidy)
tidy_age_on_inter_bpm_output$N = length(age_on_inter_bpm$gam$residuals)
summary_model <- summary(age_on_inter_bpm$gam)
tidy_age_on_inter_bpm_output$R2 = summary_model$r.sq

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: DERIVATIVE-BASED ANALYSIS OF THE AGE SMOOTH
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Simultaneous confidence intervals for the first and second derivatives of
# the age smooth are computed using derivative_stats(). This identifies:
#   - Periods of significant increase or decrease in internalizing symptoms
#     (first derivative significantly different from zero)
#   - The inflection point (maximum of the second derivative), indicating
#     where the rate of change is accelerating most rapidly

age_on_inter_bpm_dervs <- derivative_stats(
  age_on_inter_bpm,
  smooth_var = "mh_y_bpm_age",
  make_plots = TRUE)  |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = "age_on_inter_bpm")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: VISUALIZE MODEL
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# visualize_model() produces a composite figure comprising:
#   - Main panel : fitted age smooth with confidence ribbon 
#   - Derivative panel: first derivative of the age smooth,
#.                      highlighting periods of significant change
#                       (derivative_plot = TRUE)
#   - Vertical reference line at age 11.8 years (mean menarche
#                  age in this sample; v_line = 11.8)
#   - Second derivative inflection point (maximum) annotated with 95% CI
#                  (sd_max_value, sd_max_lower_ci, sd_max_upper_ci)

age_on_inter_bpm_plot <- visualize_model(
    age_on_inter_bpm,
    smooth_var = "mh_y_bpm_age",
    group_var = "participant_id",
    show.data = FALSE,
    side_density = FALSE,
    derivative_plot = FALSE,
    xlabel = "Chronological Age \n (Years)",
    ylabel = "BPM Internalizing Symptoms",
    second_deriv_x = age_on_inter_bpm_dervs$sd_max_value,
    second_deriv_lower = age_on_inter_bpm_dervs$sd_max_lower_ci,
    second_deriv_upper = age_on_inter_bpm_dervs$sd_max_upper_ci,
    v_line = 11.8,
    )
age_on_inter_bpm_plot <- age_on_inter_bpm_plot +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.5,4.5)) +
  labs(title = "Youth report")
age_on_inter_bpm_plot

# Tabulate periods of significant first-derivative change for reporting
get_derivative_table(age_on_inter_bpm, smooth_var = "mh_y_bpm_age")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Save figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

save_plot('Figures/age_on_inter_bpm_plot.pdf',
          plot = age_on_inter_bpm_plot,
          base_height = 5, 
          base_width = 7)
```

### Menarche Age (Timing)
```{r Int symptoms and timing, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# GAMM: EFFECT OF MENARCHE AGE ON BPM INTERNALIZING SYMPTOMS
# =============================================================================
# This chunk models the non-linear trajectory of parent-reported internalizing
# symptoms (BPM internalizing sum score) as a function of meanrche age (timing)
# across the study period, co-varying for general exposome.
#
# Model specification:
#   - Outcome  : BPM internalizing symptoms sum score (mh_y_bpm__int_sum)
#                modeled with a negative binomial family to account for the
#                overdispersed count distribution of symptom sum scores.
#   - Smooths  : Smooth functions for menarche age and general exposome
#                (both entered as smooth terms via s()), allowing non-linear
#                trajectories to be estimated from the data.
#   - Random effects: Random intercepts for participant (to account for
#                repeated measures) and site (to account for
#                site-level clustering), specified via the random argument.
#   - Estimation: REML, for unbiased smoothing parameter and variance
#                component estimation.
#
# Following model fitting, derivative-based analyses identify periods of
# significant change in the internalizing symptom trajectory, and a
# composite visualization is produced.
# Results are tidied and annotated with N and R² for reporting.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: FIT GAMM
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

timing_on_inter_bpm <- mgcv::gamm(mh_y_bpm__int_sum ~ 
                             s(menarche_age_y) +
                             s(General_SES_baseline),
                           data = bpm_dataframe,
                           method = "REML",
                           family = nb(),
                           random = list(participant_id = ~1, ab_g_dyn__design_site = ~1))
  
summary(timing_on_inter_bpm$gam)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# dataframe. N (number of observations) and R² (deviance explained) are
# appended for inclusion in a results table.

) %>%
  unnest(tidy)
tidy_timing_on_inter_bpm_output$N = length(timing_on_inter_bpm$gam$residuals)
summary_model <- summary(timing_on_inter_bpm$gam)
tidy_timing_on_inter_bpm_output$R2 = summary_model$r.sq

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: DERIVATIVE-BASED ANALYSIS OF THE AGE SMOOTH
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Simultaneous confidence intervals for the first and second derivatives of
# the menarche age smooth are computed using derivative_stats(). This identifies:
#   - Periods of significant increase or decrease in internalizing symptoms
#     (first derivative significantly different from zero)
#   - The inflection point (maximum of the second derivative), indicating
#     where the rate of change is accelerating most rapidly; please note that the
#     smooth term was linear (edf = 1), so no inflection point was identified

#                       highlighting periods of significant change

#   - Second derivative inflection point (maximum) is not plotted since the smooth
#                       term was linear (edf = 1) and has no inflection point

timing_on_inter_bpm_plot <- visualize_model(
    timing_on_inter_bpm,
    smooth_var = "menarche_age_y",
    group_var = "participant_id",
    show.data = FALSE,
    side_density = FALSE,
    derivative_plot = FALSE,
    xlabel = "Menarche Age \n (Years)",
    ylabel = "BPM Internalizing Symptoms")
timing_on_inter_bpm_plot <- timing_on_inter_bpm_plot +
  # coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.5,4.5)) +
  labs(title = "Youth report")
timing_on_inter_bpm_plot

# Tabulate periods of significant first-derivative change for reporting
get_derivative_table(timing_on_inter_bpm, smooth_var = "menarche_age_y")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Save figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

save_plot('Figures/timing_on_inter_bpm_plot.pdf',
          plot = timing_on_inter_bpm_plot,
          base_height = 5, 
          base_width = 7)
```

```{r Ext symptoms and timing, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# visualize_model() produces a composite figure comprising:
#   - Main panel : fitted menarche age smooth with confidence ribbon 
#   - Derivative panel: first derivative of the menarche age smooth,
#                       highlighting periods of significant change
#                       (derivative_plot = TRUE)
#   - Second derivative inflection point (maximum) is not plotted since the smooth
#                       term was linear (edf = 1) and has no inflection point

timing_on_exter_bpm_plot <- visualize_model(
    timing_on_exter_bpm,
    smooth_var = "menarche_age_y",
    group_var = "participant_id",
    show.data = FALSE,
    side_density = FALSE,
    derivative_plot = FALSE,
    xlabel = "Menarche Age \n (Years)",
    ylabel = "BPM Externalizing Symptoms")
timing_on_exter_bpm_plot <- timing_on_exter_bpm_plot +
  # coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.5,4.5)) +
  labs(title = "Youth report")
timing_on_exter_bpm_plot

# Tabulate periods of significant first-derivative change for reporting
get_derivative_table(timing_on_exter_bpm, smooth_var = "menarche_age_y")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Save figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

save_plot('Figures/timing_on_exter_bpm_plot.pdf',
          plot = timing_on_exter_bpm_plot,
          base_height = 5, 
          base_width = 7)
```

### Time from Menarche (Onset)

```{r Ext symptoms and onset, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# GAMM: EFFECT OF GYNECOLOGICAL AGE ON CBCL EXTERNALIZING SYMPTOMS
# =============================================================================
# This chunk models the non-linear trajectory of parent-reported externalizing
# symptoms (CBCL externalizing sum score) as a function of gynecological age 
# (Time from Menarche) across the study period, co-varying for both menarche age
# (menarche timing) and general exposome.
#
# Model specification:
#   - Outcome  : CBCL externalizing symptoms sum score (mh_p_cbcl__synd__ext_sum)
#                modeled with a negative binomial family to account for the
#                overdispersed count distribution of symptom sum scores.
#   - Smooths  : Smooth functions for gynecological age, menarche timing, and
#                general exposome (entered as smooth terms via s()), allowing non-linear
#                trajectories to be estimated from the data.
#   - Random effects: Random intercepts for participant (to account for
#                repeated measures) and site (to account for
#                site-level clustering), specified via the random argument.
#   - Estimation: REML, for unbiased smoothing parameter and variance
#                component estimation.
#
# Following model fitting, derivative-based analyses identify periods of
# significant change in the externalizing symptom trajectory, and a
# composite visualization is produced.
# Results are tidied and annotated with N and R² for reporting.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: FIT GAMM
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

onset_on_exter_bpm <- mgcv::gamm(mh_y_bpm__ext_sum ~
                              s(Time_to_from_Menarche_y) +
                              s(menarche_age_y) +
                              s(General_SES_baseline),
                              data = bpm_dataframe,
                              method = "REML",
                              family = nb(),
                              random = list(participant_id = ~1, ab_g_dyn__design_site = ~1))
  
summary(onset_on_exter_bpm$gam)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: TIDY MODEL OUTPUT AND EXTRACT FIT STATISTICS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# broom::tidy() extracts smooth term statistics (edf, F, p-value) into a
# dataframe. N (number of observations) and R² (deviance explained) are
# appended for inclusion in a results table.

tidy_onset_on_exter_bpm_output <- tibble(
  model = "onset_on_exter_bpm",
  tidy  = list(broom::tidy(onset_on_exter_bpm$gam))
) %>%
  unnest(tidy)
tidy_onset_on_exter_bpm_output$N = length(onset_on_exter_bpm$gam$residuals)
summary_model <- summary(onset_on_exter_bpm$gam)
tidy_onset_on_exter_bpm_output$R2 = summary_model$r.sq

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: DERIVATIVE-BASED ANALYSIS OF THE AGE SMOOTH
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Simultaneous confidence intervals for the first and second derivatives of
# the gynecological age smooth are computed using derivative_stats(). This identifies:
#   - Periods of significant increase or decrease in internalizing symptoms
#     (first derivative significantly different from zero)
#   - The inflection point (maximum of the second derivative), indicating
#     where the rate of change is accelerating most rapidly

onset_on_exter_bpm_dervs <- derivative_stats(
    onset_on_exter_bpm, 
    smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y", 
    make_plots = TRUE
    ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = "onset_on_exter_bpm")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: VISUALIZE MODEL
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# visualize_model() produces a composite figure comprising:
#   - Main panel : fitted age smooth with confidence ribbon 
#   - Derivative panel: first derivative of the age smooth,
#.                      highlighting periods of significant change
#                       (derivative_plot = TRUE)
#   - Vertical reference line at 0 (person-specific menarche onset; v_line = 0)
#   - Second derivative inflection point (maximum) annotated with 95% CI
#                  (sd_max_value, sd_max_lower_ci, sd_max_upper_ci)

onset_on_exter_bpm_plot <- visualize_model(
    onset_on_exter_bpm,
    smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y",
    group_var = "participant_id",
    show.data = FALSE,
    side_density = TRUE,
    derivative_plot = TRUE,
    xlabel = "Time from Menarche (Years)",
    ylabel = "BPM Externalizing Symptoms",
    second_deriv_x = onset_on_exter_bpm_dervs$sd_max_value,
    second_deriv_lower = onset_on_exter_bpm_dervs$sd_max_lower_ci,
    second_deriv_upper = onset_on_exter_bpm_dervs$sd_max_upper_ci,
    v_line = 0)
onset_on_exter_bpm_plot

# New Y-axis
onset_on_exter_bpm_plot <- visualize_model(
    onset_on_exter_bpm,
    smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y",
    group_var = "participant_id",
    show.data = FALSE,
    side_density = FALSE,
    derivative_plot = FALSE,
    xlabel = "Gynecological Age \n (Time from Menarche Onset in Years)",
    ylabel = "BPM Externalizing Symptoms",
    xlimits = TRUE,
    second_deriv_x = onset_on_exter_bpm_dervs$sd_max_value,
    second_deriv_lower = onset_on_exter_bpm_dervs$sd_max_lower_ci,
    second_deriv_upper = onset_on_exter_bpm_dervs$sd_max_upper_ci,
    v_line = 0)
onset_on_exter_bpm_plot <- onset_on_exter_bpm_plot +
  # coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.5,4.5)) +
  labs(title = "Youth report")
onset_on_exter_bpm_plot

# Tabulate periods of significant first-derivative change for reporting
get_derivative_table(onset_on_exter_bpm, smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Save figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

save_plot('Figures/onset_on_exter_bpm_plot.pdf',
          plot = onset_on_exter_bpm_plot,
          base_height = 5, 
          base_width = 7)
```


#### Write mental health results
```{r Write mental health results, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# SAFE RESULTS FROM MENTAL HEALTH ANALYSIS IN TABLES
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: SAFE RESULTS FROM GAMMS (CBCL)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Combine results from all mental health models (internalizing + externalizing symptoms)
tidy_inter_exter_output <- bind_rows(
  tidy_age_on_inter_output,
  tidy_timing_on_inter_output,
  tidy_onset_on_inter_output,
  tidy_age_on_exter_output,
  tidy_timing_on_exter_output,
  tidy_onset_on_exter_output) 

## Correct for multiple comparisons using different methods (e.g. FDR, Bonferroni)
## and clean the output
tidy_inter_exter_output <- tidy_inter_exter_output %>%
  mutate(
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p.value, method = "fdr"),
    p_bonferroni = p.adjust(p.value, method = "bonferroni")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(p.value, p_fdr, p_bonferroni),
      ~ ifelse(.x == 0, "<.001", formatC(.x, format = "f", digits = 3))
    )
  )

## Write out results
write.csv(
  tidy_inter_exter_output,
  file = "Results/tidy_inter_exter_output.csv",
```

## Brain Measures
### Chronological Age
```{r brain measures and age, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# GAMM: EFFECT OF CHRONOLOGICAL AGE ON GROSS BRAIN MORPHOMETRY METRICS
# =============================================================================
# This chunk models the non-linear trajectory of eight gross brain
# morphometry metrics as a function of chronological age, co-varying for general
# exposome. The analytic approach mirrors the internalizing and externalizing 
# symptoms models, extended to multiple brain outcomes fitted in parallel.
#
# Model specification (identical across all metrics):
#   - Outcome  : Brain metric value (gaussian family; continuous measure in mm³,
#                mm, or mm²depending on metric)
#   - Smooths  : Smooth functions for chronological age and general exposome
#   - Random effects: Random intercepts for participant (repeated measures)
#                and assessment site (site-level clustering)
#   - Estimation: REML
#
# Models are fitted in parallel across metrics using parLapply(). 
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: RESHAPE DATA TO LONG FORMAT
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The wide-format dataframe (one column per brain metric) is pivoted to long
# format to enable a single split-apply workflow across all eight metrics.

cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_long <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c("mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__whb_sum", 
                        "mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__scgv_sum",
                        "mr_y_smri__vol__dsk_sum",
                        "total_cerebral_WM",
                        "mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__lvs_sum",
                        "mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__csf_sum",
                        "mr_y_smri__thk__dsk_mean",
                        "mr_y_smri__area__dsk_sum"),
               names_to = "MRI_metric",
               values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(MRI_metric = factor(MRI_metric,
                             levels = c("mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__whb_sum", 
                                        "mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__scgv_sum",
                                        "mr_y_smri__vol__dsk_sum",
                                        "mr_y_smri__thk__dsk_mean",
                                        "mr_y_smri__area__dsk_sum",
                                        "total_cerebral_WM",
                                        "mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__lvs_sum",
                                        "mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__csf_sum"),
                             labels = c("Whole brain volume",
                                        "Subcortical volume",
                                        "Gray matter volume",
                                        "Cortical thickness",
                                        "Surface area",
                                        "White matter volume",
                                        "Lateral ventricles volume",
                                        "CSF")))


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: ENSURE GROUPING VARIABLES ARE CODED AS FACTORS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_long$ab_g_dyn__design_site <- factor(cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_long$ab_g_dyn__design_site)
str(cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_long$ab_g_dyn__design_site)

cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_long$participant_id <- factor(cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_long$participant_id)
str(cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_long$participant_id)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: SPLIT DATA BY METRIC AND DEFINE MODEL-FITTING FUNCTION
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The long-format datafrmae is split into a list of eight dataframes, one per
# brain metric, enabling the same model to be fitted independently to each.

data_list <- split(cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_long,
                   cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_long$MRI_metric)

# Model-fitting function applied identically to each metric (this is identical to
# the internalizing and externalizing models:

fit_model <- function(data) {
  gamm(value ~ s(ab_g_dyn__visit_age) +
         s(General_SES_baseline),
       method = "REML",
       family = gaussian(),
       random = list(participant_id = ~1, ab_g_dyn__design_site = ~1),
       data = data)
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: FIT MODELS IN PARALLEL
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Models are fitted in parallel across the eight metrics using parLapply()
# mgcv is loaded on each worker node explicitly as it is not automatically
# available in the parallel environment.

n_cores <- min(8, detectCores() - 1)  # 8 metrics
cl <- makeCluster(n_cores)
clusterEvalQ(cl, library(mgcv))

brain_models_age <- parLapply(cl, data_list, fit_model)
stopCluster(cl)

# Organize fitted models into a named tibble for downstream processing
brain_models_age_output <- tibble(
  MRI_metric = names(brain_models_age),
  model = brain_models_age
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 5: EXTRACT DERIVATIVE TABLES
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# For each model, get_derivative_table() returns the age intervals over which
# the first derivative of the age smooth is significantly different from zero,
# indicating periods of significant increase or decrease in each brain metric.

brain_models_age_output %>%
  mutate(first_derv = map(model, ~get_derivative_table(
    ., smooth_var = "ab_g_dyn__visit_age"
  ))) %>%
  unnest(first_derv) %>%
  select(-model)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 6: TIDY MODEL OUTPUT AND EXTRACT FIT STATISTICS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# broom::tidy() extracts smooth term statistics (edf, F, p-value) for each
# metric. N (observations) and R² (adjusted; proportion of variance explained)
# are appended to each row for reporting.

tidy_brain_models_age_output <- brain_models_age_output %>%
  mutate(tidy = map(model, function(x) {
    tidydf = broom::tidy(x$gam)
    tidydf$N = length(x$gam$residuals)
    summary_model <- summary(x$gam)
    tidydf$R2 = summary_model$r.sq
    tidydf
  })) %>%
  unnest(tidy) %>%
  select(-model)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 7: EXTRACT SMOOTH ESTIMATES FOR THE CHRONOLOGICAL AGE TERM
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# smooth_estimates() returns the predicted smooth function and standard error
# at each age value in the data. Only the age smooth is retained here.
# Pointwise 95% confidence intervals are computed as estimate ± 1.96 × SE.

model_smooths_brain_models_age <- brain_models_age_output%>%
  mutate(smooths = map(model,smooth_estimates)) %>%
  unnest(smooths) %>%
  select(-model)%>%
  filter(.smooth=="s(ab_g_dyn__visit_age)") %>%
  mutate(upper=.estimate+1.96*.se,lower=.estimate-1.96*.se)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 8: DERIVATIVE-BASED ANALYSIS FOR EACH METRIC
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# derivative_stats() computes simultaneous confidence intervals for the first
# and second derivatives of the age smooth per metric, identifying:
#   - Periods of significant change (first derivative ≠ 0)
#   - Inflection point: age at which the rate of change is greatest
# Results are joined back to the model output tibble for use in visualization.

derv_brain_models_age_output <- brain_models_age_output%>%
  mutate(derv_stats = map(model,~derivative_stats(
    ., smooth_var = "ab_g_dyn__visit_age", make_plots = TRUE
  ))) %>%
  unnest(derv_stats) %>%
  select(-model)

# Append derivative statistics to the main model output tibble
brain_models_age_output <- brain_models_age_output %>%
  left_join(derv_brain_models_age_output, by = "MRI_metric")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 9: VISUALIZE AGE EFFECTS FOR EACH BRAIN METRIC
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# visualize_model() produces a composite figure per metric comprising:
#   - Main panel   : fitted age smooth with confidence ribbon and marginal
#                    density of the age distribution
#   - Derivative panel: first derivative, highlighting
#                    periods of significant change
#   - Vertical reference line at age 11.8 years (mean menarche age)
#   - Second derivative inflection point annotated with 95% CI
#     (using sd_min_value here)
# pmap() iterates over the model, metric label, and derivative statistics
# simultaneously to produce one plot per metric.

plots_tibble_onset <- brain_models_age_output %>%
  mutate(
    plot = pmap(
      list(model, MRI_metric, sd_min_value, sd_min_lower_ci, sd_min_upper_ci),
      function(mod, metric, sd_val, sd_lower, sd_upper) {
        visualize_model(
          mod, 
          smooth_var = "ab_g_dyn__visit_age",
          group_var = "participant_id",
          derivative_plot = FALSE,
          xlabel = "Age (years)",
          ylabel = metric,
          plabels = metric, 
          show.data = FALSE,
          side_density = FALSE,
          v_line = 11.8,
          second_deriv_x     = sd_val,
          second_deriv_lower = sd_lower,
          second_deriv_upper = sd_upper
        )
      }
    )
  )

plots_onset <- plots_tibble_onset %>%
  pull(plot)

age_with_point <- wrap_plots(plots_onset, ncol = 1)
age_with_point

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Save figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

save_plot('Figures/brain_models_age_with_point_plot.pdf',
          plot = age_with_point,
          base_height = 30,
          base_width = 5)
```

### Menarche Age (Timing)
```{r brain measures and timing, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# GAMM: EFFECT OF MENARCHE AGE (TIMING) ON GROSS BRAIN MORPHOMETRY
# =============================================================================
# This chunk models the non-linear association between menarche age and 
# each of the eight gross brain morphometry metrics, co-varying for general exposome.
#
# This analysis is structurally identical to the chronological age models
# with menarche_age_y substituted for ab_g_dyn__visit_age as the primary smooth term. 
# The long-format dataset (cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_long) and 
# metric-split list (data_list) are carried forward directly from that chunk; 
# no reshaping is required here.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: DEFINE MODEL-FITTING FUNCTION
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The model specification mirrors the age chunk, with menarche_age_y as the
# primary smooth term in place of ab_g_dyn__visit_age.

fit_model <- function(data) {
  gamm(value ~ s(menarche_age_y) +
         s(General_SES_baseline),
       method = "REML",
       family = gaussian(),
       random = list(participant_id = ~1, ab_g_dyn__design_site = ~1),
       data = data)
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: FIT MODELS IN PARALLEL
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Models are fitted in parallel across the eight metrics using the same
# data_list and cluster configuration as the age chunk.

n_cores <- min(8, detectCores() - 1)  # 8 metrics
cl <- makeCluster(n_cores)
clusterEvalQ(cl, library(mgcv))

brain_models_timing <- parLapply(cl, data_list, fit_model)
stopCluster(cl)

# Organise fitted models into a named tibble for downstream processing
brain_models_timing_output <- tibble(
  MRI_metric = names(brain_models_timing),
  model = brain_models_timing
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: TIDY MODEL OUTPUT AND EXTRACT FIT STATISTICS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# broom::tidy() extracts smooth term statistics (edf, F, p-value) per metric.
# N (observations) and R² (adjusted) are appended for reporting.

tidy_brain_models_timing_output <- brain_models_timing_output %>%
  mutate(tidy = map(model, function(x) {
    tidydf = broom::tidy(x$gam)
    tidydf$N = length(x$gam$residuals)
    summary_model <- summary(x$gam)
    tidydf$R2 = summary_model$r.sq
    tidydf
  })) %>%
  unnest(tidy) %>%
  select(-model)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: EXTRACT SMOOTH ESTIMATES FOR THE MENARCHE AGE TERM
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# smooth_estimates() returns the predicted smooth function and standard error
# across the range of menarche ages observed in the data.

model_smooths_brain_models_timing <- brain_models_timing_output%>%
  mutate(smooths = map(model,smooth_estimates)) %>%
  unnest(smooths) %>%
  select(-model)%>%
  filter(.smooth=="s(menarche_age_y)") %>%
  mutate(upper=.estimate+1.96*.se,lower=.estimate-1.96*.se)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 5: DERIVATIVE-BASED ANALYSIS FOR EACH METRIC
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# derivative_stats() computes simultaneous confidence intervals for the first
# and second derivatives of the menarche age smooth per metric, identifying:
#   - Ranges of menarche age associated with significant change in brain
#     morphometry (first derivative ≠ 0)
#   - The inflection point: menarche age at which the association with brain
#     morphometry changes most rapidly (second derivative maximum/minimum)
# Note: no inflection points were identified, since it mostly a linear association
# (edf = 1)


derv_brain_models_timing_output <- brain_models_timing_output%>%
  mutate(derv_stats = map(model,~derivative_stats(
    ., smooth_var = "menarche_age_y", make_plots = TRUE
  ))) %>%
  unnest(derv_stats) %>%
  select(-model)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 6: VISUALIZE MENARCHE AGE EFFECTS FOR EACH BRAIN METRIC
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# visualize_model() produces a composite figure per metric comprising:
#   - Main panel     : fitted menarche age smooth with confidence ribbon
#                      and marginal density of the menarche age distribution
#   - Derivative panel: first derivative
# map2() is used (rather than pmap() in the age chunk) as no derivative
# annotation coordinates are passed to the plot here; only the model and
# metric label are iterated over simultaneously.

plots_tibble_onset <- brain_models_timing_output %>%
    mutate(
    plot = map2(
      .x = model, 
      .y = MRI_metric,   
      .f = ~ visualize_model(
        .x, 
        smooth_var = "menarche_age_y",
        group_var = "participant_id",
        derivative_plot = FALSE,
        xlabel = "Menarche Age (years)",
        ylabel = paste(.y),
        plabels = paste(.y), 
        show.data = FALSE,
        side_density = FALSE
      )
    )
  )

plots_onset <- plots_tibble_onset %>%
  pull(plot)

timing <- wrap_plots(plots_onset, ncol = 1)
timing

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Save figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

save_plot('Figures/brain_models_timing_plot.pdf',
          plot = timing,
          base_height = 30, 
          base_width = 5)
```

### Time from Menarche (Onset)
```{r brain measures and onset, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# GAMM: EFFECT OF MENARCHE AGE (TIMING) ON GROSS BRAIN MORPHOMETRY
# =============================================================================
# This chunk models the non-linear association between gynecological age 
# (Time from Menarche) and each of the eight gross brain morphometry metrics, 
# co-varying for age at menarche (timing) and general exposome.
#
# This analysis is structurally identical to the chronological age models.
# The long-format dataset (cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_long) and 
# metric-split list (data_list) are carried forward directly from that chunk; 
# no reshaping is required here.
#
# Note: cache=TRUE is set as parallel GAMM estimation is computationally
# intensive. Rerun with cache=FALSE if model specification or data change.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: DEFINE MODEL-FITTING FUNCTION
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The model specification mirrors the age chunk, with Time_to_from_Menarche_y as the
# primary smooth term.

fit_model <- function(data) {
  gamm(value ~ s(Time_to_from_Menarche_y) +
         s(menarche_age_y) +
         s(General_SES_baseline),
       method = "REML",
       family = gaussian(),
       random = list(participant_id = ~1, ab_g_dyn__design_site = ~1),
       data = data)
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: FIT MODELS IN PARALLEL
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Models are fitted in parallel across the eight metrics using parLapply()
# mgcv is loaded on each worker node explicitly as it is not automatically
# available in the parallel environment.

n_cores <- min(8, detectCores() - 1)  # 8 metrics
cl <- makeCluster(n_cores)
clusterEvalQ(cl, library(mgcv))

brain_models_onset <- parLapply(cl, data_list, fit_model)
stopCluster(cl)

# Organize fitted models into a named tibble for downstream processing
brain_models_onset_output <- tibble(
  MRI_metric = names(brain_models_onset),
  model = brain_models_onset
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: EXTRACT DERIVATIVE TABLES
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# For each model, get_derivative_table() returns the age intervals over which
# the first derivative of the gyncecological age smooth is significantly different from zero,
# indicating periods of significant increase or decrease in each brain metric.

brain_models_onset_output %>%
  mutate(first_derv = map(model, ~get_derivative_table(
    ., smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y"
  ))) %>%
  unnest(first_derv) %>%
  select(-model)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: TIDY MODEL OUTPUT AND EXTRACT FIT STATISTICS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# broom::tidy() extracts smooth term statistics (edf, F, p-value) for each
# metric. N (observations) and R² (adjusted; proportion of variance explained)
# are appended to each row for reporting.

tidy_brain_models_onset_output <- brain_models_onset_output %>%
  mutate(tidy = map(model, function(x) {
    tidydf = broom::tidy(x$gam)
    tidydf$N = length(x$gam$residuals)
    summary_model <- summary(x$gam)
    tidydf$R2 = summary_model$r.sq
    tidydf
  })) %>%
  unnest(tidy) %>%
  select(-model)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 5: EXTRACT SMOOTH ESTIMATES FOR THE GYNCECOLOGICAL AGE TERM
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# smooth_estimates() returns the predicted smooth function and standard error
# at each age value in the data. Only the age smooth is retained here.
# Pointwise 95% confidence intervals are computed as estimate ± 1.96 × SE.

model_smooths_brain_models_onset <- brain_models_onset_output%>%
  mutate(smooths = map(model,smooth_estimates)) %>%
  unnest(smooths) %>%
  select(-model)%>%
  filter(.smooth=="s(Time_to_from_Menarche_y)") %>%
  mutate(upper=.estimate+1.96*.se,lower=.estimate-1.96*.se)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 6: DERIVATIVE-BASED ANALYSIS FOR EACH METRIC
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# derivative_stats() computes simultaneous confidence intervals for the first
# and second derivatives of the age smooth per metric, identifying:
#   - Periods of significant change (first derivative ≠ 0)
#   - Inflection point: age at which the rate of change is greatest
# Results are joined back to the model output tibble for use in visualization.

derv_brain_models_onset_output <- brain_models_onset_output%>%
  mutate(derv_stats = map(model,~derivative_stats(
    ., smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y", make_plots = TRUE
  ))) %>%
  unnest(derv_stats) %>%
  select(-model)

# Append derivative statistics to the main model output tibble
brain_models_onset_output <- brain_models_onset_output %>%
  left_join(derv_brain_models_onset_output, by = "MRI_metric")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 9: VISUALIZE GYNCECOLOGICAL AGE EFFECTS FOR EACH BRAIN METRIC
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# visualize_model() produces a composite figure per metric comprising:
#   - Main panel   : fitted age smooth with confidence ribbon and marginal
#                    density of the gynecological age distribution
#   - Derivative panel: first derivative, highlighting
#                    periods of significant change
#   - Vertical reference line at age 11.8 years (mean menarche age)
#   - Second derivative inflection point annotated with 95% CI
#     (using sd_min_value here)
# pmap() iterates over the model, metric label, and derivative statistics
# simultaneously to produce one plot per metric.

plots_tibble_onset <- brain_models_onset_output %>%
  mutate(
    plot = pmap(
      list(model, MRI_metric, sd_min_value, sd_min_lower_ci, sd_min_upper_ci),
      function(mod, metric, sd_val, sd_lower, sd_upper) {
        visualize_model(
          mod, 
          smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y",
          group_var = "participant_id",
          derivative_plot = FALSE,
          xlabel = "Time from Menarche (years)",
          ylabel = metric,
          plabels = metric, 
          show.data = FALSE,
          side_density = FALSE,
          v_line = 0,
          second_deriv_x     = sd_val,
          second_deriv_lower = sd_lower,
          second_deriv_upper = sd_upper
        )
      }
    )
  )

plots_onset <- plots_tibble_onset %>%
  pull(plot)

onset_with_point <- wrap_plots(plots_onset, ncol = 1)
onset_with_point

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Save figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

save_plot('Figures/brain_models_onset_with_point_plot.pdf',
          plot = onset_with_point,
          base_height = 30,
          base_width = 5)
```

```{r write brain measures results, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# SAFE RESULTS FROM BRAIN ANALYSES IN TABLES
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: SAFE RESULTS FROM GAMMS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Combine results from all brain models (age, timing, onset)
tidy_brain_results_output <- bind_rows(
  tidy_brain_models_age_output,
  tidy_brain_models_timing_output,
  tidy_brain_models_onset_output) 

## Correct for multiple comparisons using different methods (e.g. FDR, Bonferroni)

tidy_brain_results_output <- tidy_brain_results_output %>%

    p_fdr = p.adjust(p.value, method = "fdr"),

      sprintf("%.3f", sd_max_value), " [",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_max_lower_ci), ";",

    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(model, second_derv_min_CI, second_derv_max_CI)

## Write out results
write.csv(
  second_derv_output_brain,
  file = "Results/second_derv_output_brain.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
