# Broken stick analyses + CBCL
```{r Broken stick analyses, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# BROKEN STICK (PIECEWISE LINEAR) ANALYSES
# =============================================================================
# This section implements a two-stage broken stick approach to test whether
# the rate of post-menarcheal brain change (brain velocity) predicts
# internalizing symptoms, over and above pubertal timing and SES.
#
# The rationale for a broken stick model is that brain development may follow
# qualitatively different trajectories before and after menarche. A standard
# linear or smooth term cannot capture this discontinuity. The broken stick
# approach fits separate pre- and post-menarcheal slopes by introducing a
# "hinge" variable (time_post_0) that is zero before menarche and equals
# time from menarche after — allowing the trajectory to bend at menarche onset.
#
# The analysis proceeds in two stages:
#
#   STAGE 1 — BRAIN MODEL (lmer): A piecewise linear mixed-effects model is
#   fitted to each brain metric to extract individual-level post-menarcheal
#   brain change rates (brain velocity). Menarche age is included as a fixed
#   effect to ensure velocity estimates are not confounded by whether a
#   participant was an early or late maturer.
#
#   STAGE 2 — RISK MODEL (GAMM): The individual brain velocity estimates from
#   Stage 1 are entered as a predictor of internalizing symptoms in a GAMM,
#   along with a tensor product interaction with time from menarche. This tests
#   whether faster or slower post-menarcheal brain change predicts symptoms
#   independently of chronological age and pubertal timing.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STAGE 1, STEP 1: FEATURE ENGINEERING — CREATE THE BROKEN STICK VARIABLE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# time_post_0 is the "hinge" variable encoding post-menarcheal time:
#   - Before menarche (Time_to_from_Menarche_y < 0): time_post_0 = 0
#   - After menarche  (Time_to_from_Menarche_y ≥ 0): time_post_0 = time from menarche
# This allows the model to fit one slope before menarche and a different
# (additive) slope after, with the change point fixed at menarche onset.


df_clean <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_long %>%
  mutate(
    # 1. Create the Spline Basis for the "Broken Stick"
    # This is 0 before menarche, and equals time_from_menarche after.
    time_post_0 = ifelse(Time_to_from_Menarche_y >= 0, Time_to_from_Menarche_y, 0),
    
    # 2. Ensure Age at Menarche is constant per subject (just a sanity check)
    # This is your critical control for "Chronological Age"
    menarche_age_y = as.numeric(menarche_age_y)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Re-split the cleaned data by metric for parallel model fitting
data_list <- split(df_clean,
                   df_clean$MRI_metric)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STAGE 1, STEP 2: FIT PIECEWISE LINEAR MIXED MODEL PER BRAIN METRIC
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The lmer model decomposes each participant's brain trajectory into:
#   - A pre-menarcheal slope  (Time_to_from_Menarche_y fixed + random effect)
#   - A post-menarcheal slope (time_post_0 fixed + random effect)
# Random slopes for both time variables allow individual variation in the
# rate of change before and after menarche. A random intercept for site
# accounts for site-level differences in scanner or acquisition protocols.
# menarche_age_y is included as a fixed effect to partial out the confound
# between pubertal timing and the brain trajectory estimates.
# bobyqa optimiser is specified to improve convergence stability.

fit_model_broken_stick_lmer <- function(data) {
  lmer(value ~ 
    menarche_age_y +     
    Time_to_from_Menarche_y +  
    time_post_0 +         
    (1 + Time_to_from_Menarche_y | participant_id) +
    (0 + time_post_0 | participant_id) +
    (1 | ab_g_dyn__design_site), 
  data = data,
  control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))
}

# Fit Stage 1 models in parallel across the eight brain metrics
n_cores <- min(8, detectCores() - 1)  
cl <- makeCluster(n_cores)
clusterEvalQ(cl, library(lme4))

# here we can run the analysis for all 8 metrics again
broken_stick_lmer <- parLapply(cl, data_list, fit_model_broken_stick_lmer)
stopCluster(cl)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STAGE 1, STEP 3: EXTRACT INDIVIDUAL-LEVEL BRAIN VELOCITY ESTIMATES
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Post-menarcheal brain velocity for each participant is computed as the sum
# of the population-average (fixed) effects and the individual deviations
# (random effects) for both the pre- and post-menarcheal slope terms.
#
# This gives a participant-level index of how rapidly each individual's brain
# morphometry changed in the post-menarcheal period, over and above the
# average trajectory.

# 1. Extract population-average fixed effects for the two slope terms
betas_df <- map_dfr(
  broken_stick_lmer,
  ~ {
    fe <- fixef(.x)
    tibble(
      beta_time     = fe["Time_to_from_Menarche_y"],
      beta_time_post    = fe["time_post_0"]
    )
  },
  .id = "MRI_metric"
)

# 2. Extract individual random effect deviations from the participant-level grouping
rand_effs_df <- map_dfr(
  broken_stick_lmer,
  ~ {
    re <- ranef(.x, condVar = FALSE)$participant_id %>%
      as.data.frame() %>%
      rownames_to_column("participant_id")

    re
  },
  .id = "MRI_metric"
)

# 3. Compute total post-menarcheal brain velocity per participant:
#    Total post-menarche slope = (avg pre + indiv pre deviation) +
#                                (avg post + indiv post deviation)
#    This captures each participant's overall rate of brain change
#    in the post-menarcheal period.
subject_brain_velocity <- rand_effs_df %>%
  left_join(betas_df, by = "MRI_metric") %>%
  mutate(
    post_menarche_velocity  = (beta_time_post + time_post_0) +
                             (beta_time + Time_to_from_Menarche_y)
  ) %>%
  select(MRI_metric, participant_id, post_menarche_velocity)

# 4. Merge individual brain velocity estimates back into the analysis dataset
df_analysis <- df_clean %>%
  left_join(subject_brain_velocity, by = c("participant_id", "MRI_metric"))

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STAGE 2, STEP 1: FIT GAMM PREDICTING INTERNALIZING SYMPTOMS FROM BRAIN
#                  VELOCITY AND TIME FROM MENARCHE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The Stage 2 GAMM tests whether individual post-menarcheal brain velocity
# predicts internalizing symptoms over and above pubertal stage, timing,
# and SES. The tensor product interaction ti() tests whether the effect of
# brain velocity on symptoms varies as a function of pubertal stage (and
# vice versa). Menarche age is included to ensure results are not attributable
# to pubertal timing differences between participants.

# Re-split df_analysis by metric for Stage 2 parallel fitting

data_list <- split(df_analysis,
                   df_analysis$MRI_metric)

fit_model_broken_stick_gamm <- function(data) {
  gamm(mh_p_cbcl__synd__int_sum ~ 
         s(Time_to_from_Menarche_y) +                         
         s(post_menarche_velocity) +                        
         ti(Time_to_from_Menarche_y, post_menarche_velocity) +
         s(menarche_age_y) +   
         s(General_SES_baseline),
       data = data,
       method = "REML",
       family = nb(),
       random = list(participant_id = ~1, ab_g_dyn__design_site = ~1)
       )
}

# Fit Stage 2 models in parallel
n_cores <- min(8, detectCores() - 1)  
cl <- makeCluster(n_cores)
clusterEvalQ(cl, library(mgcv))

broken_stick_gamm <- parLapply(cl, data_list, fit_model_broken_stick_gamm)
stopCluster(cl)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STAGE 2, STEP 2: TIDY OUTPUT, APPLY MULTIPLE COMPARISON CORRECTION,
#                  AND SAVE RESULTS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Factor levels are set to enforce a consistent metric display order across
# all output tables and figures. FDR and Bonferroni corrections are applied
# across all smooth terms and metrics simultaneously.

desired_order <- c(
  "Whole brain volume",
  "Subcortical volume",
  "Gray matter volume",
  "Cortical thickness",
  "Surface area",
  "White matter volume",
  "Lateral ventricles volume",
  "CSF")

broken_stick_gamm_output <- tibble(
  MRI_metric = names(broken_stick_gamm),
  model = broken_stick_gamm
) %>%
  mutate(MRI_metric = factor(MRI_metric, levels = desired_order)) %>%
  arrange(MRI_metric)

tidy_broken_stick_gamm_output <- broken_stick_gamm_output %>%
  mutate(tidy = map(model, function(x) {
    tidydf = broom::tidy(x$gam)
    tidydf$N = length(x$gam$residuals)
    summary_model <- summary(x$gam)
    tidydf$R2 = summary_model$r.sq
    tidydf
  })) %>%
  unnest(tidy) %>%
  select(-model) %>%
  mutate(
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p.value, method = "fdr"),
    p_bonferroni = p.adjust(p.value, method = "bonferroni")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(p.value, p_fdr, p_bonferroni),
      ~ ifelse(.x == 0, "<.001", formatC(.x, format = "f", digits = 3))
    )
  )

# Save full results table to CSV for reporting
write.csv(
  tidy_broken_stick_gamm_output,
  file = "Results/tidy_broken_stick_gamm_output.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STAGE 2, STEP 3: VISUALIZE RESULTS FOR ALL EIGHT METRICS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# visualize_model() is called with int_var = "post_menarche_velocity" to
# display the interaction between time from menarche and brain velocity.
# quantile_limits = FALSE ensures the full range of the interaction surface
# is shown rather than being clipped to the interquartile range.
# map2() iterates over model and metric label simultaneously.

plots_tibble_onset <- broken_stick_gamm_output %>%
    mutate(
    plot = map2(
      .x = model, 
      .y = MRI_metric,   
      .f = ~ visualize_model(
        .x, 
        smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y",
        group_var = "participant_id",
        int_var = "post_menarche_velocity",
        xlabel = "Time from Menarche (years)",
        ylabel = paste(.y),
        show.data = FALSE,
        quantile_limits = FALSE,
        plabels = paste(.y)
      )
    )
  )

# Arrange all eight metric panels into a single stacked figure
plots_onset <- plots_tibble_onset %>%
  pull(plot)
broken_stick_gamm_plot <- wrap_plots(plots_onset, ncol = 1)
broken_stick_gamm_plot

#save figure
save_plot('Figures/broken_stick_gamm_plot.pdf',
          plot = broken_stick_gamm_plot,
          base_height = 45, 
          base_width = 10)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STAGE 2, STEP 4: PUBLICATION FIGURES FOR SIGNIFICANT METRICS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Individual figures are produced for surface area and gray matter volume,
# the two metrics showing significant interactions in the main analysis.
# Custom colour schemes distinguish high-velocity (blue) from low-velocity
# (pink/purple) brain change trajectories. These are combined into a single
# two-panel figure for journal submission.

# Surface area: interaction of time from menarche × post-menarcheal brain velocity
broken_stick_surface <- visualize_model(broken_stick_gamm$`Surface area`,
                smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y",
                group_var = "participant_id",
                int_var = "post_menarche_velocity",
                xlabel = "Time from Menarche (Years)",
                ylabel = "CBCL Internalizing Symptoms",
                show.data = FALSE,
                quantile_limits = FALSE,
                high_line = "#045a8d",
                high_color = "#d0d1e6",
                low_line = "#980043",
                low_color = "#d4b9da",
                plabels = "Surface area",
                show.legend = TRUE)
broken_stick_surface <- broken_stick_surface +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(2.5,5.5))
broken_stick_surface

# Gray matter volume: same specification with legend shown for the combined figure
broken_stick_gmw <- visualize_model(broken_stick_gamm$`Gray matter volume`,
                smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y",
                group_var = "participant_id",
                int_var = "post_menarche_velocity",
                xlabel = "Time from Menarche (Years)",
                ylabel = "CBCL Internalizing Symptoms",
                show.data = FALSE,
                quantile_limits = FALSE,
                high_line = "#045a8d",
                high_color = "#d0d1e6",
                low_line = "#980043",
                low_color = "#d4b9da",
                plabels = "Gray matter vol.",
                show.legend = TRUE)
broken_stick_gmw <- broken_stick_gmw +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(2.5,5.5))
broken_stick_gmw

# Combine the two panels side by side using patchwork and save
combined_plot <- broken_stick_surface / broken_stick_gmw
combined_plot

save_plot('Figures/broken_stick_significance_plot.pdf',
          plot = combined_plot,
          base_height = 7.5, 
          base_width = 7)
```

# Broken stick analyses + BPM
```{r Broken stick analyses, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# BROKEN STICK (PIECEWISE LINEAR) ANALYSES
# =============================================================================
# This section implements a two-stage broken stick approach to test whether
# the rate of post-menarcheal brain change (brain velocity) predicts
# internalizing symptoms, over and above pubertal timing and SES.
#
# The rationale for a broken stick model is that brain development may follow
# qualitatively different trajectories before and after menarche. A standard
# linear or smooth term cannot capture this discontinuity. The broken stick
# approach fits separate pre- and post-menarcheal slopes by introducing a
# "hinge" variable (time_post_0) that is zero before menarche and equals
# time from menarche after — allowing the trajectory to bend at menarche onset.
#
# The analysis proceeds in two stages:
#
#   STAGE 1 — BRAIN MODEL (lmer): A piecewise linear mixed-effects model is
#   fitted to each brain metric to extract individual-level post-menarcheal
#   brain change rates (brain velocity). Menarche age is included as a fixed
#   effect to ensure velocity estimates are not confounded by whether a
#   participant was an early or late maturer.
#
#   STAGE 2 — RISK MODEL (GAMM): The individual brain velocity estimates from
#   Stage 1 are entered as a predictor of internalizing symptoms in a GAMM,
#   along with a tensor product interaction with time from menarche. This tests
#   whether faster or slower post-menarcheal brain change predicts symptoms
#   independently of chronological age and pubertal timing.
# =============================================================================


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STAGE 2, STEP 1: FIT GAMM PREDICTING INTERNALIZING SYMPTOMS FROM BRAIN
#                  VELOCITY AND TIME FROM MENARCHE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The Stage 2 GAMM tests whether individual post-menarcheal brain velocity
# predicts internalizing symptoms over and above pubertal stage, timing,
# and SES. The tensor product interaction ti() tests whether the effect of
# brain velocity on symptoms varies as a function of pubertal stage (and
# vice versa). Menarche age is included to ensure results are not attributable
# to pubertal timing differences between participants.

# Re-split df_analysis by metric for Stage 2 parallel fitting

data_list <- split(df_analysis,
                   df_analysis$MRI_metric)

fit_model_broken_stick_gamm <- function(data) {
  gamm(mh_y_bpm__int_sum ~ 
         s(Time_to_from_Menarche_y) +                         
         s(post_menarche_velocity) +                        
         ti(Time_to_from_Menarche_y, post_menarche_velocity) +
         s(menarche_age_y) +   
         s(General_SES_baseline),
       data = data,
       method = "REML",
       family = nb(),
       random = list(participant_id = ~1, ab_g_dyn__design_site = ~1)
       )
}

# Fit Stage 2 models in parallel
n_cores <- min(8, detectCores() - 1)  
cl <- makeCluster(n_cores)
clusterEvalQ(cl, library(mgcv))

broken_stick_gamm <- parLapply(cl, data_list, fit_model_broken_stick_gamm)
stopCluster(cl)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STAGE 2, STEP 2: TIDY OUTPUT, APPLY MULTIPLE COMPARISON CORRECTION,
#                  AND SAVE RESULTS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Factor levels are set to enforce a consistent metric display order across
# all output tables and figures. FDR and Bonferroni corrections are applied
# across all smooth terms and metrics simultaneously.

desired_order <- c(
  "Whole brain volume",
  "Subcortical volume",
  "Gray matter volume",
  "Cortical thickness",
  "Surface area",
  "White matter volume",
  "Lateral ventricles volume",
  "CSF")

broken_stick_gamm_output <- tibble(
  MRI_metric = names(broken_stick_gamm),
  model = broken_stick_gamm
) %>%
  mutate(MRI_metric = factor(MRI_metric, levels = desired_order)) %>%
  arrange(MRI_metric)

tidy_broken_stick_gamm_bpm_output <- broken_stick_gamm_output %>%
  mutate(tidy = map(model, function(x) {
    tidydf = broom::tidy(x$gam)
    tidydf$N = length(x$gam$residuals)
    summary_model <- summary(x$gam)
    tidydf$R2 = summary_model$r.sq
    tidydf
  })) %>%
  unnest(tidy) %>%
  select(-model) %>%
  mutate(
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p.value, method = "fdr"),
    p_bonferroni = p.adjust(p.value, method = "bonferroni")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(p.value, p_fdr, p_bonferroni),
      ~ ifelse(.x == 0, "<.001", formatC(.x, format = "f", digits = 3))
    )
  )

# Save full results table to CSV for reporting
write.csv(
  tidy_broken_stick_gamm_bpm_output,
  file = "Results/tidy_broken_stick_gamm_bpm_output.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STAGE 2, STEP 3: VISUALIZE RESULTS FOR ALL EIGHT METRICS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# visualize_model() is called with int_var = "post_menarche_velocity" to
# display the interaction between time from menarche and brain velocity.
# quantile_limits = FALSE ensures the full range of the interaction surface
# is shown rather than being clipped to the interquartile range.
# map2() iterates over model and metric label simultaneously.

plots_tibble_onset <- broken_stick_gamm_output %>%
    mutate(
    plot = map2(
      .x = model, 
      .y = MRI_metric,   
      .f = ~ visualize_model(
        .x, 
        smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y",
        group_var = "participant_id",
        int_var = "post_menarche_velocity",
        xlabel = "Time from Menarche (years)",
        ylabel = paste(.y),
        show.data = FALSE,
        quantile_limits = FALSE,
        plabels = paste(.y)
      )
    )
  )

# Arrange all eight metric panels into a single stacked figure
plots_onset <- plots_tibble_onset %>%
  pull(plot)
broken_stick_gamm_plot <- wrap_plots(plots_onset, ncol = 1)
broken_stick_gamm_plot

#save figure
save_plot('Figures/broken_stick_gamm_bpm_plot.pdf',
          plot = broken_stick_gamm_plot,
          base_height = 45, 
          base_width = 10)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STAGE 2, STEP 4: PUBLICATION FIGURES FOR SIGNIFICANT METRICS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Individual figures are produced for surface area and gray matter volume,
# the two metrics showing significant interactions in the main analysis.
# Custom colour schemes distinguish high-velocity (blue) from low-velocity
# (pink/purple) brain change trajectories. These are combined into a single
# two-panel figure for journal submission.

# Whole brain volume: interaction of time from menarche × post-menarcheal brain velocity
broken_stick_whole <- visualize_model(broken_stick_gamm$`Whole brain volume`,
                smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y",
                group_var = "participant_id",
                int_var = "post_menarche_velocity",
                xlabel = "Time from Menarche (Years)",
                ylabel = "BPM Internalizing Symptoms",
                show.data = FALSE,
                quantile_limits = FALSE,
                high_line = "#045a8d",
                high_color = "#d0d1e6",
                low_line = "#980043",
                low_color = "#d4b9da",
                plabels = "Whole brain vol.",
                show.legend = FALSE)
broken_stick_whole <- broken_stick_whole +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.6,6))
broken_stick_whole

# Subcortical volume: interaction of time from menarche × post-menarcheal brain velocity
broken_stick_subcortical <- visualize_model(broken_stick_gamm$`Subcortical volume`,
                smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y",
                group_var = "participant_id",
                int_var = "post_menarche_velocity",
                xlabel = "Time from Menarche (Years)",
                ylabel = "BPM Internalizing Symptoms",
                show.data = FALSE,
                quantile_limits = FALSE,
                high_line = "#045a8d",
                high_color = "#d0d1e6",
                low_line = "#980043",
                low_color = "#d4b9da",
                plabels = "Subcortical vol.",
                show.legend = TRUE)
broken_stick_subcortical <- broken_stick_subcortical +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.6,6))
broken_stick_subcortical

# Cortical thickness: interaction of time from menarche × post-menarcheal brain velocity
broken_stick_thk <- visualize_model(broken_stick_gamm$`Cortical thickness`,
                smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y",
                group_var = "participant_id",
                int_var = "post_menarche_velocity",
                xlabel = "Time from Menarche (Years)",
                ylabel = "BPM Internalizing Symptoms",
                show.data = FALSE,
                quantile_limits = FALSE,
                high_line = "#045a8d",
                high_color = "#d0d1e6",
                low_line = "#980043",
                low_color = "#d4b9da",
                plabels = "Cortical Thickness",
                show.legend = TRUE)
broken_stick_thk <- broken_stick_thk +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.6,6))
broken_stick_thk

# Cortical thickness: interaction of time from menarche × post-menarcheal brain velocity
broken_stick_wm <- visualize_model(broken_stick_gamm$`White matter volume`,
                smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y",
                group_var = "participant_id",
                int_var = "post_menarche_velocity",
                xlabel = "Time from Menarche (Years)",
                ylabel = "BPM Internalizing Symptoms",
                show.data = FALSE,
                quantile_limits = FALSE,
                high_line = "#045a8d",
                high_color = "#d0d1e6",
                low_line = "#980043",
                low_color = "#d4b9da",
                plabels = "White matter volume.",
                show.legend = TRUE)
broken_stick_wm <-  broken_stick_wm +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.6,6))
broken_stick_wm

# Combine the two panels side by side using patchwork and save
combined_plot <- broken_stick_whole / broken_stick_subcortical / broken_stick_thk / broken_stick_wm
combined_plot

save_plot('Figures/broken_stick_significance_bpm_plot.pdf',
```

# Sensitivity analyses
```{r Sensitivity analyses - into, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# SENSITIVITY ANALYSES
# =============================================================================
# This section contains four sets of sensitivity analyses designed to test the
# robustness of the main findings:
#
#   1. INTERACTION MODELS: Main models extended with all pairwise tensor product
#      interactions among time from menarche, menarche age, and General SES,
#      for both internalizing symptoms and brain metrics.
#
#   2. ABCD-ARMS REPLICATION: Main models replicated within the two matched
#      maturation timing groups from the ABCD-ARMS dataset (early-maturing vs.
#      on-time), providing an independent replication sample with controlled
#      pubertal timing.
#
#   3. ALTERNATIVE PUBERTY MARKERS (YOUTH REPORT): Main models replicated using time from
#      onset of four alternative pubertal markers (growth spurt, breast
#      budding, body hair, skin changes) in place of time from menarche,
#      testing whether findings generalize across pubertal indicators.
#
#   4. SIBLING EXCLUSION: Main models replicated in a dataset restricted to
#      one randomly selected participant per family, to rule out bias from
#      family-level clustering of pubertal timing and brain development.
#
#   5. BPM REPLICATION: Main internalizing symptom model replicated using
#      youth-reported Brief Problem Monitor (BPM) internalizing score in
#      place of parent-reported CBCL, testing reporter-bias.
#
#   6. GYNECOLOCIGAL AGE AND ALTERNATIVE PUBERTY MARKERS (PARENT REPORT): 
#      Main models replicated using time from onset of four gynecological
#      and alternative pubertal markers (growth spurt, breast
#      budding, body hair, skin changes) based on parent report, testing
#      reporter-bias.
# =============================================================================

```

```{r Sensitivity analyses - with interaction terms int symptoms, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# SENSITIVITY 1A: INTERACTION MODELS — CBCL INTERNALIZING SYMPTOMS
# =============================================================================
# The main internalizing symptoms model is extended to include all pairwise
# tensor product interactions among the three primary predictors:
#   - ti(Time_to_from_Menarche_y, General_SES_baseline): tests whether the
#     association between gynecological age and symptoms differs by general exposome
#   - ti(menarche_age_y, General_SES_baseline): tests whether the effect of
#     gynecological age on symptoms differs by general exposome
#   - ti(Time_to_from_Menarche_y, menarche_age_y): tests whether the
#     trajectory of symptoms across gynecological age differs by timing (i.e.,
#     whether early maturers show a different symptom profile over time)
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

                              s(menarche_age_y) +
                              s(General_SES_baseline) +

                              ti(menarche_age_y, General_SES_baseline) +
                              ti(Time_to_from_Menarche_y, menarche_age_y),
```

### Brain Measures
```{r Sensitivity analyses - with interaction terms brain, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# SENSITIVITY 1B: INTERACTION MODELS — BRAIN MORPHOMETRY METRICS
# =============================================================================
# The same interaction model structure is applied to each of the eight gross
# brain morphometry metrics in parallel, with gaussian family (continuous
# outcomes).
# The data_list object from the brain_measures_and_age chunk is reused.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: FIT INTERACTION MODELS IN PARALLEL
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

data_list <- split(cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_long,
                   cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_long$MRI_metric)

fit_model <- function(data) {
  gamm(value ~
         s(Time_to_from_Menarche_y) +
         s(menarche_age_y) +
         s(General_SES_baseline) +
         ti(Time_to_from_Menarche_y, General_SES_baseline) +
         ti(menarche_age_y, General_SES_baseline) +
         ti(Time_to_from_Menarche_y, menarche_age_y),
       method = "REML",
       family = gaussian(),
       random = list(participant_id = ~1, ab_g_dyn__design_site = ~1),
       data = data)
}

# Parallel execution
n_cores <- min(8, detectCores() - 1)  # 8 metrics
cl <- makeCluster(n_cores)
clusterEvalQ(cl, library(mgcv))

brain_models_interaction_raw <- parLapply(cl, data_list, fit_model)
stopCluster(cl)

# Organize models; apply desired metric display order
brain_models_interaction_raw_output <- tibble(
  MRI_metric = names(brain_models_interaction_raw),
  model = brain_models_interaction_raw) %>%
  mutate(MRI_metric = factor(MRI_metric, levels = desired_order)) %>%
  arrange(MRI_metric)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: TIDY OUTPUT, APPLY MULTIPLE COMPARISON CORRECTION, SAVE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

tidy_brain_models_interaction_raw_output <- brain_models_interaction_raw_output %>%
  mutate(tidy = map(model, function(x) {
    tidydf = broom::tidy(x$gam)
    tidydf$N = length(x$gam$residuals)
    summary_model <- summary(x$gam)
    tidydf$R2 = summary_model$r.sq
    tidydf
  })) %>%
  unnest(tidy) %>%
  select(-model) %>%
  #group_by(term) %>%
  mutate(
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p.value, method = "fdr"),
    p_bonferroni = p.adjust(p.value, method = "bonferroni")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(p.value, p_fdr, p_bonferroni),
      ~ ifelse(.x == 0, "<.001", formatC(.x, format = "f", digits = 3))
    )
  )

write.csv(
  tidy_brain_models_interaction_raw_output,
  file = "Results/tidy_brain_models_interaction_raw_output.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: VISUALIZE — MAIN EFFECT OF GYNECOLOGCIAL AGE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

    mutate(
    plot = map2(
      .x = model, 
      .y = MRI_metric,   
      .f = ~ visualize_model(
        .x, 
        smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y",
        group_var = "participant_id",
        xlabel = "Gynecological Age \n (Time from Menarche Onset in Years)",
        ylabel = paste(.y),
        show.data = FALSE,
        side_density = FALSE,
        derivative_plot = FALSE,
        plabels = paste(.y)
      )
    )
  )

plots_onset <- plots_tibble_onset %>%
  pull(plot)
onset_on_brain_with_interaction <- wrap_plots(plots_onset, ncol = 1)

# save figure
save_plot('Figures/onset_on_brain_with_interaction.pdf',
          plot = onset_on_brain_with_interaction,
          base_height = 25, 
          base_width = 5)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: VISUALIZE — INTERACTION WITH TIMING (menarche_age_y)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Lines shown at 20th and 80th percentiles of menarche age.

    mutate(

      .y = MRI_metric,

# save figure
```

```{r Sensitivity analyses - ARMS int symptoms, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# SENSITIVITY 2A: ABCD-ARMS REPLICATION — CBCL INTERNALIZING SYMPTOMS
# =============================================================================
# The main internalizing symptoms model is replicated within the two matched
# ABCD-ARMS datasets.
# =============================================================================

# Restrict to ARMS participants (Groups 1 and 2 only)
Arms <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  filter(Matched_groups_baseline == 1 | Matched_groups_baseline == 2)

# Confirm participant counts per ARMS group
Arms %>%
  group_by(Matched_groups_baseline) %>%
  summarise(
    n_participants = n_distinct(participant_id),
    participant_ids = list(unique(participant_id))
  )

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: FIT MODELS SEPARATELY PER ARMS GROUP IN PARALLEL
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data are split by ARMS group and the same GAMM is fitted independently to 
# each group.

data_list_ARMS <- split(Arms,
                        Arms$Matched_groups_baseline)

# Function to fit model
fit_model <- function(data) {
  gamm(mh_p_cbcl__synd__int_sum ~ s(Time_to_from_Menarche_y) +
         s(menarche_age_y) +
         s(General_SES_baseline),
       method = "REML",
       family = nb(),
       random = list(participant_id = ~1, ab_g_dyn__design_site = ~1),
       data = data)
}

# Parallel execution
n_cores <- min(2, detectCores() - 1)  # 2 groups
cl <- makeCluster(n_cores)
clusterEvalQ(cl, library(mgcv))

Arms_internalizing_models <- parLapply(cl, data_list_ARMS, fit_model)
stopCluster(cl)

# Convert to tibble format
Arms_internalizing_models_output <- tibble(
  ARM = names(Arms_internalizing_models),
  model = Arms_internalizing_models
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: TIDY OUTPUT, APPLY CORRECTIONS, SAVE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

tidy_Arms_internalizing_models_output <- Arms_internalizing_models_output %>%
  mutate(tidy = map(model, function(x) {
    tidydf = broom::tidy(x$gam)
    tidydf$N = length(x$gam$residuals)
    summary_model <- summary(x$gam)
    tidydf$R2 = summary_model$r.sq
    tidydf
  })) %>%
  unnest(tidy) %>%
  select(-model) %>%
  mutate(
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p.value, method = "fdr"),
    p_bonferroni = p.adjust(p.value, method = "bonferroni")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(p.value, p_fdr, p_bonferroni),
      ~ ifelse(.x == 0, "<.001", formatC(.x, format = "f", digits = 3))
    )
  )

write.csv(
  tidy_Arms_internalizing_models_output,
  file = "Results/tidy_Arms_internalizing_models_output.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: EXTRACT AND FORMAT SECOND DERIVATIVE STATISTICS PER GROUP
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Derivative statistics are extracted for each ARMS group and then separated
# so that Group 1 and Group 2 inflection points can be passed individually
# to visualize_model().

second_derv_Arms_internalizing_models_output <- Arms_internalizing_models_output%>%
  mutate(derv_stats = map(model,~derivative_stats(
    ., smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y", make_plots = TRUE
  ))) %>%
  unnest(derv_stats) %>%
  select(-model)

# Separate derivative stats by ARMS group for individual plot annotation
second_derv_Arms_internalizing_models_output_Arm1 <- second_derv_Arms_internalizing_models_output %>%
  filter(ARM ==1)

second_derv_Arms_internalizing_models_output_Arm2 <- second_derv_Arms_internalizing_models_output %>%
  filter(ARM ==2)

# Format inflection point estimates with 95% CIs as strings for reporting
second_derv_Arms_internalizing_models_output <- second_derv_Arms_internalizing_models_output %>%
  dplyr::select(ARM, sd_min_value, sd_min_lower_ci, sd_min_upper_ci, sd_max_value, sd_max_lower_ci, sd_max_upper_ci) %>%
  mutate(
    second_derv_min_CI = paste0(
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_min_value), " [",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_min_lower_ci), ";",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_min_upper_ci), "]"
    ),
    second_derv_max_CI = paste0(
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_max_value), " [",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_max_lower_ci), ";",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_max_upper_ci), "]"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(ARM, second_derv_min_CI, second_derv_max_CI)

write.csv(
  second_derv_Arms_internalizing_models_output,
  file = "Results/second_derv_Arms_internalizing_models_output.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: VISUALIZE PER ARMS GROUP
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Separate figures are produced for AMR 1 and ARM 2
# A reference line at 0 marks menarche onset. The second derivative
# maximum (accelerating increase in symptoms) is annotated with its 95% CI.

Arm1_inter_plot <- visualize_model(
        Arms_internalizing_models_output$model[[1]], 
        smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y",
        group_var = "participant_id",
        show.data = FALSE,
        derivative_plot = FALSE,
        xlabel = "Gynecological Age \n (Time from Menarche Onset in Years)",
        ylabel = "CBCL Internalizing Symptoms",
        side_density = FALSE,
        v_line = 0,
        second_deriv_x = second_derv_Arms_internalizing_models_output_Arm1$sd_max_value,
        second_deriv_lower = second_derv_Arms_internalizing_models_output_Arm1$sd_max_lower_ci,
        second_deriv_upper = second_derv_Arms_internalizing_models_output_Arm1$sd_max_upper_ci)
Arm1_inter_plot <- Arm1_inter_plot +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(2.5,5.5)) +
  labs(title = "Parent report")
Arm1_inter_plot

Arm2_inter_plot <- visualize_model(
        Arms_internalizing_models_output$model[[2]], 
        smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y",
        group_var = "participant_id",
        show.data = FALSE,
        derivative_plot = FALSE,
        xlabel = "Gynecological Age \n (Time from Menarche Onset in Years)",
        ylabel = "CBCL Internalizing Symptoms",
        side_density = FALSE,
        v_line = 0,
        second_deriv_x = second_derv_Arms_internalizing_models_output_Arm2$sd_max_value,
        second_deriv_lower = second_derv_Arms_internalizing_models_output_Arm2$sd_max_lower_ci,
        second_deriv_upper = second_derv_Arms_internalizing_models_output_Arm2$sd_max_upper_ci)
Arm2_inter_plot <- Arm2_inter_plot +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(2.5,5.5)) +
  labs(title = "Parent report")
Arm2_inter_plot

#save figures
save_plot('Figures/Arm1_inter_plot.pdf',
          plot = Arm1_inter_plot,base_height = 5, 
          base_width = 7)

save_plot('Figures/Arm2_inter_plot.pdf',
          plot = Arm2_inter_plot,base_height = 5,
```

### Brain measures
```{r Sensitivity analyses - ARMS brain, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# SENSITIVITY 2B: ABCD-ARMS REPLICATION — BRAIN MORPHOMETRY METRICS
# =============================================================================
# The main brain morphometry models are replicated within each ARMS group.
# Data are split by the crossing of MRI metric × ARMS group, yielding 16
# subsets (8 metrics × 2 groups), fitted in parallel.
# =============================================================================

# Restrict long-format brain data to ARMS participants
Arms_brain <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_long %>%
  filter(Matched_groups_baseline == 1 | Matched_groups_baseline == 2)

# Split by metric × ARMS group crossing (16 subsets: 8 metrics × 2 groups)
data_list_brain_ARMS <- split(Arms_brain,
                                  ~ Arms_brain$MRI_metric +
                                    Arms_brain$Matched_groups_baseline)

# Function to fit model
fit_model <- function(data) {
  gamm(value ~ s(Time_to_from_Menarche_y) +
         s(menarche_age_y) +
         s(General_SES_baseline),
       method = "REML",
       family = gaussian(),
       random = list(participant_id = ~1, ab_g_dyn__design_site = ~1),
       data = data)
}

# Parallel execution
n_cores <- min(16, detectCores() - 1)
cl <- makeCluster(n_cores)
clusterEvalQ(cl, library(mgcv))

Arms_brain_models <- parLapply(cl, data_list_brain_ARMS, fit_model)
stopCluster(cl)

# Convert to tibble format
Arms_brain_models_output <- tibble(
  ARM = names(Arms_brain_models),
  model = Arms_brain_models
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: TIDY OUTPUT AND PARSE COMBINED ARM IDENTIFIER
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

tidy_Arms_brain_models_output <- Arms_brain_models_output %>%
  mutate(tidy = map(model, function(x) {
    tidydf = broom::tidy(x$gam)
    tidydf$N = length(x$gam$residuals)
    summary_model <- summary(x$gam)
    tidydf$R2 = summary_model$r.sq
    tidydf
  })) %>%
  unnest(tidy) %>%
  select(-model) %>%
  separate(
    col = ARM,
    into = c("MRI_metric", "Arms"),
    sep = "\\.",
    extra = "merge"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p.value, method = "fdr"),
    p_bonferroni = p.adjust(p.value, method = "bonferroni")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(p.value, p_fdr, p_bonferroni),
      ~ ifelse(.x == 0, "<.001", formatC(.x, format = "f", digits = 3))
    )
  )

write.csv(
  tidy_Arms_brain_models_output,
  file = "Results/tidy_Arms_brain_models_output.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: EXTRACT DERIVATIVE STATISTICS AND JOIN TO MODEL OUTPUT
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

second_derv_Arms_brain_models_output <- Arms_brain_models_output%>%
  mutate(derv_stats = map(model,~derivative_stats(
    ., smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y", make_plots = TRUE
  ))) %>%
  unnest(derv_stats) %>%
  select(-model)

# Parse ARM identifier in derivative output to enable joining
second_derv_Arms_brain_models_output <- second_derv_Arms_brain_models_output %>%
  separate(
    col = ARM,
    into = c("MRI_metric", "Arms"),
    sep = "\\.",
    extra = "merge",
    remove = FALSE  # Keep original ARM column too
  )

# Parse ARM identifier in model output tibble (retain original for joining)
Arms_brain_models_output <- Arms_brain_models_output %>%
  separate(
    col = ARM,
    into = c("MRI_metric", "Arms"),
    sep = "\\.",
    extra = "merge",
    remove = FALSE
  )

# Join derivative statistics to model output
Arms_brain_models_output <- Arms_brain_models_output %>%
  left_join(second_derv_Arms_brain_models_output, by = c("ARM", "MRI_metric", "Arms"))


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: VISUALIZE PER ARMS GROUP
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Separate stacked figures are produced for Group 1 and Group 2.
# pmap() is used to iterate over model, metric, group, and derivative
# Figures are combined side-by-side for easy comparison across groups.

plots_tibble_arms <- Arms_brain_models_output %>%
  filter(Arms == "1") %>%
  mutate(
    plot = pmap(
      list(model, MRI_metric, Arms, sd_min_value, sd_min_lower_ci, sd_min_upper_ci),
      function(mod, metric, arm, sd_val, sd_lower, sd_upper) {
        visualize_model(
          mod,
```

## Alternative puberty markers - youth reported
### CBCL Internalizing symptoms
```{r Sensitivity analyses - other growth variables - inter, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# SENSITIVITY 3A: ALTERNATIVE PUBERTY MARKERS — CBCL INTERNALIZING SYMPTOMS
# =============================================================================
# The internalizing symptoms model is replicated using time from onset of four
# alternative pubertal markers in place of time from menarche:
#   - Growth spurt onset
#   - Breast budding onset
#   - Body hair onset
#   - Skin change onset
# This tests whether associations with internalizing symptoms are specific to
# menarche or generalize across other pubertal indicators. Models are fitted in
# parallel across the four markers.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: RESHAPE TO LONG FORMAT
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The four time-from-onset variables are pivoted to long format so that the
# same model can be fitted to each marker via a split-apply workflow.

cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_puberty_marker <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c("Time_to_from_growth_spurt_onset",
                        "Time_to_from_breast_budding_onset",
                        "Time_to_from_body_hair_onset",
                        "Time_to_from_skin_changes_onset"),
               names_to = "Puberty_marker",
               values_to = "Time_from_puberty_marker") %>%
  mutate(Puberty_marker = factor(Puberty_marker,
                             levels = c("Time_to_from_growth_spurt_onset",
                                        "Time_to_from_breast_budding_onset",
                                        "Time_to_from_body_hair_onset",
                                        "Time_to_from_skin_changes_onset"),
                             labels = c("Time from Growth Spurt Onset (Years)",
                                        "Time from Breast Budding Onset (Years)",
                                        "Time from Body Hair Onset (Years)",
                                        "Time from Skin Change Onset (Years)")))

data_list_puberty_marker <- split(cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_puberty_marker,
                                  cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_puberty_marker$Puberty_marker)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: FIT MODELS IN PARALLEL ACROSS FOUR MARKERS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

fit_model_puberty_marker <- function(data) {
  gamm(mh_p_cbcl__synd__int_sum ~ s(Time_from_puberty_marker) +
         s(menarche_age_y) +
         s(General_SES_baseline),
       method = "REML",
       family = nb(),
       random = list(participant_id = ~1, ab_g_dyn__design_site = ~1),
       data = data)
}

# Parallel execution
n_cores <- min(4, detectCores() - 1)  # 4 markers
cl <- makeCluster(n_cores)
clusterEvalQ(cl, library(mgcv))

internalizing_models_puberty_marker <- parLapply(cl, data_list_puberty_marker, fit_model_puberty_marker)
stopCluster(cl)

# Convert to tibble format
internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output <- tibble(
  MARKER = names(internalizing_models_puberty_marker),
  model = internalizing_models_puberty_marker
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: TIDY OUTPUT, APPLY MULTIPLE CORRECTIONS, SAVE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

tidy_internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output <- internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output %>%
  mutate(tidy = map(model, function(x) {
    tidydf = broom::tidy(x$gam)
    tidydf$N = length(x$gam$residuals)
    summary_model <- summary(x$gam)
    tidydf$R2 = summary_model$r.sq
    tidydf
  })) %>%
  unnest(tidy) %>%
  select(-model) %>%
  mutate(
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p.value, method = "fdr"),
    p_bonferroni = p.adjust(p.value, method = "bonferroni")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(p.value, p_fdr, p_bonferroni),
      ~ ifelse(.x == 0, "<.001", formatC(.x, format = "f", digits = 3))
    )
  )

write.csv(
  tidy_internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output,
  file = "Results/tidy_internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output.csv",
  row.names = FALSE)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: EXTRACT DERIVATIVE STATISTICS AND JOIN TO MODEL OUTPUT
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

second_derv_internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output <- internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output%>%
  mutate(derv_stats = map(model,~derivative_stats(
    ., smooth_var = "Time_from_puberty_marker", make_plots = TRUE
  ))) %>%
  unnest(derv_stats) %>%
  select(-model)

internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output <- internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output %>%
  left_join(second_derv_internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output, by = c("MARKER"))

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 5: VISUALIZE AND SAVE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# pmap() iterates over model, marker label, and second derivative max
# annotation coordinates. Reference line at 0 marks marker onset.

plots_tibble_puberty_markers <- internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output %>%
  mutate(
    plot = pmap(
      list(model, MARKER, sd_max_value, sd_max_lower_ci, sd_max_upper_ci),
      function(mod, marker, sd_val, sd_lower, sd_upper) {
        visualize_model(
          mod, 
          smooth_var = "Time_from_puberty_marker",
          group_var = "participant_id",
          derivative_plot = TRUE,
          xlabel = "Time from Puberty Marker (Years)",
          ylabel = "CBCL Internalizing Symptoms",
          plabels = paste(marker),
          show.data = FALSE,
          side_density = TRUE,
          v_line = 0,
          second_deriv_x     = sd_val,
          second_deriv_lower = sd_lower,
          second_deriv_upper = sd_upper
        )
      }
    )
  )

plots_onset <- plots_tibble_puberty_markers %>%
  pull(plot)

Puberty_markers_inter_plots <- wrap_plots(plots_onset, ncol = 1)
Puberty_markers_inter_plots

#save figure
save_plot('Figures/Puberty_markers_inter_with_point_plots.pdf',
          plot = Puberty_markers_inter_plots,
          base_height = 20, 
          base_width = 7)

# Format and save second derivative table
second_derv_internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output_clean <- second_derv_internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output %>%
  dplyr::select(MARKER, sd_min_value, sd_min_lower_ci, sd_min_upper_ci, sd_max_value, sd_max_lower_ci, sd_max_upper_ci) %>%
  mutate(
    second_derv_min_CI = paste0(
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_min_value), " [",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_min_lower_ci), ";",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_min_upper_ci), "]"
    ),
    second_derv_max_CI = paste0(
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_max_value), " [",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_max_lower_ci), ";",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_max_upper_ci), "]"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(MARKER, second_derv_min_CI, second_derv_max_CI)

write.csv(
  second_derv_internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output_clean,
  file = "Results/second_derv_internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output.csv",
  row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r Sensitivity analyses - other growth variables - brain, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_min_lower_ci), ";",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_min_upper_ci), "]"
    ),
    second_derv_max_CI = paste0(
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_max_value), " [",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_max_lower_ci), ";",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_max_upper_ci), "]"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(MARKER, second_derv_min_CI, second_derv_max_CI) %>%
  separate(
    col = MARKER,
    into = c("MRI_metric", "Puberty_marker"),
    sep = "\\.",
    extra = "merge"
  )

write.csv(
  second_derv_brain_model_output_puberty_marker_clean,
  file = "Results/second_derv_brain_model_output_puberty_marker.csv",
  row.names = FALSE)
```

#### Extended Data Figure
```{r Sensitivity analyses - other growth variables - figures, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# SENSITIVITY 3C: EXTENDED DATA FIGURE — SECOND DERIVATIVE INFLECTION POINTS
#                 ACROSS ALL PUBERTY MARKERS AND OUTCOMES
# =============================================================================
# A summary figure is assembled showing the second derivative minimum and
# maximum inflection points (with 95% CIs) for each puberty marker (including menarche)
# across all outcomes (internalizing symptoms + 8 brain metrics). This provides a
# compact cross-marker comparison of when associations accelerate and decelerate
# relative to each pubertal event.
# =============================================================================

# Compile second derivative statistics from all marker-outcome combinations
# into a single long-format table for plotting

# Tag each source dataframe with Metric and MARKER labels before combining
puberty_figure_table <- second_derv_internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output %>%
  mutate(Metric = "CBCL Internalizing Symptoms")

onset_on_inter_dervs <- onset_on_inter_dervs %>%
  mutate(Metric = "CBCL Internalizing Symptoms",
         MARKER = "Menarche Onset")

second_derv_bpm_models_puberty_marker_output <- second_derv_bpm_models_puberty_marker_output %>%
  mutate(Metric = "BPM Internalizing Symptoms")

onset_on_inter_bpm_dervs <- onset_on_inter_bpm_dervs %>%
  mutate(Metric = "BPM Internalizing Symptoms",
         MARKER = "Menarche Onset")

derv_brain_models_onset_output <- derv_brain_models_onset_output %>%
  mutate(Metric = MRI_metric,
         MARKER = "Menarche Onset")

second_derv_brain_model_output_puberty_marker <- second_derv_brain_model_output_puberty_marker %>%
  mutate(Metric = MRI_metric,
         MARKER = Puberty_marker)

# Combine all derivative statistics using full_join to retain all rows
puberty_figure_table <- puberty_figure_table %>%
  full_join(second_derv_bpm_models_puberty_marker_output) %>%
  full_join(second_derv_brain_model_output_puberty_marker) %>%
  full_join(onset_on_inter_dervs) %>%
  full_join(onset_on_inter_bpm_dervs) %>%
  full_join(derv_brain_models_onset_output)

# Set factor levels for consistent display order across both panels
desired_order <- c(
  "CBCL Internalizing Symptoms",
  "BPM Internalizing Symptoms",
  "Whole brain volume",
  "Subcortical volume",
  "Gray matter volume",
  "Cortical thickness",
  "Surface area",
  "White matter volume",
  "Lateral ventricles volume",
  "CSF")

puberty_figure_table <- puberty_figure_table %>%
  mutate(Metric = factor(Metric, levels = desired_order))

# Recode MARKER labels for concise display on the y-axis
puberty_figure_table <- puberty_figure_table %>%
  mutate(MARKER = factor(MARKER,
                         levels = c("Time from Growth Spurt Onset (Years)",
                                    "Time from Breast Budding Onset (Years)",
                                    "Time from Body Hair Onset (Years)",
                                    "Time from Skin Change Onset (Years)",
                                    "Menarche Onset"),
                         labels = c("Growth Spurt Onset",
                                    "Breast Budding Onset",
                                    "Body Hair Onset",
                                    "Skin Change Onset",
                                    "Menarche Onset")))

# Left panel: second derivative minimum inflection points
second_derv_inter_min <- ggplot(puberty_figure_table, aes(y = MARKER)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray90") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(
      xmin = sd_min_lower_ci,
      xmax = sd_min_upper_ci),
    height = 0.2,
    color = "gray40",
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_point(aes(x = sd_min_value),
             shape = 21,
             size = 4,
             colour = "black",
             fill = "gray80") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-5, 10)) +
  labs(
    title = "Second derivative min + CI",
    x = "Time from Marker Onset in Years",
    y = "") +
  facet_wrap(~Metric, ncol = 1)

# Right panel: second derivative maximum inflection points
puberty_figure_table <- puberty_figure_table %>%
  mutate(
    plot_value = if_else(MARKER == "Body Hair Onset" & Metric == "BPM Internalizing Symptoms", sd_max_median, sd_max_value)
  )

second_derv_inter_max <- ggplot(puberty_figure_table, aes(y = MARKER)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray90") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(
      xmin = sd_max_lower_ci,
      xmax = sd_max_upper_ci),

    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_point(aes(x = plot_value),
             shape = 21,
             size = 4,
             colour = "black",
             fill = "gray80") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-5, 10)) +
  labs(
    title = "Second derivative max + CI",
    x = "Time from Marker Onset in Years",
    y = "") +
  facet_wrap(~Metric, ncol = 1)
```

## Siblings settings
### Make dataframe
```{r family, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# SENSITIVITY 4: SIBLING EXCLUSION — ONE PARTICIPANT PER FAMILY
# =============================================================================
# The ABCD Study includes sibling pairs, which may introduce non-independence
# in e.g. brain morphometry due to shared genetic and environmental factors. 
# This sensitivity analysis restricts the sample to one randomly selected 
# participant per family (identified by ab_g_stc__design_id__fam), replicating 
# the main models in this sibling-excluded subset.
# set.seed(123) ensures the random selection is reproducible.
# =============================================================================

set.seed(123) # set seed for reproducible random sibling selection

# CBCL and Brain dataframe
# Step 1: Randomly select one participant per family
selected_sibling <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  distinct(ab_g_stc__design_id__fam, participant_id) %>%
  group_by(ab_g_stc__design_id__fam) %>%
  slice_sample(n = 1) %>%
  ungroup()

# Step 2: Retain all waves for selected participants only
df_no_siblings <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  filter(participant_id %in% selected_sibling$participant_id)

# BPM dataframe
# Step 1: Randomly select one participant per family
selected_sibling_bpm <- bpm_dataframe %>%
  distinct(ab_g_stc__design_id__fam, participant_id) %>%
  group_by(ab_g_stc__design_id__fam) %>%
  slice_sample(n = 1) %>%
  ungroup()

# Step 2: Retain all waves for selected participants only
df_no_siblings_bpm <- bpm_dataframe %>%
  filter(participant_id %in% selected_sibling_bpm$participant_id)
```

```{r family - inter symptoms, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================

onset_on_inter_sibling <- mgcv::gamm(mh_p_cbcl__synd__int_sum ~
                              s(Time_to_from_Menarche_y) +
                              s(menarche_age_y) +
                              s(General_SES_baseline),
                              data = df_no_siblings,
                              method = "REML",
                              family = nb(),
                              random = list(participant_id = ~1, ab_g_dyn__design_site = ~1))
  
summary(onset_on_inter_sibling$gam)

tidy_onset_on_inter_sibling_output <- tibble(
  model = "onset_on_inter_sibling",
  tidy  = list(broom::tidy(onset_on_inter_sibling$gam))
) %>%
  unnest(tidy)
tidy_onset_on_inter_sibling_output$N = length(onset_on_inter_sibling$gam$residuals)
summary_model <- summary(onset_on_inter_sibling$gam)
tidy_onset_on_inter_sibling_output$R2 = summary_model$r.sq

tidy_onset_on_inter_sibling_output <- tidy_onset_on_inter_sibling_output %>%
  mutate(
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p.value, method = "fdr"),
    p_bonferroni = p.adjust(p.value, method = "bonferroni")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(p.value, p_fdr, p_bonferroni),
      ~ ifelse(.x == 0, "<.001", formatC(.x, format = "f", digits = 3))
    )
  )

## Write out results
```

### Brain measures
```{r family - brain, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# SENSITIVITY 4B: SIBLING EXCLUSION — BRAIN MORPHOMETRY METRICS
# =============================================================================
# The sibling-excluded dataset is reshaped to long format and the main brain
# morphometry models are replicated in parallel. Reshaping is necessary here
# as df_no_siblings is wide-format; the same factor level ordering and labels
# as the main analysis are applied for consistency.
# =============================================================================

# Reshape sibling-excluded dataset to long format
df_no_siblings_long <- df_no_siblings %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c("mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__whb_sum", 
                        "mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__scgv_sum",
                        "mr_y_smri__vol__dsk_sum",
                        "total_cerebral_WM",
                        "mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__lvs_sum",
                        "mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__csf_sum",
                        "mr_y_smri__thk__dsk_mean",
                        "mr_y_smri__area__dsk_sum"),
               names_to = "MRI_metric",
               values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(MRI_metric = factor(MRI_metric,
                             levels = c("mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__whb_sum", 
                                        "mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__scgv_sum",
                                        "mr_y_smri__vol__dsk_sum",
                                        "mr_y_smri__thk__dsk_mean",
                                        "mr_y_smri__area__dsk_sum",
                                        "total_cerebral_WM",
                                        "mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__lvs_sum",
                                        "mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__csf_sum"),
                             labels = c("Whole brain volume",
                                        "Subcortical volume",
                                        "Gray matter volume",
                                        "Cortical thickness",
                                        "Surface area",
                                        "White matter volume",
                                        "Lateral ventricles volume",
                                        "CSF")))

# Split data by metric
data_list_sibling <- split(df_no_siblings_long,
                   df_no_siblings_long$MRI_metric)

# Function to fit one model
fit_model <- function(data) {
  gamm(value ~ s(Time_to_from_Menarche_y) +
         s(menarche_age_y) +
         s(General_SES_baseline),
       method = "REML",
       family = gaussian(),
       random = list(participant_id = ~1, ab_g_dyn__design_site = ~1),
       data = data)
}

# Parallel execution
n_cores <- min(8, detectCores() - 1)  # 8 metrics
cl <- makeCluster(n_cores)
clusterEvalQ(cl, library(mgcv))

brain_models_onset_sibling <- parLapply(cl, data_list_sibling, fit_model)
stopCluster(cl)

# Convert to tibble format
brain_models_onset_sibling_output <- tibble(
  MRI_metric = names(brain_models_onset_sibling),
  model = brain_models_onset_sibling
)

brain_models_onset_sibling_output %>%
  mutate(first_derv = map(model, ~get_derivative_table(
    ., smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y"
  ))) %>%
  unnest(first_derv) %>%
  select(-model)

tidy_brain_models_onset_sibling_output <- brain_models_onset_sibling_output %>%
  mutate(tidy = map(model, function(x) {
    tidydf = broom::tidy(x$gam)
    tidydf$N = length(x$gam$residuals)
    summary_model <- summary(x$gam)
    tidydf$R2 = summary_model$r.sq
    tidydf
  })) %>%
  unnest(tidy) %>%
  select(-model)

tidy_brain_models_onset_sibling_output <- tidy_brain_models_onset_sibling_output %>%
  mutate(
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p.value, method = "fdr"),
    p_bonferroni = p.adjust(p.value, method = "bonferroni")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(p.value, p_fdr, p_bonferroni),
      ~ ifelse(.x == 0, "<.001", formatC(.x, format = "f", digits = 3))
    )
  )

## Write out results
write.csv(
  tidy_brain_models_onset_sibling_output,
  file = "Results/tidy_brain_models_onset_sibling_output.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

model_smooths_brain_models_onset_sibling <- brain_models_onset_sibling_output%>%
  mutate(smooths = map(model,smooth_estimates)) %>%
  unnest(smooths) %>%
  select(-model)%>%
  filter(.smooth=="s(Time_to_from_Menarche_y)") %>%
  mutate(upper=.estimate+1.96*.se,lower=.estimate-1.96*.se)

derv_brain_models_onset_sibling_output <- brain_models_onset_sibling_output%>%
  mutate(derv_stats = map(model,~derivative_stats(
    ., smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y", make_plots = TRUE
  ))) %>%
  unnest(derv_stats) %>%
  select(-model)

brain_models_onset_sibling_output <- brain_models_onset_sibling_output %>%
  left_join(derv_brain_models_onset_sibling_output, by = "MRI_metric")

# Visualize age effects for top ROIs using partial_resid_plot
plots_tibble_onset <- brain_models_onset_sibling_output %>%
  mutate(
    plot = pmap(
      list(model, MRI_metric, sd_min_value, sd_min_lower_ci, sd_min_upper_ci),
      function(mod, metric, sd_val, sd_lower, sd_upper) {
        visualize_model(
          mod, 
          smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y",
          group_var = "participant_id",
          derivative_plot = TRUE,
          xlabel = "Time from Menarche (years)",
          ylabel = metric,
          plabels = metric, 
          show.data = FALSE,
          side_density = TRUE,
          v_line = 0,
          second_deriv_x     = sd_val,
          second_deriv_lower = sd_lower,
          second_deriv_upper = sd_upper
        )
      }
    )
  )

plots_onset <- plots_tibble_onset %>%
  pull(plot)

onset_with_point <- wrap_plots(plots_onset, ncol = 1)
onset_with_point

#save figure
save_plot('Figures/brain_models_onset_with_point_sibling_plot.pdf',
          plot = onset_with_point,
          base_height = 30, 
          base_width = 5)

derv_brain_models_onset_sibling_output_clean <- derv_brain_models_onset_sibling_output %>%
  dplyr::select(MRI_metric, sd_min_value, sd_min_lower_ci, sd_min_upper_ci, sd_max_value, sd_max_lower_ci, sd_max_upper_ci) %>%
  mutate(
    second_derv_min_CI = paste0(
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_min_value), " [",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_min_lower_ci), ";",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_min_upper_ci), "]"
    ),
    second_derv_max_CI = paste0(
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_max_value), " [",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_max_lower_ci), ";",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_max_upper_ci), "]"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(MRI_metric, second_derv_min_CI, second_derv_max_CI)

## Write out results
write.csv(
  derv_brain_models_onset_sibling_output_clean,
  file = "Results/derv_brain_models_onset_sibling_output_clean.csv",
  row.names = FALSE)
```

## BMI as covarite
### CBCL Internalizing symptoms
```{r Int symptoms and onset with BMI, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# GAMM: EFFECT OF GYNECOLOGICAL AGE ON CBCL INTERNALIZING SYMPTOMS
# =============================================================================
# This chunk models the non-linear trajectory of parent-reported internalizing
# symptoms (CBCL internalizing sum score) as a function of gynecological age 
# (Time from Menarche) across the study period, co-varying for menarche age
# (menarche timing), general exposome, and BMI.
#
# Model specification:
#   - Outcome  : CBCL internalizing symptoms sum score (mh_p_cbcl__synd__int_sum)
#                modeled with a negative binomial family to account for the
#                overdispersed count distribution of symptom sum scores.
#   - Smooths  : Smooth functions for gynecological age, menarche timing,
#                general exposome, and BMI (entered as smooth terms via s()), 
#                allowing non-linear trajectories to be estimated from the data.
#   - Random effects: Random intercepts for participant (to account for
#                repeated measures) and site (to account for
#                site-level clustering), specified via the random argument.
#   - Estimation: REML, for unbiased smoothing parameter and variance
#                component estimation.
#
# Following model fitting, derivative-based analyses identify periods of
# significant change in the internalizing symptom trajectory, and a
# composite visualization is produced.
# Results are tidied and annotated with N and R² for reporting.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: FIT GAMM
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

onset_on_inter_bmi <- mgcv::gamm(mh_p_cbcl__synd__int_sum ~
                              s(Time_to_from_Menarche_y) +
                              s(menarche_age_y) +
                              s(General_SES_baseline) +
                              s(bmi),
                              data = cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain,
                              method = "REML",
                              family = nb(),
                              random = list(participant_id = ~1, ab_g_dyn__design_site = ~1))
  
summary(onset_on_inter_bmi$gam)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: TIDY MODEL OUTPUT AND EXTRACT FIT STATISTICS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# broom::tidy() extracts smooth term statistics (edf, F, p-value) into a
# dataframe. N (number of observations) and R² (deviance explained) are
# appended for inclusion in a results table.

tidy_onset_on_inter_bmi_output <- tibble(
  model = "onset_on_inter_bmi",
  tidy  = list(broom::tidy(onset_on_inter_bmi$gam))
) %>%
  unnest(tidy)
tidy_onset_on_inter_bmi_output$N = length(onset_on_inter_bmi$gam$residuals)
summary_model <- summary(onset_on_inter_bmi$gam)
tidy_onset_on_inter_bmi_output$R2 = summary_model$r.sq

write.csv(
  tidy_onset_on_inter_bmi_output,
  file = "Results/tidy_onset_on_inter_bmi_output.csv",
  row.names = FALSE)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: DERIVATIVE-BASED ANALYSIS OF THE AGE SMOOTH
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Simultaneous confidence intervals for the first and second derivatives of
# the gynecological age smooth are computed using derivative_stats(). This identifies:
#   - Periods of significant increase or decrease in internalizing symptoms
#     (first derivative significantly different from zero)
#   - The inflection point (maximum of the second derivative), indicating
#     where the rate of change is accelerating most rapidly

onset_on_inter_bmi_dervs <- derivative_stats(
    onset_on_inter_bmi, 
    smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y", 
    make_plots = TRUE
    ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = "onset_on_inter_bmi")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: VISUALIZE MODEL
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# visualize_model() produces a composite figure comprising:
#   - Main panel : fitted age smooth with confidence ribbon 
#   - Derivative panel: first derivative of the age smooth,
#.                      highlighting periods of significant change
#                       (derivative_plot = TRUE)
#   - Vertical reference line at 0 (person-specific menarche onset; v_line = 0)
#   - Second derivative inflection point (maximum) annotated with 95% CI
#                  (sd_max_value, sd_max_lower_ci, sd_max_upper_ci)

onset_on_inter_bmi_plot <- visualize_model(
    onset_on_inter_bmi,
    smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y",
    group_var = "participant_id",
    show.data = FALSE,
    side_density = TRUE,
    derivative_plot = TRUE,
    xlabel = "Time from Menarche (Years)",
    ylabel = "CBCL Internalizing Symptoms",
    second_deriv_x = onset_on_inter_bmi_dervs$sd_max_value,
    second_deriv_lower = onset_on_inter_bmi_dervs$sd_max_lower_ci,
    second_deriv_upper = onset_on_inter_bmi_dervs$sd_max_upper_ci,
    v_line = 0)
onset_on_inter_bmi_plot

# Tabulate periods of significant first-derivative change for reporting
get_derivative_table(onset_on_inter_bmi, smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Save figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

save_plot('Figures/onset_on_inter_bmi_plot.pdf',
          plot = onset_on_inter_bmi_plot,
          base_height = 5, 
          base_width = 7)

onset_on_inter_bmi_dervs_clean <- onset_on_inter_bmi_dervs %>%
  dplyr::select(sd_min_value, sd_min_lower_ci, sd_min_upper_ci, sd_max_value, sd_max_lower_ci, sd_max_upper_ci) %>%
  mutate(
    second_derv_min_CI = paste0(
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_min_value), " [",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_min_lower_ci), ";",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_min_upper_ci), "]"
    ),
    second_derv_max_CI = paste0(
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_max_value), " [",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_max_lower_ci), ";",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_max_upper_ci), "]"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(second_derv_min_CI, second_derv_max_CI)

## Write out results
write.csv(
  onset_on_inter_bmi_dervs_clean,
  file = "Results/onset_on_inter_bmi_dervs_clean.csv",
  row.names = FALSE)
```
