### Brain measures
```{r brain measures and onset, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# GAMM: EFFECT OF MENARCHE AGE (TIMING) ON GROSS BRAIN MORPHOMETRY
# =============================================================================
# This chunk models the non-linear association between gynecological age 
# (Time from Menarche) and each of the eight gross brain morphometry metrics, 
# co-varying for age at menarche (timing) and general exposome.
#
# This analysis is structurally identical to the chronological age models.
# The long-format dataset (cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_long) and 
# metric-split list (data_list) are carried forward directly from that chunk; 
# no reshaping is required here.
#
# Note: cache=TRUE is set as parallel GAMM estimation is computationally
# intensive. Rerun with cache=FALSE if model specification or data change.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: DEFINE MODEL-FITTING FUNCTION
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The model specification mirrors the age chunk, with Time_to_from_Menarche_y as the
# primary smooth term.

fit_model <- function(data) {
  gamm(value ~ s(Time_to_from_Menarche_y) +
         s(menarche_age_y) +
         s(General_SES_baseline) +
         s(bmi),
       method = "REML",
       family = gaussian(),
       random = list(participant_id = ~1, ab_g_dyn__design_site = ~1),
       data = data)
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: FIT MODELS IN PARALLEL
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Models are fitted in parallel across the eight metrics using parLapply()
# mgcv is loaded on each worker node explicitly as it is not automatically
# available in the parallel environment.

n_cores <- min(8, detectCores() - 1)  # 8 metrics
cl <- makeCluster(n_cores)
clusterEvalQ(cl, library(mgcv))

brain_models_onset_bmi <- parLapply(cl, data_list, fit_model)
stopCluster(cl)

# Organize fitted models into a named tibble for downstream processing
brain_models_onset_bmi_output <- tibble(
  MRI_metric = names(brain_models_onset_bmi),
  model = brain_models_onset_bmi
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: EXTRACT DERIVATIVE TABLES
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# For each model, get_derivative_table() returns the age intervals over which
# the first derivative of the gyncecological age smooth is significantly different from zero,
# indicating periods of significant increase or decrease in each brain metric.

brain_models_onset_bmi_output %>%
  mutate(first_derv = map(model, ~get_derivative_table(
    ., smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y"
  ))) %>%
  unnest(first_derv) %>%
  select(-model)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: TIDY MODEL OUTPUT AND EXTRACT FIT STATISTICS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# broom::tidy() extracts smooth term statistics (edf, F, p-value) for each
# metric. N (observations) and R² (adjusted; proportion of variance explained)
# are appended to each row for reporting.

tidy_brain_models_onset_bmi_output <- brain_models_onset_bmi_output %>%
  mutate(tidy = map(model, function(x) {
    tidydf = broom::tidy(x$gam)
    tidydf$N = length(x$gam$residuals)
    summary_model <- summary(x$gam)
    tidydf$R2 = summary_model$r.sq
    tidydf
  })) %>%
  unnest(tidy) %>%
  select(-model)

tidy_brain_models_onset_bmi_output <- tidy_brain_models_onset_bmi_output %>%
  mutate(
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p.value, method = "fdr"),
    p_bonferroni = p.adjust(p.value, method = "bonferroni")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(p.value, p_fdr, p_bonferroni),
      ~ ifelse(.x == 0, "<.001", formatC(.x, format = "f", digits = 3))
    )
  )

## Write out results
write.csv(
  tidy_brain_models_onset_bmi_output,
  file = "Results/tidy_brain_models_onset_bmi_output.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 5: EXTRACT SMOOTH ESTIMATES FOR THE GYNCECOLOGICAL AGE TERM
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# smooth_estimates() returns the predicted smooth function and standard error
# at each age value in the data. Only the age smooth is retained here.
# Pointwise 95% confidence intervals are computed as estimate ± 1.96 × SE.

model_smooths_brain_models_onset_bmi <- brain_models_onset_bmi_output%>%
  mutate(smooths = map(model,smooth_estimates)) %>%
  unnest(smooths) %>%
  select(-model)%>%
  filter(.smooth=="s(Time_to_from_Menarche_y)") %>%
  mutate(upper=.estimate+1.96*.se,lower=.estimate-1.96*.se)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 6: DERIVATIVE-BASED ANALYSIS FOR EACH METRIC
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# derivative_stats() computes simultaneous confidence intervals for the first
# and second derivatives of the age smooth per metric, identifying:
#   - Periods of significant change (first derivative ≠ 0)
#   - Inflection point: age at which the rate of change is greatest
# Results are joined back to the model output tibble for use in visualization.

derv_brain_models_onset_bmi_output <- brain_models_onset_bmi_output%>%
  mutate(derv_stats = map(model,~derivative_stats(
    ., smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y", make_plots = TRUE
  ))) %>%
  unnest(derv_stats) %>%
  select(-model)

# Append derivative statistics to the main model output tibble
brain_models_onset_bmi_output <- brain_models_onset_bmi_output %>%
  left_join(derv_brain_models_onset_bmi_output, by = "MRI_metric")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 9: VISUALIZE GYNCECOLOGICAL AGE EFFECTS FOR EACH BRAIN METRIC
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# visualize_model() produces a composite figure per metric comprising:
#   - Main panel   : fitted age smooth with confidence ribbon and marginal
#                    density of the gynecological age distribution
#   - Derivative panel: first derivative, highlighting
#                    periods of significant change
#   - Vertical reference line at age 11.8 years (mean menarche age)
#   - Second derivative inflection point annotated with 95% CI
#     (using sd_min_value here)
# pmap() iterates over the model, metric label, and derivative statistics
# simultaneously to produce one plot per metric.

plots_tibble_onset <- brain_models_onset_bmi_output %>%
  mutate(
    plot = pmap(
      list(model, MRI_metric, sd_min_value, sd_min_lower_ci, sd_min_upper_ci),
      function(mod, metric, sd_val, sd_lower, sd_upper) {
        visualize_model(
          mod, 
          smooth_var = "Time_to_from_Menarche_y",
          group_var = "participant_id",
          derivative_plot = TRUE,
          xlabel = "Time from Menarche (years)",
          ylabel = metric,
          plabels = metric, 
          show.data = FALSE,
          side_density = TRUE,
          v_line = 0,
          second_deriv_x     = sd_val,
          second_deriv_lower = sd_lower,
          second_deriv_upper = sd_upper
        )
      }
    )
  )

plots_onset <- plots_tibble_onset %>%
  pull(plot)

onset_with_point <- wrap_plots(plots_onset, ncol = 1)
onset_with_point

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Save figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

save_plot('Figures/brain_models_onset_bmi_with_point_plot.pdf',
          plot = onset_with_point,
          base_height = 30,
          base_width = 5)

derv_brain_models_onset_bmi_output_clean <- derv_brain_models_onset_bmi_output %>%
  dplyr::select(MRI_metric, sd_min_value, sd_min_lower_ci, sd_min_upper_ci, sd_max_value, sd_max_lower_ci, sd_max_upper_ci) %>%
  mutate(
    second_derv_min_CI = paste0(
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_min_value), " [",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_min_lower_ci), ";",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_min_upper_ci), "]"
    ),
    second_derv_max_CI = paste0(
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_max_value), " [",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_max_lower_ci), ";",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_max_upper_ci), "]"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(MRI_metric, second_derv_min_CI, second_derv_max_CI)

## Write out results
write.csv(
  derv_brain_models_onset_bmi_output_clean,
  file = "Results/derv_brain_models_onset_bmi_output_clean.csv",
  row.names = FALSE)
```

## Puberty markers - parent reported
```{r create_age_of_menarche_variable parent report, echo=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# SENSITIVITY 6: PARENT-REPORTED PUBERTY MARKERS
# =============================================================================
# This section replicates the youth-reported pubertal marker analyses using
# parent-reported equivalents from the parent PDS (ph_p_pds). Parent and
# youth reports may differ due to informant effects, particularly.
# Using both reporters allows assessment of rater bias.
#
# The section proceeds in five stages:
#   1. Clean parent-reported age at menarche and derive menarche_age_p
#      and Time_to_from_Menarche_p (parallel to the youth-report pipeline)
#   2. Visualize the parent-reported menarche age distribution
#   3. Derive parent-reported onset ages for four alternative puberty markers
#      and compute time-from-onset variables
#   4. Fit parallel GAMMs for internalizing symptoms and brain morphometry
#      using all five parent-reported puberty markers
#   5. Make extended data figure
# =============================================================================
```

### Create Variable "Age of Menrache Onset" from parent report
```{r create_age_of_menarche_variable parent report, echo=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# STAGE 1: CLEAN PARENT-REPORTED AGE AT MENARCHE AND DERIVE TIMING VARIABLES
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: SET AGE AT MENARCHE TO NA FOR NON-MENARCHEAL PARTICIPANTS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# If a parent reported their child has not yet menstruated (ph_p_pds__f_002 == 0),
# but reported a menarche age, the corresponding age at menarche entry is set 
# to NA.

cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  mutate(
    ph_p_pds__f_002__01 = ifelse(ph_p_pds__f_002 == 0, NA, ph_p_pds__f_002__01)
  )

# Inspect distribution of parent-reported menarche ages before cleaning
cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  count(ph_p_pds__f_002__01)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: IDENTIFY AND INSPECT IMPLAUSIBLE VALUES
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The following values were flagged as implausible or erroneous on the basis
# of cross-wave inspection and contextual review:
#
#   3        → NA  (implausibly young; no corroborating entries)
#   99       → NA  (likely missing/refused code entered as age)
#   111      → NA  (no corroborating entries to infer correct value)
#   112      → NA  (no corroborating entries to infer correct value)
#   130      → NA  (no corroborating entries to infer correct value)
#   1200     → NA  (implausible; likely data entry error)
#   2017–2022→ NA  (calendar years entered instead of age)
#   5122022  → NA  (likely full date string entered instead of age: 5/12/2022)
#   8252023  → NA  (likely full date string entered instead of age: 8/25/2023)
#
# Unlike the youth-report cleaning (where some values could be corrected based
# on longitudinal patterns), all parent-report anomalies are set to NA because
# no consistent corrected value could be inferred from cross-wave inspection.

# Extract all sessions for participants with any flagged value for review
tbl_zero_participants_p <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  filter(
    ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 3 | 
    ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 99 | 
    ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 111 | 
    ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 112 | 
    ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 130 | 
    ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 1200 | 
    ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 2017 | 
    ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 2018 | 
    ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 2019 | 
    ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 2020 | 
    ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 2021 | 
    ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 2022 | 
    ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 5122022 | 
    ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 8252023) %>%      
  distinct(participant_id) %>%               
  inner_join(cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain, by = "participant_id") %>%  
  dplyr::select(participant_id, session_id, ph_p_pds__f_002__01, ab_g_dyn__visit_age, ab_g_dyn__visit_dtt) %>%
  arrange(participant_id, session_id) %>%
  as_tibble()  # ensures it's a neat tbl_df
tbl_zero_participants_p

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: APPLY CORRECTIONS — SET ALL FLAGGED VALUES TO NA
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# All flagged values are set to NA as no reliable corrected value could be
# inferred from the longitudinal record (contrast with youth-report cleaning,
# where several values were corrected rather than removed).

cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  mutate(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 = if_else(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 3, NA, ph_p_pds__f_002__01)) %>%
  mutate(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 = if_else(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 99, NA, ph_p_pds__f_002__01)) %>%
  mutate(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 = if_else(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 111, NA, ph_p_pds__f_002__01)) %>%
  mutate(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 = if_else(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 112, NA, ph_p_pds__f_002__01)) %>%
  mutate(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 = if_else(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 130, NA, ph_p_pds__f_002__01)) %>%
  mutate(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 = if_else(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 1200, NA, ph_p_pds__f_002__01)) %>%
  mutate(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 = if_else(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 2017, NA, ph_p_pds__f_002__01)) %>%
  mutate(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 = if_else(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 2018, NA, ph_p_pds__f_002__01)) %>%
  mutate(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 = if_else(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 2019, NA, ph_p_pds__f_002__01)) %>%
  mutate(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 = if_else(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 2020, NA, ph_p_pds__f_002__01)) %>%
  mutate(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 = if_else(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 2021, NA, ph_p_pds__f_002__01)) %>%
  mutate(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 = if_else(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 2022, NA, ph_p_pds__f_002__01)) %>%
  mutate(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 = if_else(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 5122022, NA, ph_p_pds__f_002__01)) %>%
  mutate(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 = if_else(ph_p_pds__f_002__01 == 8252023, NA, ph_p_pds__f_002__01))

# Verify cleaned distribution
cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  count(ph_p_pds__f_002__01)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: IDENTIFY PARTICIPANTS WITH INCONSISTENT CROSS-WAVE REPORTS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Participants reporting different menarche ages across waves are identified.
# Results are pivoted to wide format for visual inspection, consistent with
# the youth-report pipeline.

# Summarise number of distinct non-missing values and list of reported ages
pds_summary_p <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  summarise(
    unique_ph_y_pds = n_distinct(ph_p_pds__f_002__01, na.rm = TRUE),
    ages_list = paste(sort(unique(ph_p_pds__f_002__01[!is.na(ph_p_pds__f_002__01)])), collapse = ", "),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# Flag inconsistent reporters (more than one distinct reported menarche age)
inconsistent_participants_p <- pds_summary_p %>%
  filter(unique_ph_y_pds > 1)

inconsistent_participants_p


# Re-summarise using parent-specific column name for downstream use
pds_summary_p <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  summarise(
    unique_ph_p_pds = n_distinct(ph_p_pds__f_002__01, na.rm = TRUE),
    ages_list = paste(sort(unique(ph_p_pds__f_002__01[!is.na(ph_p_pds__f_002__01)])), collapse = ", "),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# Pivot session-level data wide for cross-wave inspection of inconsistencies
pds_wide_p <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  dplyr::select(participant_id, session_id, ph_p_pds__f_002__01) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = session_id,
    values_from = ph_p_pds__f_002__01,
    names_prefix = "session_"
  )

# Combine inconsistency summary with wide-format session data
pds_full_summary_p <- pds_summary_p %>%
  filter(unique_ph_p_pds > 1) %>%  # keep only participants with inconsistencies
  left_join(pds_wide, by = "participant_id")

pds_full_summary_p

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 5: DERIVE FINAL MENARCHE AGE — MEDIAN ACROSS WAVES (PARENT REPORT)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Consistent with the youth-report derivation, the median of all valid
# parent-reported menarche ages across waves is used as the final estimate
# (menarche_age_p).

cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  mutate(
    menarche_age_p = median(ph_p_pds__f_002__01, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Inspect derived variable alongside raw values
menarche_age_p <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  dplyr::select(participant_id, session_id, ph_p_pds__f_002__01, menarche_age_p) %>%
  arrange(participant_id, session_id) %>%
  as_tibble()  # ensures it's a neat tbl_df
menarche_age_p

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 6: DERIVE TIME FROM MENARCHE AT EACH WAVE (PARENT REPORT)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Time from parent-reported menarche is computed as visit age minus
# menarche_age_p. Negative values = pre-menarche; positive = post-menarche.

cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  mutate(
    Time_to_from_Menarche_p = ab_g_dyn__visit_age - menarche_age_p
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Inspect derived variable
Time_from_Menarche_p <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  dplyr::select(participant_id, session_id, ph_p_pds__f_002__01, menarche_age_p, Time_to_from_Menarche_p) %>%
```

### Alternative puberty markers with parent report
```{r make growth variables, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# STAGE 3: PARENT-REPORTED ALTERNATIVE PUBERTY MARKER ONSET AGES
# =============================================================================
# Onset ages for four alternative pubertal markers are derived from parent-
# reported PDS items, following the same logic as the youth-report pipeline
# (see chunk: alternative_puberty_markers). The earliest session at which
# the parent reported a marker as "definitely underway" (2) or "seems
# complete" (3) is used as the onset session, and the visit age at that
# session is taken as the onset age.
# =============================================================================

# Growth spurt: first session where parent reported height growth as started/underway
growth_spurt_p <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  filter(ph_p_pds_001 == 2 | ph_p_pds_001 == 3) %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  summarise(session_id = min(session_id)) %>%
  left_join(dynamicVariables %>% dplyr::select(participant_id, session_id, ab_g_dyn__visit_age),
            by = c("participant_id", "session_id")) %>%
  rename(growth_spurt_started_p = ab_g_dyn__visit_age)

# Breast budding: first session where parent reported breast development as started/underway
breast_budding_p <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  filter(ph_p_pds__f_001 == 2 | ph_p_pds__f_001 == 3) %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  summarise(session_id = min(session_id)) %>%
  left_join(dynamicVariables %>% dplyr::select(participant_id, session_id, ab_g_dyn__visit_age),
            by = c("participant_id", "session_id")) %>%
  rename(breast_budding_started_p = ab_g_dyn__visit_age)

# Body hair: first session where parent reported body hair growth as started/underway
body_hair_p <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  filter(ph_p_pds_002 == 2 | ph_p_pds_002 == 3) %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  summarise(session_id = min(session_id)) %>%
  left_join(dynamicVariables %>% dplyr::select(participant_id, session_id, ab_g_dyn__visit_age),
            by = c("participant_id", "session_id")) %>%
  rename(body_hair_started_p = ab_g_dyn__visit_age)

# Skin changes: first session where parent reported skin/acne changes as started/underway
skin_changes_p <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  filter(ph_p_pds_003 == 2 | ph_p_pds_003 == 3) %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  summarise(session_id = min(session_id)) %>%
  left_join(dynamicVariables %>% dplyr::select(participant_id, session_id, ab_g_dyn__visit_age),
            by = c("participant_id", "session_id")) %>%
  rename(skin_changes_started_p = ab_g_dyn__visit_age)

# Combine all parent-reported marker onset ages into a single wide-format dataframe
menarche_unique_p <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  select(participant_id, menarche_age_p) %>%
  distinct()

# Descriptive statistics for parent-reported marker onset ages
growth_charts_p <- growth_spurt_p %>%
  dplyr::select(participant_id, growth_spurt_started_p) %>%
  full_join(breast_budding_p %>% dplyr::select(participant_id, breast_budding_started_p),
            by = c("participant_id")) %>%
  full_join(body_hair_p %>% dplyr::select(participant_id, body_hair_started_p),
            by = c("participant_id")) %>%
  full_join(skin_changes_p %>% dplyr::select(participant_id, skin_changes_started_p),
            by = c("participant_id")) %>%
  full_join(menarche_unique_p %>% dplyr::select(participant_id, menarche_age_p),
            by = c("participant_id"))

# Compile mean and SD into a summary table (parallel to growth_charts_mean_sd)
growth_charts_mean_sd_p <- data.frame(
    growth_variable = c("growth spurt onset", "breast budding onset", "body hair onset", "skin changes onset", "menarche onset"),
    mean = c(mean(growth_charts_p$growth_spurt_started_p, na.rm = TRUE),
             mean(growth_charts_p$breast_budding_started_p, na.rm = TRUE),
             mean(growth_charts_p$body_hair_started_p, na.rm = TRUE),
             mean(growth_charts_p$skin_changes_started_p, na.rm = TRUE),
             mean(growth_charts_p$menarche_age_p, na.rm = TRUE)),
    sd = c(sd(growth_charts_p$growth_spurt_started_p, na.rm = TRUE),
           sd(growth_charts_p$breast_budding_started_p, na.rm = TRUE),
           sd(growth_charts_p$body_hair_started_p, na.rm = TRUE),
           sd(growth_charts_p$skin_changes_started_p, na.rm = TRUE),
           sd(growth_charts_p$menarche_age_p, na.rm = TRUE))
    )

# Merge parent-reported onset ages into main dataframe
cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  left_join(growth_charts_p %>% dplyr::select(participant_id,
                                            growth_spurt_started_p,
                                            breast_budding_started_p,
                                            body_hair_started_p,
                                            skin_changes_started_p),
            by = c("participant_id"))

# Derive time-from-onset variables for each parent-reported puberty marker
# (visit age − marker onset age; negative = pre-onset, positive = post-onset)
cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  mutate(
    # Compute time-from-onset variables using parent-report
    Time_to_from_growth_spurt_onset_p = ab_g_dyn__visit_age - growth_spurt_started_p,
    Time_to_from_breast_budding_onset_p = ab_g_dyn__visit_age - breast_budding_started_p,
    Time_to_from_body_hair_onset_p = ab_g_dyn__visit_age - body_hair_started_p,
    Time_to_from_skin_changes_onset_p = ab_g_dyn__visit_age - skin_changes_started_p)
```

#### CBCL Internalizing symptoms - parent
```{r Sensitivity analyses - other growth variables - inter, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# STAGE 4A: GAMM — PARENT-REPORTED PUBERTY MARKERS --> CBCL INTERNALIZING SYMPTOMS
# =============================================================================
# Five parent-reported time-from-onset variables (menarche + four alternative 
# markers) are pivoted to long format and separate GAMMs are fitted for each, 
# predicting CBCL internalizing symptoms. This is structurally identical to 
# Sensitivity 3A but uses parent-reported rather than youth-reported puberty markers.
# menarche_age_p (parent-reported) is used as the menarche timing covariate.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: RESHAPE TO LONG FORMAT 
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_puberty_marker_p <- cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c("Time_to_from_Menarche_p",
                        "Time_to_from_growth_spurt_onset_p",
                        "Time_to_from_breast_budding_onset_p",
                        "Time_to_from_body_hair_onset_p",
                        "Time_to_from_skin_changes_onset_p"),
               names_to = "Puberty_marker",
               values_to = "Time_from_puberty_marker") %>%
  mutate(Puberty_marker = factor(Puberty_marker,
                             levels = c("Time_to_from_Menarche_p",
                                        "Time_to_from_growth_spurt_onset_p",
                                        "Time_to_from_breast_budding_onset_p",
                                        "Time_to_from_body_hair_onset_p",
                                        "Time_to_from_skin_changes_onset_p"),
                             labels = c("Time from Menarche Onset (Years)",
                                        "Time from Growth Spurt Onset (Years)",
                                        "Time from Breast Budding Onset (Years)",
                                        "Time from Body Hair Onset (Years)",
                                        "Time from Skin Change Onset (Years)")))

# Ensure grouping variables are factors for gamm()
cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_puberty_marker_p$ab_g_dyn__design_site <- factor(cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_puberty_marker_p$ab_g_dyn__design_site)
str(cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_puberty_marker_p$ab_g_dyn__design_site)

cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_puberty_marker_p$participant_id <- factor(cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_puberty_marker_p$participant_id)
str(cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_puberty_marker_p$participant_id)

# Split by puberty marker (5 subsets)
data_list_puberty_marker_p <- split(cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_puberty_marker_p,
                                  cleaned_filtered_female_only_brain_puberty_marker_p$Puberty_marker)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: FIT MODELS IN PARALLEL
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# same covariates are used as in main model

fit_model_puberty_marker <- function(data) {
  gamm(mh_p_cbcl__synd__int_sum ~ s(Time_from_puberty_marker) +
         s(menarche_age_p) +
         s(General_SES_baseline),
       method = "REML",
       family = nb(),
       random = list(participant_id = ~1, ab_g_dyn__design_site = ~1),
       data = data)
}

# Parallel execution
n_cores <- min(5, detectCores() - 1)  # 5 markers
cl <- makeCluster(n_cores)
clusterEvalQ(cl, library(mgcv))

internalizing_models_puberty_marker_p <- parLapply(cl, data_list_puberty_marker_p, fit_model_puberty_marker)
stopCluster(cl)

# Convert to tibble format
internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output_p <- tibble(
  MARKER = names(internalizing_models_puberty_marker_p),
  model = internalizing_models_puberty_marker_p
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: TIDY OUTPUT, APPLY CORRECTIONS, SAVE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

tidy_internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output_p <- internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output_p %>%
  mutate(tidy = map(model, function(x) {
    tidydf = broom::tidy(x$gam)
    tidydf$N = length(x$gam$residuals)
    summary_model <- summary(x$gam)
    tidydf$R2 = summary_model$r.sq
    tidydf
  })) %>%
  unnest(tidy) %>%
  select(-model) %>%
  mutate(
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p.value, method = "fdr"),
    p_bonferroni = p.adjust(p.value, method = "bonferroni")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(p.value, p_fdr, p_bonferroni),
      ~ ifelse(.x == 0, "<.001", formatC(.x, format = "f", digits = 3))
    )
  )

write.csv(
  tidy_internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output_p,
  file = "Results/tidy_internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output_p.csv",
  row.names = FALSE)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: EXTRACT DERIVATIVE STATISTICS AND JOIN TO MODEL OUTPUT
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

second_derv_internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output_p <- internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output_p%>%
  mutate(derv_stats = map(model,~derivative_stats(
    ., smooth_var = "Time_from_puberty_marker", make_plots = TRUE
  ))) %>%
  unnest(derv_stats) %>%
  select(-model)

internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output_p <- internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output_p %>%
  left_join(second_derv_internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output_p, by = c("MARKER"))

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 5: VISUALIZE AND SAVE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

plots_tibble_puberty_markers_p <- internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output_p %>%
  mutate(
    plot = pmap(
      list(model, MARKER, sd_max_value, sd_max_lower_ci, sd_max_upper_ci),
      function(mod, marker, sd_val, sd_lower, sd_upper) {
        visualize_model(
          mod, 
          smooth_var = "Time_from_puberty_marker",
          group_var = "participant_id",
          derivative_plot = TRUE,
          xlabel = "Time from Puberty Marker (Years)",
          ylabel = "CBCL Internalizing Symptoms",
          plabels = paste(marker),
          show.data = FALSE,
          side_density = TRUE,
          v_line = 0,
          second_deriv_x     = sd_val,
          second_deriv_lower = sd_lower,
          second_deriv_upper = sd_upper
        )
      }
    )
  )

plots_onset <- plots_tibble_puberty_markers_p %>%
  pull(plot)
```

#### BPM Internalizing symptoms - parent
```{r Sensitivity analyses - other growth variables - inter, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# STAGE 4A: GAMM — PARENT-REPORTED PUBERTY MARKERS --> CBCL INTERNALIZING SYMPTOMS
# =============================================================================
# Five parent-reported time-from-onset variables (menarche + four alternative 
# markers) are pivoted to long format and separate GAMMs are fitted for each, 
# predicting BPM internalizing symptoms. This is structurally identical to 
# Sensitivity 3A but uses parent-reported rather than youth-reported puberty markers.
# menarche_age_p (parent-reported) is used as the menarche timing covariate.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: RESHAPE TO LONG FORMAT 
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

bpm_dataframe_long <- bpm_dataframe %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c("Time_to_from_Menarche_p",
                        "Time_to_from_growth_spurt_onset_p",
                        "Time_to_from_breast_budding_onset_p",
                        "Time_to_from_body_hair_onset_p",
                        "Time_to_from_skin_changes_onset_p"),
               names_to = "Puberty_marker",
               values_to = "Time_from_puberty_marker") %>%
  mutate(Puberty_marker = factor(Puberty_marker,
                             levels = c("Time_to_from_Menarche_p",
                                        "Time_to_from_growth_spurt_onset_p",
                                        "Time_to_from_breast_budding_onset_p",
                                        "Time_to_from_body_hair_onset_p",
                                        "Time_to_from_skin_changes_onset_p"),
                             labels = c("Time from Menarche Onset (Years)",
                                        "Time from Growth Spurt Onset (Years)",
                                        "Time from Breast Budding Onset (Years)",
                                        "Time from Body Hair Onset (Years)",
                                        "Time from Skin Change Onset (Years)")))

# Ensure grouping variables are factors for gamm()
bpm_dataframe_long$ab_g_dyn__design_site <- factor(bpm_dataframe_long$ab_g_dyn__design_site)
str(bpm_dataframe_long$ab_g_dyn__design_site)

bpm_dataframe_long$participant_id <- factor(bpm_dataframe_long$participant_id)
str(bpm_dataframe_long$participant_id)

# Split by puberty marker (5 subsets)
data_list_puberty_marker_p <- split(bpm_dataframe_long,
                                  bpm_dataframe_long$Puberty_marker)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: FIT MODELS IN PARALLEL
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# same covariates are used as in main model

fit_model_puberty_marker <- function(data) {
  gamm(mh_y_bpm__int_sum ~ s(Time_from_puberty_marker) +
         s(menarche_age_p) +
         s(General_SES_baseline),
       method = "REML",
       family = nb(),
       random = list(participant_id = ~1, ab_g_dyn__design_site = ~1),
       data = data)
}

# Parallel execution
n_cores <- min(5, detectCores() - 1)  # 5 markers
cl <- makeCluster(n_cores)
clusterEvalQ(cl, library(mgcv))

bpm_models_puberty_marker_p <- parLapply(cl, data_list_puberty_marker_p, fit_model_puberty_marker)
stopCluster(cl)

# Convert to tibble format
bpm_models_puberty_marker_output_p <- tibble(
  MARKER = names(bpm_models_puberty_marker_p),
  model = bpm_models_puberty_marker_p
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: TIDY OUTPUT, APPLY CORRECTIONS, SAVE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

tidy_bpm_models_puberty_marker_output_p <- bpm_models_puberty_marker_output_p %>%
  mutate(tidy = map(model, function(x) {
    tidydf = broom::tidy(x$gam)
    tidydf$N = length(x$gam$residuals)
    summary_model <- summary(x$gam)
    tidydf$R2 = summary_model$r.sq
    tidydf
  })) %>%
  unnest(tidy) %>%
  select(-model) %>%
  mutate(
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p.value, method = "fdr"),
    p_bonferroni = p.adjust(p.value, method = "bonferroni")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(p.value, p_fdr, p_bonferroni),
      ~ ifelse(.x == 0, "<.001", formatC(.x, format = "f", digits = 3))
    )
  )

write.csv(
  tidy_bpm_models_puberty_marker_output_p,
  file = "Results/tidy_bpm_models_puberty_marker_output_p.csv",
  row.names = FALSE)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: EXTRACT DERIVATIVE STATISTICS AND JOIN TO MODEL OUTPUT
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

second_derv_bpm_models_puberty_marker_output_p <- bpm_models_puberty_marker_output_p%>%
  mutate(derv_stats = map(model,~derivative_stats(
    ., smooth_var = "Time_from_puberty_marker", make_plots = TRUE
  ))) %>%
  unnest(derv_stats) %>%
  select(-model)

bpm_models_puberty_marker_output_p <- bpm_models_puberty_marker_output_p %>%
  left_join(second_derv_bpm_models_puberty_marker_output_p, by = c("MARKER"))

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 5: VISUALIZE AND SAVE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

plots_tibble_puberty_markers_p <- bpm_models_puberty_marker_output_p %>%
  mutate(
    plot = pmap(
      list(model, MARKER, sd_max_value, sd_max_lower_ci, sd_max_upper_ci),
      function(mod, marker, sd_val, sd_lower, sd_upper) {
        visualize_model(
          mod, 
          smooth_var = "Time_from_puberty_marker",
          group_var = "participant_id",
          derivative_plot = TRUE,
          xlabel = "Time from Puberty Marker (Years)",
          ylabel = "BPM Internalizing Symptoms",
          plabels = paste(marker),
          show.data = FALSE,
          side_density = TRUE,
          v_line = 0,
          second_deriv_x     = sd_val,
          second_deriv_lower = sd_lower,
          second_deriv_upper = sd_upper
        )
      }
    )
  )

plots_onset <- plots_tibble_puberty_markers_p %>%
  pull(plot)

Puberty_markers_inter_plots_p <- wrap_plots(plots_onset, ncol = 1)
Puberty_markers_inter_plots_p

#save figures
save_plot('Figures/Puberty_markers_inter_bpm_with_point_plots_p.pdf',
          plot = Puberty_markers_inter_plots_p,
          base_height = 20, 
          base_width = 7)

# Format and save second derivative inflection point table
second_derv_bpm_models_puberty_marker_output_clean_p <- second_derv_bpm_models_puberty_marker_output_p %>%
  dplyr::select(MARKER, sd_min_value, sd_min_lower_ci, sd_min_upper_ci, sd_max_value, sd_max_lower_ci, sd_max_upper_ci) %>%
  mutate(
    second_derv_min_CI = paste0(
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_min_value), " [",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_min_lower_ci), ";",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_min_upper_ci), "]"
    ),
    second_derv_max_CI = paste0(
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_max_value), " [",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_max_lower_ci), ";",
      sprintf("%.3f", sd_max_upper_ci), "]"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(MARKER, second_derv_min_CI, second_derv_max_CI)

write.csv(
  second_derv_bpm_models_puberty_marker_output_clean_p,
```

##### Parent report - Extended Data Figure
```{r Sensitivity analyses - other growth variables - figures, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# STAGE 5: EXTENDED DATA FIGURE — SECOND DERIVATIVE INFLECTION POINTS
#          ACROSS ALL PUBERTY MARKERS AND OUTCOMES (PARENT REPORT)
# =============================================================================
# A summary figure is assembled showing the second derivative minimum and
# maximum inflection points (with 95% CIs) for each puberty marker (including 
# menarche) across all outcomes (internalizing symptoms + 8 brain metrics) based
# on parent report. This provides a compact cross-marker and rater comparison 
# of when associations accelerate and decelerate relative to each pubertal event.
# =============================================================================

# Compile second derivative statistics from all marker-outcome combinations
# into a single long-format table for plotting

# Tag each source dataframe with Metric and MARKER labels before combining
puberty_figure_table_p <- second_derv_internalizing_models_puberty_marker_output_p %>%
  mutate(Metric = "CBCL Internalizing Symptoms")

second_derv_bpm_models_puberty_marker_output_p <- second_derv_bpm_models_puberty_marker_output_p %>%
  mutate(Metric = "BPM Internalizing Symptoms")

second_derv_brain_model_output_puberty_marker_p <- second_derv_brain_model_output_puberty_marker_p %>%
  mutate(Metric = MRI_metric,
         MARKER = Puberty_marker) %>%
  dplyr::select(-MRI_metric, -Puberty_marker)

# Combine all derivative statistics using full_join to retain all rows
puberty_figure_table_p <- puberty_figure_table_p %>%
  full_join(second_derv_bpm_models_puberty_marker_output_p) %>%
  full_join(second_derv_brain_model_output_puberty_marker_p)

# Set factor levels for consistent display order across both panels
desired_order <- c(
  "CBCL Internalizing Symptoms",
  "BPM Internalizing Symptoms",
  "Whole brain volume",
  "Subcortical volume",
  "Gray matter volume",
  "Cortical thickness",
  "Surface area",
  "White matter volume",
  "Lateral ventricles volume",
  "CSF")

puberty_figure_table_p <- puberty_figure_table_p %>%
  mutate(Metric = factor(Metric, levels = desired_order))

# Recode MARKER labels for concise display on the y-axis
puberty_figure_table_p <- puberty_figure_table_p %>%
  mutate(MARKER = factor(MARKER,
                         levels = c("Time from Growth Spurt Onset (Years)",
                                    "Time from Breast Budding Onset (Years)",
                                    "Time from Body Hair Onset (Years)",
                                    "Time from Skin Change Onset (Years)",
                                    "Time from Menarche Onset (Years)"),
                         labels = c("Growth Spurt Onset",
                                    "Breast Budding Onset",
                                    "Body Hair Onset",
                                    "Skin Change Onset",
                                    "Menarche Onset")))

# Left panel: second derivative minimum inflection points
second_derv_inter_min_p <- ggplot(puberty_figure_table_p, aes(y = MARKER)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray90") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(
      xmin = sd_min_lower_ci,
      xmax = sd_min_upper_ci),
    height = 0.2,
    color = "gray40",
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_point(aes(x = sd_min_value),
             shape = 21,
             size = 4,
             colour = "black",
             fill = "gray80") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-5, 10)) +
  labs(
    title = "Second derivative min + CI",
    x = "Time from Marker Onset in Years",
    y = "") +
  facet_wrap(~Metric, ncol = 1)

# Right panel: second derivative maximum inflection points
second_derv_inter_max_p <- ggplot(puberty_figure_table_p, aes(y = MARKER)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray90") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(
      xmin = sd_max_lower_ci,
      xmax = sd_max_upper_ci),
    height = 0.2,
    color = "gray40",
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_point(aes(x = sd_max_value),
             shape = 21,
             size = 4,
             colour = "black",
             fill = "gray80") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-5, 10)) +
  labs(
    title = "Second derivative max + CI",
    x = "Time from Marker Onset in Years",
    y = "") +
  facet_wrap(~Metric, ncol = 1)

# Combine panels side by side and save
combined_plot <- second_derv_inter_min_p | second_derv_inter_max_p
combined_plot

# save figure
save_plot('Figures/Puberty_markers_extended_figure_p.pdf',
          plot = combined_plot,
          base_height = 20, 
          base_width = 13)
```

## Comparing CI width
### CBCL
```{r Int symptoms and onset, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# COMPARE CI WIDTHS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### CBCL INTERNALIZING & EXTERNALIZING #####

boot_combined_cbcl_inter <- read.csv("/projects/standard/bart/shared/projects/ABCD_menarche/Bootstrapping_results/cbcl/internalizing/boot_combined_cbcl_inter.csv")

boot_combined_cbcl_exter <- read.csv("/projects/standard/bart/shared/projects/ABCD_menarche/Bootstrapping_results/cbcl/externalizing/boot_combined_cbcl_exter.csv")

boot_summary_cbcl_inter <- boot_combined_cbcl_inter %>%
  filter(is.na(error)) %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  summarise(
    n_successful = n(),
    mean_width   = mean(ci_width),
    median_width = median(ci_width),
    sd_width     = sd(ci_width),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
print(boot_summary_cbcl_inter)

boot_summary_cbcl_exter <- boot_combined_cbcl_exter %>%
  filter(is.na(error)) %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  summarise(
    n_successful = n(),
    mean_width   = mean(ci_width),
    median_width = median(ci_width),
    sd_width     = sd(ci_width),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
print(boot_summary_cbcl_exter)

paired_wide_cbcl_inter <- boot_combined_cbcl_inter %>%
  filter(is.na(error)) %>%
  select(iter, model, ci_width) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = ci_width) %>%
  filter(if_all(-iter, ~ !is.na(.))) %>%
  slice_head(n=1100)

paired_wide_cbcl_exter <- boot_combined_cbcl_exter %>%
  filter(is.na(error)) %>%
  select(iter, model, ci_width) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = ci_width) %>%
```

#### Write table
```{r CIs CSF, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

# =============================================================================
# SAFE RESULTS FROM MENTAL HEALTH ANALYSIS IN TABLES
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: SAFE RESULTS FROM GAMMS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Combine results from all mental health models (internalizing + externalizing symptoms)
tidy_CI_mental <- bind_rows(
  tidy_binom_cbcl_inter,
  tidy_binom_cbcl_exter,
  tidy_binom_bpm_inter,
  tidy_binom_bpm_exter,
  tidy_binom_cbcl_inter_vs_exter,
  tidy_binom_bpm_inter_vs_exter) 

## Correct for multiple comparisons using different methods (e.g. FDR, Bonferroni)
## and clean the output
tidy_CI_mental <- tidy_CI_mental %>%
  mutate(
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p.value, method = "fdr"),
    p_bonferroni = p.adjust(p.value, method = "bonferroni")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(p.value, p_fdr, p_bonferroni),
      ~ ifelse(.x == 0, "<.001", formatC(.x, format = "f", digits = 3))
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(model, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, p.value, p_fdr, p_bonferroni) %>%
  mutate(
    value_CI = paste0(
      sprintf("%.3f", estimate), " [",
      sprintf("%.3f", conf.low), ";",
      sprintf("%.3f", conf.high), "]"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(model, value_CI, p.value, p_fdr, p_bonferroni)


## Write out results
write.csv(
  tidy_CI_mental,
  file = "Results/tidy_CI_sig_mental.csv",
  row.names = FALSE)

```

```{r CIs CSF, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
## and clean the output
tidy_CI_mri <- tidy_CI_mri %>%
  mutate(
    p_fdr = p.adjust(p.value, method = "fdr"),
    p_bonferroni = p.adjust(p.value, method = "bonferroni")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(p.value, p_fdr, p_bonferroni),
      ~ ifelse(.x == 0, "<.001", formatC(.x, format = "f", digits = 3))
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(model, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, p.value, p_fdr, p_bonferroni) %>%
  mutate(
    value_CI = paste0(
      sprintf("%.3f", estimate), " [",
      sprintf("%.3f", conf.low), ";",
      sprintf("%.3f", conf.high), "]"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(model, value_CI, p.value, p_fdr, p_bonferroni)


## Write out results
write.csv(
  tidy_CI_mri,
  file = "Results/tidy_CI_sig_mri.csv",
  row.names = FALSE)

```

# Main Figures for publication - Smooths brain plots
```{r Figures smooths, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# PUBLICATION FIGURES: MIN-MAX SCALED BRAIN SMOOTH TRAJECTORIES
# =============================================================================
# This chunk produces two publication-quality overlay panels showing the
# fitted smooth trajectories for all eight brain metrics on a common scale:
#
#   Panel 1: Smooths as a function of chronological age
#            (smooths_brain_models_age_plot.pdf)
#   Panel 2: Smooths as a function of time from menarche (gynecological age)
#            (smooths_brain_models_onset_plot.pdf)
#
# Because the eight brain metrics have different units and absolute scales
# (mm³, mm, mm²), raw smooth estimates cannot be meaningfully overlaid on a
# shared y-axis. Min-max scaling is applied within each metric to express
# all trajectories on a common 0–1 scale, where 0 = the metric's minimum
# fitted value and 1 = its maximum fitted value across the plotted range.
# This preserves the shape of each trajectory while enabling direct visual
# comparison of developmental timing across metrics.
#
# Inflection points (second derivative minima from derivative_stats()) are
# annotated on each trajectory as a point estimate with a horizontal 95% CI
# bar.
#
# Metrics are grouped into four biologically meaningful facets:
#   - Gross metrics          : Whole brain volume, Subcortical volume
#   - Gray matter metrics    : Gray matter volume, Cortical thickness, Surface area
#   - White matter metrics   : White matter volume
#   - Water content metrics  : Lateral ventricles volume, CSF
#
# an additional package is needed:
  library(ggpattern)
# =============================================================================

# Define consistent colour palette for all eight brain metrics
# (used across both figures and any other smooth overlay plots)
metric_colors <- c(
  "Whole brain volume"        = "#bebada",
  "Subcortical volume"        = "#9970ab",
  "Gray matter volume"        = "#fcc5c0",
  "Cortical thickness"        = "#fa9fb5",
  "Surface area"              = "#f768a1",
  "White matter volume"       = "#fed9a6",
  "Lateral ventricles volume" = "#8dd3c7",
  "CSF"                       = "#ccebc5"
)

# =============================================================================
# PANEL 1: BRAIN SMOOTHS AS A FUNCTION OF CHRONOLOGICAL AGE
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: MIN-MAX SCALE SMOOTH ESTIMATES WITHIN EACH METRIC
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
model_smooths_brain_models_age <- model_smooths_brain_models_age %>%
  group_by(MRI_metric) %>%
  mutate(estimate_scaled_min_max = (.estimate - min(.estimate))/ (max(.estimate) - min(.estimate))) %>%
  mutate(upper_scaled_min_max = (upper - min(.estimate))/ (max(.estimate) - min(.estimate))) %>%
  mutate(lower_scaled_min_max = (lower - min(.estimate))/ (max(.estimate) - min(.estimate))) %>%
  ungroup()

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: ASSIGN METRICS TO BIOLOGICAL GROUPING VARIABLE FOR FACETING
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

model_smooths_brain_models_age <- model_smooths_brain_models_age %>%
  mutate(
    MRI_metric_group = case_when(
      MRI_metric %in% c("Whole brain volume", "Subcortical volume") ~ "Gross metrics",
      MRI_metric %in% c("Gray matter volume", "Cortical thickness", "Surface area") ~ "Gray matter metrics",
      MRI_metric %in% c("White matter volume") ~ "White matter metrics",
      MRI_metric %in% c("Lateral ventricles volume", "CSF") ~ "Water content metrics",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    MRI_metric_group = factor(
      MRI_metric_group,
      levels = c("Gross metrics", "Gray matter metrics", "White matter metrics", "Water content metrics")
    )
  )

# Apply the same grouping variable to the derivative statistics dataframe
# so that inflection point annotations are faceted consistently with smooths
derv_brain_models_age_output <- derv_brain_models_age_output %>%
  mutate(
    MRI_metric_group = case_when(
      MRI_metric %in% c("Whole brain volume", "Subcortical volume") ~ "Gross metrics",
      MRI_metric %in% c("Gray matter volume", "Cortical thickness", "Surface area") ~ "Gray matter metrics",
      MRI_metric %in% c("White matter volume") ~ "White matter metrics",
      MRI_metric %in% c("Lateral ventricles volume", "CSF") ~ "Water content metrics",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    MRI_metric_group = factor(
      MRI_metric_group,
      levels = c("Gross metrics", "Gray matter metrics", "White matter metrics", "Water content metrics")
    )
  )

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: COMPUTE Y-POSITION FOR INFLECTION POINT ANNOTATIONS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
ylab_df <- model_smooths_brain_models_age %>%
  group_by(MRI_metric) %>%
  slice_min(
    abs(ab_g_dyn__visit_age - unique(
      derv_brain_models_age_output$sd_min_value[
        derv_brain_models_age_output$MRI_metric == first(MRI_metric)
      ]
    )),
    n = 1,
    with_ties = FALSE
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(MRI_metric, ylab_point = estimate_scaled_min_max)

# Append y-position to derivative statistics for use in geom_linerange/geom_point
derv_brain_models_age_output <- derv_brain_models_age_output %>%
  left_join(ylab_df, by = "MRI_metric")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: PLOT
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

smooths_brain_models_age_plot <- ggplot(model_smooths_brain_models_age, aes(x=ab_g_dyn__visit_age, y=estimate_scaled_min_max, color = MRI_metric, fill = MRI_metric)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 11.8, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray90") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower_scaled_min_max,
              ymax = upper_scaled_min_max),
              alpha = 0.3,
              color = NA) +
  geom_line(size = 2.75) +
  geom_linerange(
    data = derv_brain_models_age_output,
    aes(
      y = ylab_point,
      xmin = sd_min_lower_ci,
      xmax = sd_min_upper_ci
    ),
    height = 0.05,       # vertical thickness of the bar
    colour = "gray40",
    alpha = 1,
    linewidth = 0.5,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = derv_brain_models_age_output,
    aes(x = sd_min_value,
        y = ylab_point),
    shape = 21,
    size = 3,
    colour = "black",
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = metric_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = metric_colors) +
  facet_wrap(~ MRI_metric_group, ncol=1) +
  ylab("Relative magnitude (min-max scaled)") +
  xlab("Age (Years)") +
  theme_classic(base_family = "Helvetica", base_size = 14) +
    theme(
      text = element_text(family = "Helvetica", size = 14, color = "black"),
      axis.title = element_text(family = "Helvetica", size = 14, color = "black"),
      axis.text = element_text(family = "Helvetica", size = 14, color = "black"),
      plot.title = element_text(family = "Helvetica", size = 14, color = "black"),
      legend.text = element_text(family = "Helvetica", size = 14, color = "black"),
      legend.title = element_text(family = "Helvetica", size = 14, color = "black")
    )
smooths_brain_models_age_plot <- smooths_brain_models_age_plot +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0,1))

#save figure
save_plot('Figures/smooths_brain_models_age_plot.pdf',plot = smooths_brain_models_age_plot,base_height = 8, base_width = 6)
```

# Main Figures - Credible Interval Width for inflection points
```{r Figures - CI width, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# PUBLICATION FIGURES: INFLECTION POINT PRECISION
# =============================================================================
# This chunk produces bar charts comparing the width of the 95% confidence
# interval (CI) around the second derivative inflection point for each outcome,
# contrasting chronological age models against gynecological age (time from
# menarche) models.
#
# CI width is used as an index of inflection point precision: a narrower CI
# indicates that the model can localize the inflection point more precisely.
#
# CI widths are entered as hardcoded values computed from the second derivative
# output tables (upper CI bound − lower CI bound for sd_min or sd_max,
# depending on the outcome). These are entered manually here rather than
# computed from dataframes to allow precise control over figure content and
# to decouple figure production from upstream model objects.
#
# Three figures are produced:
#   1. Internalizing symptoms (precision_inter_plot.pdf)
#   2. Externalizing symptoms (precision_exter_plot.pdf)
#   3. Brain morphometry metrics (precision_brain_plot.pdf)
# =============================================================================

# =============================================================================
# FIGURE 1: INTERNALIZING SYMPTOMS — INFLECTION POINT CI WIDTH
# =============================================================================

df_inter <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Chronological Age", "Gynecological Age"),
  CIs = c(14.403-11.121, 0.947-(-0.203)))

precision_inter <- ggplot(df_inter, aes(x = CIs, y = Model)) +
  geom_col_pattern(
    aes(group = Model, pattern = Model),
    fill = "grey85",
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), 
    width = 0.4,
    pattern_color = "white",
    pattern_fill = "white",
    pattern_angle = 45,
    pattern_density = 0.1,
    pattern_spacing = 0.07,
    pattern_key_scale_factor = 0.6
  ) +
  scale_pattern_manual(values = c("Gynecological Age" = "none", 
                                  "Chronological Age" = "stripe")) +
  labs(
    x = "CI Width of Inflection Points \n (Years)",
    y = "",
    pattern = "Model",
    title = "Inflection point precision"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_family = "Helvetica", base_size = 16) +
  xlim(0, max(df_inter$CIs) * 1.15) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    text = element_text(family = "Helvetica", size = 16, color = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(family = "Helvetica", size = 16, color = "black"),
    axis.text = element_text(family = "Helvetica", size = 16, color = "black")
  )
precision_inter

#save figure
save_plot('Figures/precision_inter_plot.pdf',
          plot = precision_inter,
          base_height = 5, 
          base_width = 8)


########## FOR BPM AND CBCL #############

# =============================================================================
# FIGURE 3: BRAIN MORPHOMETRY METRICS — INFLECTION POINT CI WIDTH
# =============================================================================

metric_colors <- c(
  "Whole brain volume"        = "#bebada",
  "Subcortical volume"        = "#9970ab",
  "Gray matter volume"        = "#fcc5c0",
  "Cortical thickness"        = "#fa9fb5",
  "Surface area"              = "#f768a1",
  "White matter volume"       = "#fed9a6",
  "Lateral ventricles volume" = "#8dd3c7",
  "CSF"                       = "#ccebc5"
)

df_brain <- data.frame(
  MRI_Metric = c(rep("Whole brain volume",2),
                 rep("Subcortical volume", 2),
                 rep("Gray matter volume", 2),
                 rep("Cortical thickness", 2),
                 rep("Surface area", 2),
                 rep("White matter volume", 2),
                 rep("Lateral ventricles volume", 2),
                 rep("CSF", 2)),
  Model = c("Chronological Age", "Gynecological Age"),
  CIs = c(12.848-11.352, 0.362-0.202,
          13.139-11.753, 0.442-0.282,
          12.556-10.914, 0.322-0.082,
          16.423-10.695, 0.442-(-0.678),
          12.702-10.841, 0.362-0.082,
          12.738-11.644, 0.522-0.202,
          15.401-12.227, 2.162-1.002,
          15.438-9.783, 3.042-0.842))

desired_order <- c(
  "Whole brain volume",
  "Subcortical volume",
  "Gray matter volume",
  "Cortical thickness",
  "Surface area",
  "White matter volume",
  "Lateral ventricles volume",
  "CSF")

df_brain <- df_brain %>%
  mutate(MRI_Metric = factor(MRI_Metric, levels = desired_order)) %>%
  arrange(MRI_Metric)

df_brain$MRI_Metric <- factor(df_brain$MRI_Metric, levels = rev(unique(df_brain$MRI_Metric)))

precision_brain <- ggplot(df_brain, aes(x = CIs, y = MRI_Metric, fill = MRI_Metric)) +
  geom_col_pattern(
    aes(group = Model, pattern = Model),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), 
    width = 0.4,
    pattern_color = "white",
    pattern_fill = "white",
    pattern_angle = 45,
    pattern_density = 0.1,
    pattern_spacing = 0.07,
    pattern_key_scale_factor = 0.6
  ) +
  scale_pattern_manual(values = c("Gynecological Age" = "none", 
                                  "Chronological Age" = "stripe")) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(CIs, 2), group = Model), 
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
            hjust = -0.2, size = 4) +
  labs(
    x = "CI Width of Inflection Points \n (Years)",
    y = "",
    pattern = "Model",
    title = "Inflection point precision"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_family = "Helvetica", base_size = 12) +
  xlim(0, max(df_brain$CIs) * 1.15) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = metric_colors) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    text = element_text(family = "Helvetica", size = 12, color = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(family = "Helvetica", size = 12, color = "black"),
    axis.text = element_text(family = "Helvetica", size = 12, color = "black")
  )
precision_brain

#save figure
save_plot('precision_brain_plot.pdf',
          plot = precision_brain,
          base_height = 8,
```

# Sample size for specific analyses (BPM)
```{r baseline_exposome NA, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Define sample sizes for specific analyses (females only)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Rationale:
# Different analyses require different data availability (e.g., menarche timing,
# mental health outcomes, neuroimaging measures). We therefore define analysis-
# specific samples based on the presence of required variables.

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Menarche sample: participants with available menarche age
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
menarche_sample_size <- bpm_dataframe %>%
  filter(!is.na(menarche_age_y)) %>%
  distinct(participant_id)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mental health sample: participants with menarche age AND at least one
# internalizing AND externalizing assessment across any session (CBCL)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

mental_health_sample_size_bpm <- bpm_dataframe %>%
  filter(!is.na(menarche_age_y)) %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  filter(any(!is.na(mh_y_bpm__int_sum)),
         any(!is.na(mh_y_bpm__ext_sum))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  distinct(participant_id)

mental_health_sample_size_bpm_arm1 <- Arms %>%
  filter(!is.na(menarche_age_y)) %>%
  filter(Matched_groups_baseline == 1) %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  filter(any(!is.na(mh_y_bpm__int_sum)),
         any(!is.na(mh_y_bpm__ext_sum))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  distinct(participant_id)

mental_health_sample_size_bpm_arm2 <- Arms %>%
  filter(!is.na(menarche_age_y)) %>%
  filter(Matched_groups_baseline == 2) %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  filter(any(!is.na(mh_y_bpm__int_sum)),
         any(!is.na(mh_y_bpm__ext_sum))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  distinct(participant_id)

mental_health_sample_size_bpm_sibling <- df_no_siblings_bpm %>%
  filter(!is.na(menarche_age_y)) %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  filter(any(!is.na(mh_y_bpm__int_sum)),
         any(!is.na(mh_y_bpm__ext_sum))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  distinct(participant_id)

mental_health_sample_size_bpm_bmi <- bpm_dataframe %>%
  filter(!is.na(menarche_age_y)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(bmi)) %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  filter(any(!is.na(mh_y_bpm__int_sum)),
         any(!is.na(mh_y_bpm__ext_sum))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  distinct(participant_id)

brain_sample_size_brokenstick_bpm <- bpm_dataframe %>%
  filter(!is.na(menarche_age_y)) %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  filter(
    # At least one structural MRI metric available across sessions
         any(!is.na(mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__whb_sum)) |
         any(!is.na(mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__scgv_sum)) |  
         any(!is.na(mr_y_smri__vol__dsk_sum)) |   
         any(!is.na(total_cerebral_WM)) |   
         any(!is.na(mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__lvs_sum)) |   
         any(!is.na(mr_y_smri__vol__aseg__csf_sum)) |   
         any(!is.na(mr_y_smri__thk__dsk_mean)) |   
         any(!is.na(mr_y_smri__area__dsk_sum))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  distinct(participant_id)
```
